papers.title: Wavelet-based study and analysis of human papillomavirus (HPV) through a new mathematical model
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is recognized as the leading cause of cervical cancer, one of the most prevalent malignancies affecting women worldwide. This article presents a compartmental mathematical model that describes the transmission of HPV leading to cervical cancer. The model divides the total population into six compartments: susceptible, exposed, infected, cervical cancer, recovered, and vaccinated. The formulated nonlinear system of differential equations captures the epidemiological transitions among these classes, including infection, progression, recovery, and disease-induced mortality. To obtain an efficient and accurate approximate solution, the Lucas wavelet method (LuWM) is employed. The Lucas wavelet basis functions, possessing orthogonality and compact support, are used to transform the system into a set of algebraic equations. Convergence analyses confirm the reliability of the proposed scheme. The method’s efficiency is demonstrated through numerical simulations and graphical illustrations. The results of various techniques are compared with the proposed LuWM. The variation of different dependent variables with respect to different parameters is discussed using figures. The findings provide valuable insight into HPV dynamics and can assist in designing optimal control strategies for cervical cancer prevention.

papers.abstract_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 感染被认为是 宫颈癌 的主要原因,宫颈癌 是影响全球女性的最常见恶性肿瘤之一。本文提出了一个分区数学模型,描述了 HPV 的 传播 导致 宫颈癌。该模型将总人口分为六个部分:易感人群、暴露人群、感染人群、宫颈癌、康复人群和接种疫苗人群。制定的非线性微分方程系统捕获了这些类别之间的流行病学转变,包括感染、进展、恢复和疾病引起的 死亡率。为了获得高效且准确的近似解,采用卢卡斯小波方法(LuWM)。Lucas小波基函数具有正交性和紧支持性,可将系统转化为一组代数方程组。收敛分析证实了所提出方案的可靠性。通过数值模拟和图形说明证明了该方法的效率。各种技术的结果与所提出的 LuWM 进行了比较。使用图形讨论不同因变量相对于不同参数的变化。这些发现为 HPV 动态提供了宝贵的见解,并有助于设计 宫颈癌 预防的最佳控制策略。

papers.title: Impact of Human Papillomavirus Vaccination Coverage on Cytopathological Findings: A Cross-sectional Study in a Tertiary Care Teaching Hospital of Uttar Pradesh
papers.abstract: Background: Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) is the primary etiological factor in cervical cancer development.Although HPV vaccines provide strong protection, disparities exist between full-dose and incomplete/no vaccination in their impact on cytological outcomes.Objective: To evaluate and compare the prevalence of cervical cytological abnormalities among women who completed the full HPV vaccine schedule and those who received partial or no vaccination.Materials and methods: This hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted from January 2023 to January 2025 in a tertiary care hospital in Agra, Uttar Pradesh, India.A total of 4,200 women aged 25-45 years undergoing cervical cancer screening were included.Participants were categorized based on HPV vaccination status: Full-dose (three-doses) vs partial/no-dose.Pap smears were classified per the Bethesda 2014 system.Demographics, reproductive history, and behavioral risk factors were assessed.Multivariable logistic regression determined adjusted associations.Results: Abnormal Pap smear prevalence was significantly lower in the full-dose group (5.8%) compared to the partial/no-dose group (14.7%) (p < 0.001).Fully vaccinated women had reduced odds of high-grade lesions (HSIL+) [adjusted odds ratio (aOR): 0.23; 95% CI: 0.15-0.36].The protective effect remained consistent across subgroups stratified by age, parity, and sexual debut.Conclusion: Completion of the full HPV vaccine schedule is associated with markedly lower rates of cytological abnormalities.Enhancing vaccine adherence should be a priority for cervical cancer prevention.
papers.journal: Journal of South Asian Federation of Obstetrics and Gynaecology

papers.abstract_original: Background: Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) is the primary etiological factor in cervical cancer development.Although HPV vaccines provide strong protection, disparities exist between full-dose and incomplete/no vaccination in their impact on cytological outcomes.Objective: To evaluate and compare the prevalence of cervical cytological abnormalities among women who completed the full HPV vaccine schedule and those who received partial or no vaccination.Materials and methods: This hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted from January 2023 to January 2025 in a tertiary care hospital in Agra, Uttar Pradesh, India.A total of 4,200 women aged 25-45 years undergoing cervical cancer screening were included.Participants were categorized based on HPV vaccination status: Full-dose (three-doses) vs partial/no-dose.Pap smears were classified per the Bethesda 2014 system.Demographics, reproductive history, and behavioral risk factors were assessed.Multivariable logistic regression determined adjusted associations.Results: Abnormal Pap smear prevalence was significantly lower in the full-dose group (5.8%) compared to the partial/no-dose group (14.7%) (p < 0.001).Fully vaccinated women had reduced odds of high-grade lesions (HSIL+) [adjusted odds ratio (aOR): 0.23; 95% CI: 0.15-0.36].The protective effect remained consistent across subgroups stratified by age, parity, and sexual debut.Conclusion: Completion of the full HPV vaccine schedule is associated with markedly lower rates of cytological abnormalities.Enhancing vaccine adherence should be a priority for cervical cancer prevention.

elements_zh.methods: 高危人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV)的持续感染是宫颈癌发展的主要病因。尽管HPV 疫苗提供了强有力的保护,但全剂量和不完整/无疫苗接种对细胞学结果的影响存在差异。目的:评估和比较完成完整HPV的女性中患病率对宫颈细胞学异常的影响疫苗 时间表以及部分或未接受 疫苗接种 的患者。材料和方法:这项以医院为基础的横断面研究于 2023 年 1 月至 2025 年 1 月在印度北方邦阿格拉的一家三级护理医院进行。总共纳入了 4,200 名年龄在 25-45 岁之间接受 宫颈癌 筛查的女性。参与者根据以下条件进行分类: HPV 疫苗接种 状态:全剂量(三剂量)与部分/无剂量。根据 Bethesda 2014 系统对巴氏涂片进行分类。评估人口统计学、生殖史和行为风险因素。多变量逻辑回归确定调整后的关联。结果:与部分/无剂量组相比,全剂量组中异常子宫颈抹片检查 (5.8%) 显着降低(14.7%) (p < 0.001)。完全接种疫苗的女性出现高级别病变 (HSIL+) 的几率降低[调整后的比值比 (aOR):0.23;95% CI: 0.15-0.36]。按年龄、胎次和初次性行为分层的亚组中,保护作用保持一致。结论:完成完整的 HPV 疫苗 时间表与显着降低的细胞学异常率相关。增强 疫苗 的依从性应成为 宫颈癌 预防的优先事项。

papers.title: Presence of Human Papillomavirus and Epstein-Barr Virus in Breast Cancer Biopsies as Potential Risk Factors
papers.abstract: Introduction: Breast cancer represents the leading cause of cancer-related death in the Venezuelan female population.Many risk factors favoring its appearance have been reported; however, human papillomavirus and Epstein-Barr virus have been associated in the past few decades as potential risk factors in the development of this malignancy.Objective: To detect the presence of human papillomavirus and Epstein-Barr virus in breast cancer biopsies in order to establish a possible link between infection with these viral agents and the development of this pathology.Methods: Fresh biopsies were collected from patients with breast cancer and patients with breast benign pathology attending the Hospital Universitario de Caracas for surgery.Human papillomavirus detection was made using the INNO-LIPA ® HPV Genotyping Extra commercial kit (Innogenetics), and Epstein-Barr virus genome was detected with Epstein-Barr Virus BMLF1 commercial kit (Maxim Biotech, Inc.).Results: 63.6 and 13.6% of breast cancer cases were positive for human papillomavirus and Epstein-Barr virus DNA, respectively, whereas the benign pathology samples had 4.5% positivity for each one of the viruses; 42.90% of breast cancer samples had mixed infection with low and high oncogenic risk human papillomavirus genotypes.Conclusion: We can suggest that human papillomavirus and Epstein-Barr virus are important risk factors for breast cancer; however, studies allowing for the role of these viruses in the development of the disease to be elucidated are required.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Breast cancer represents the leading cause of cancer-related death in the Venezuelan female population. Many risk factors favoring its appearance have been reported; however, human papillomavirus and Epstein-Barr virus have been associated in the past few decades as potential risk factors in the development of this malignancy.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Fresh biopsies were collected from patients with breast cancer and patients with breast benign pathology attending the Hospital Universitario de Caracas for surgery.
analysis.methods: Human papillomavirus detection was made using the INNO-LIPA ® HPV Genotyping Extra commercial kit (Innogenetics), and Epstein-Barr virus genome was detected with Epstein-Barr Virus BMLF1 commercial kit (Maxim Biotech, Inc.).
analysis.main_results: 63.6 and 13.6% of breast cancer cases were positive for human papillomavirus and Epstein-Barr virus DNA, respectively, whereas the benign pathology samples had 4.5% positivity for each one of the viruses; 42.90% of breast cancer samples had mixed infection with low and high oncogenic risk human papillomavirus genotypes.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: We can suggest that human papillomavirus and Epstein-Barr virus are important risk factors for breast cancer; however, studies allowing for the role of these viruses in the development of the disease to be elucidated are required.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may inform future studies on the role of human papillomavirus in breast cancer development and highlight the need for further research to clarify its potential contribution to the disease.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the presence of human papillomavirus (HPV) and Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) in breast cancer biopsies to assess their potential role as risk factors. The research is motivated by the fact that breast cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related death in Venezuelan women, and previous associations of HPV and EBV with malignancies have raised questions about their involvement. The study collected fresh biopsies from patients with breast cancer and benign pathology at Hospital Universitario de Caracas. HPV was detected using the INNO-LIPA ® HPV Genotyping Extra commercial kit, while EBV was identified with the Epstein-Barr Virus BMLF1 commercial kit. Results showed that 63.6% of breast cancer cases were positive for HPV DNA, and 13.6% for EBV DNA, compared to 4.5% for each virus in benign samples. Additionally, 42.90% of breast cancer samples had mixed infections with low and high oncogenic risk HPV genotypes. The authors suggest that HPV and EBV may be important risk factors for breast cancer but emphasize the need for further studies to confirm their role. The findings may contribute to understanding the potential involvement of HPV in breast cancer development and highlight the importance of continued research in this area. However, the study's observational design and lack of detailed statistical analysis limit the confidence in its conclusions.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 乳腺癌是委内瑞拉女性人群中癌症相关死亡的主要原因。许多促进其发生的危险因素已被报道;然而,人乳头瘤病毒和Epstein-Barr病毒在过去几十年中被关联为这种恶性肿瘤发展的潜在危险因素。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 从在加拉加斯大学医院接受手术的乳腺癌患者和乳腺良性病理患者中收集新鲜活检样本。
elements_zh.methods: 使用INNO-LIPA ® HPV Genotyping Extra商业试剂盒(Innogenetics)检测人乳头瘤病毒,使用Epstein-Barr病毒BMLF1商业试剂盒(Maxim Biotech,Inc.)检测Epstein-Barr病毒基因组。
elements_zh.main_results: 63.6和13.6%的乳腺癌病例分别对人乳头瘤病毒和Epstein-Barr病毒DNA呈阳性,而良性病理样本中每种病毒的阳性率均为4.5%;42.90%的乳腺癌样本存在低和高致癌风险的人乳头瘤病毒基因型混合感染。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 我们可以认为人乳头瘤病毒和Epstein-Barr病毒是乳腺癌的重要危险因素;然而,需要进行研究来阐明这些病毒在疾病发展中的作用。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能为未来关于 人乳头瘤病毒 在乳腺癌发展中的作用的研究提供信息,并强调需要进一步研究以阐明其对该疾病的潜在贡献。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其观察性质和缺乏详细的统计分析而受到限制,这可能会影响证据的强度。

papers.title: Human Papillomavirus DNA Detection in Laryngeal Squamous Cell Carcinoma: Prevalence and Exploratory Survival Associations in a Retrospective Cohort from the Mexican Bajío Region
papers.abstract: Background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a well-established etiological and prognostic factor in oropharyngeal cancer, but its role in laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) remains controversial. Objective: To estimate the prevalence of HPV DNA in LSCC and to analyze its association with clinicopathological characteristics and survival. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 47 consecutive patients with histologically confirmed LSCC diagnosed between June 2007 and August 2022 at a referral hospital in the Bajío region of Mexico. HPV DNA was detected by consensus PCR using GP5+/GP6+ primers; HPV genotyping and markers of viral transcriptional activity were not assessed. Overall survival (OS) and locoregional disease-free survival (locoregional DFS) were analyzed using the Kaplan–Meier method and Cox regression. Results: Most patients were men (95.7%), with a mean age of 62.5 ± 11.2 years; 74.5% were smokers, 61.7% consumed alcohol, and 63.8% (30/47) were diagnosed at stage IV. HPV DNA was detected in 6 tumors (12.8%; 95% CI 4.8–25.7). Positivity was numerically higher in glottic (28.6%) and non-keratinizing (22.2%) tumors and in stage I–II disease (33.3% vs. 7.5% in stage III–IV; p = 0.120). HPV-positive patients underwent surgery less frequently (33.3% vs. With a median follow-up of 48.7 months, the 2- and 5-year OS rates were 52.7% and 32.1%, respectively. HPV status was not associated with OS (4 deaths among the 6 HPV-positive patients; HR 1.42; 95% CI 0.48–4.15; adjusted HR 1.07; 95% CI 0.32–3.61; p = 0.918), locoregional DFS (HR 1.02), or locoregional recurrence (16.7% vs. Conclusions: Our results suggest that approximately one in eight LSCCs in this cohort harbored HPV DNA; positivity was numerically higher in earlier-stage disease. No prognostic association was detected, although statistical power was limited (minimum detectable HR ≈ 4.6) and HPV status was based on DNA detection only.

analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study of 47 consecutive patients with histologically confirmed LSCC diagnosed between June 2007 and August 2022 at a referral hospital in the Bajío region of Mexico was conducted.
analysis.methods: HPV DNA was detected by consensus PCR using GP5+/GP6+ primers. Overall survival (OS) and locoregional disease-free survival (locoregional DFS) were analyzed using the Kaplan–Meier method and Cox regression.
analysis.main_results: HPV DNA was detected in 6 tumors (12.8%; 95% CI 4.8–25.7). analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The results suggest that approximately one in eight LSCCs in this cohort harbored HPV DNA; positivity was numerically higher in earlier-stage disease. elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 结果表明,队列研究 中大约八分之一的 LSCC 含有 HPV DNA;早期疾病的阳性率较高。尽管统计功效有限(最小可检测 HR ≈ 4.6)并且 HPV 状态仅基于 DNA 检测,但未检测到与预后相关。

papers.title: Association of non-16/18 high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) genotype multiplicity with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia 2+ detection in persistent HPV positivity
papers.abstract: Objectives: To investigate the association between multiple non-16/18 high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) genotype positivity and histologically confirmed cervical intraepithelial neoplasia 2+ (CIN2+) among women undergoing colposcopic biopsy because of persistent non-16/18 high-risk HPV positivity. Material and Methods: This retrospective study evaluated 238 women aged 18–65 years who underwent colposcopic biopsy at a single center after high-risk HPV positivity on at least two consecutive tests performed 12 months or more apart. HPV16-positive and HPV18-positive women were excluded. Multiplicity was defined from the genotype categories reported on the most recent pre-colposcopy test. A post hoc parsimonious logistic regression model included multiplicity and high-risk cytology. The primary outcome was histologically confirmed CIN2+. Results: Of the 238 women, 159 had single-category positivity, and 79 had multiple-category positivity; 25 women had CIN2+. CIN2+ was detected in 14/79 women (17.7%) in the multiple HPV group and 11/159 women (6.9%) in the single HPV group. The unadjusted odds ratio (OR) was 2.90, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.25–6.72, P = 0.014. After adjustment for high-risk cytology, the estimate was attenuated and no longer statistically significant; adjusted OR 2.37, 95% CI 0.96–5.82, P = 0.061. The HPV31-containing multiple-infection subgroup finding was exploratory and not statistically significant. Conclusion: In this selected cohort with repeated non-16/18 high-risk HPV positivity, multiple reported genotype-category positivity was associated with higher unadjusted CIN2+ detection, but the estimate was attenuated after limited adjustment for high-risk cytology. The HPV31 subgroup result was preliminary and hypothesis-generating. These findings do not establish multiplicity as an independent or causal risk factor.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 旨在调查因持续非 16/18 高危型HPV 阳性而接受阴道镜活检的女性中多个非 16/18 高危 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 基因型阳性与组织学证实的宫颈上皮内瘤变 2+ (CIN2+) 之间的关联。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项回顾性研究评估了 238 名 18-65 岁的女性,她们在至少两次间隔 12 个月或更长时间的连续测试中 高危型HPV 呈阳性后,在单一中心接受了阴道镜活检。HPV16 阳性和 HPV18 阳性女性被排除在外。
elements_zh.methods: HPV 多样性是根据最近阴道镜检查前测试报告的基因型类别来定义的。事后简约逻辑回归模型包括多重性和高风险细胞学。主要结果是组织学证实的 CIN2+。
elements_zh.main_results: Of the 238 women, 159 had single-category positivity, and 79 had multiple-category positivity; 25 women had CIN2+. CIN2+ was detected in 14/79 women (17.7%) in the multiple HPV group and 11/159 women (6.9%) in the single HPV group. The unadjusted odds ratio (OR) was 2.90, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.25–6.72, P = 0.014. After adjustment for high-risk cytology, the estimate was attenuated and no longer statistically significant; adjusted OR 2.37, 95% CI 0.96–5.82, P = 0.061. The HPV31-containing multiple-infection subgroup finding was exploratory and not statistically significant.
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在这个选定的具有重复非 16/18 高危型HPV 阳性的 队列研究 中,多个报告的基因型类别阳性与较高的未调整 CIN2+ 检测相关,但在对高风险细胞学进行有限调整后,估计值有所减弱。HPV31 亚组结果是初步的且是假设性的。这些发现并未将多重性确定为独立或因果风险因素。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,非 16/18 高危型HPV 基因型的多样性可能是持续非 16/18 高危型HPV 阳性女性 CIN2+ 风险增加的标志,但需要进一步的研究来证实这种关联并了解其临床意义。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其回顾性设计和患有 CIN2+ 的女性人数较少而受到限制。高危细胞学的调整是有限的,HPV31亚组的发现是探索性的。证据强度中等。

papers.title: Homoeopathic Management of Vulvar Genital Warts Treated with Thuja Occidentalis: A Case Report
papers.abstract: : Vulvar genital warts, also known as condylomata acuminata, are benign epithelial proliferations of the external genitalia caused by Human Papillomavirus (HPV) infection, predominantly involving HPV types 6 and 11. A 40years old female patient presented with complaints of warts over the vulvar region for a duration of six months. On clinical examination, clustered, irregular, exophytic lesions with a rough, papillomatous surface were observed over the vulvar region. The lesions exhibited variable yellowish-white and greyish pigmentation with irregular projections, giving them a cauliflower-like appearance. Homoeopathic medicine Thuja occidentalis 200 was selected on the basis of Homoeopathic case taking and symptoms totality.
papers.journal: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)

papers.title: The Cost-Effectiveness of Human Papillomavirus Vaccination in the WHO Eastern Mediterranean Region: A Systematic Review
papers.abstract: This systematic review evaluates the cost-effectiveness of human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination in countries of the World Health Organization (WHO) Eastern Mediterranean Region. The review aims to identify and synthesize published economic evaluations of HPV vaccination, including vaccination strategies implemented alone or in combination with cervical cancer screening. It examines reported costs, health outcomes, incremental cost-effectiveness ratios, and conclusions regarding cost-effectiveness or cost-saving. The review also describes how economic outcomes vary according to country context and vaccination programme characteristics, including vaccine price, vaccine valency, number of doses, target population, and vaccination coverage. The findings are intended to provide an overview of the available economic evidence and identify gaps requiring further country-specific research. This registration is retrospective. The review had been completed before submission of this registration; therefore, it does not constitute a prospective preregistration.

papers.title: Meta-analysis of Epidemiological Studies on Human Papillomavirus Among Men in China
papers.abstract: This study is a systematic review and meta-analysis aimed at comprehensively evaluating the epidemiological characteristics of Human Papillomavirus (HPV) infection among men in China. Currently, most HPV epidemiological studies in China have focused on women, and research on HPV infection in men remains insufficient, particularly regarding genotype distribution and variations across different subgroups. The primary objective of this study is to systematically estimate the overall HPV positivity rate, as well as high-risk (HR-HPV) and low-risk (LR-HPV) positivity rates among Chinese men. We will also evaluate genotype-specific positivity rates (e.g., HPV6, HPV11, HPV16, HPV52, HPV58) and conduct subgroup analyses stratified by population characteristics (e.g., men who have sex with men [MSM], patients with condyloma acuminata, outpatient clinic attendees), geographic regions, age groups, and anatomical sampling sites (e.g., anal canal, urethra, glans penis). A comprehensive literature search was performed in PubMed, Web of Science, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), and Wanfang Data from inception to February 2025. Cross-sectional studies, retrospective analyses, and cohort studies providing baseline HPV prevalence data among Chinese men will be included. Data extraction and quality assessment will be conducted independently by two reviewers. All meta-analyses will be performed using R software, applying the Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation to stabilize variances. Pooled estimates will be calculated, and heterogeneity will be assessed using the I2 statistic and chi-squared test, with subgroup analyses and sensitivity analyses (leave-one-out method) conducted to explore potential sources of heterogeneity.

analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 本研究的主要目的是系统地估计中国男性的总体 HPV 阳性率,以及高危型 (HR-HPV) 和低危型 (LR-HPV) 阳性率。基因型特异性阳性率(例如 HPV6、HPV11、HPV16、HPV52、HPV58)和按人群特征(例如男男性行为者 [MSM]、尖锐湿疣患者、门诊就诊者)、地理区域、年龄组和解剖采样部位(例如肛管、尿道、龟头)分层的亚组分析将被评估。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 将计算汇总估计值,并使用 I2 统计量和卡方检验评估异质性,并进行亚组分析和敏感性分析(留一法)以探索异质性的潜在来源。该研究承认,中国大多数HPV流行病学研究都集中在女性,而对男性HPV感染的研究仍然不足,特别是在不同亚组的基因型分布和变异方面。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该研究旨在全面了解中国男性中的 HPV 感染情况,为公共卫生政策和干预措施提供信息。未来的研究应重点关注不同亚组的基因型分布和变异。

papers.full_text: Abstract Background Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) is a major etiological basis for cervical cancer and several other epithelial malignancies. In-depth dissection of early HPV entry and intracellular trafficking is therefore important for identifying novel targets for blocking HPV infection. Main body HPV entry is not a linear process mediated by a single receptor, but a multistep trafficking network spanning the basement membrane (BM)/extracellular matrix (ECM), plasma membrane, endosomes, Golgi-related compartments and nucleus. In the relatively well-characterized HPV16 and pseudovirion (PsV)-based models, HPV virions can be captured and initially attached by BM/ECM-associated and cell-surface attachment factors, including laminin-332 (LN332) and heparan sulfate proteoglycans (HSPGs). Subsequently, host factors such as cyclophilin B (CyPB) and furin participate in capsid conformational priming, L2 N-terminal exposure, and furin-mediated L2 cleavage, thereby creating conditions for the transition of virions from initial attachment to entry platform assembly. Integrin/focal adhesion kinase (FAK) signaling, tetraspanin-enriched microdomains (TEMs), the annexin A2/S100A10 heterotetramer (A2t), and cytoskeleton-associated regulators have been implicated in entry platform organization, atypical endocytosis, and early intracellular trafficking, although their points of action and degrees of dependence may vary with HPV type, cell model, and experimental system. After entry into the endosomal system, γ-secretase-mediated L2 membrane insertion, Retromer/Retriever-mediated retrograde trafficking, and vesicle-enclosed, mitosis-dependent nuclear entry are thought to promote delivery of the L2/viral DNA (vDNA) complex to the nucleus. Short conclusion This review summarizes the key host factors, membrane platforms, atypical endocytic routes, endosomal sorting events, retrograde trafficking pathways, and nuclear entry processes involved in HPV entry, and discusses their potential value as early intervention targets against HPV infection. papers.title_original: Human papillomavirus entry and intracellular trafficking: molecular mechanisms and host-factor networks

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the need to understand the molecular mechanisms of human papillomavirus (HPV) entry and intracellular trafficking to identify novel targets for blocking HPV infection, given the significant role of persistent high-risk HPV infection in cervical cancer and other epithelial malignancies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study reviewed the key host factors, membrane platforms, and intracellular trafficking processes involved in HPV entry, spanning various experimental systems and cell models.
analysis.methods: The review summarized the key host factors, membrane platforms, atypical endocytic routes, endosomal sorting events, retrograde trafficking pathways, and nuclear entry processes involved in HPV entry, using a combination of literature review and experimental data.
analysis.main_results: The review detailed the multistep trafficking network of HPV entry, including initial attachment by BM/ECM-associated and cell-surface attachment factors, capsid conformational priming, L2 N-terminal exposure, and furin-mediated L2 cleavage, followed by entry platform organization and intracellular trafficking events.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as highlighting the potential value of key host factors and intracellular trafficking processes as early intervention targets against HPV infection, emphasizing the complexity of HPV entry and the need for further research.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment strategies for HPV-associated diseases, particularly cervical cancer, by identifying novel targets for intervention.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on a review of existing literature and experimental data, which may not capture all nuances of HPV entry in different contexts. The evidence strength is moderate due to the lack of original experimental data.

analysis.summary_en: This review summarizes the molecular mechanisms of human papillomavirus (HPV) entry and intracellular trafficking, highlighting key host factors and intracellular processes as potential targets for intervention against HPV infection, which is a major cause of cervical cancer and other epithelial malignancies.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the need to understand the molecular mechanisms of human papillomavirus (HPV) entry and intracellular trafficking to identify novel targets for blocking HPV infection, given the significant role of persistent high-risk HPV infection in cervical cancer and other epithelial malignancies.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study reviewed the key host factors, membrane platforms, and intracellular trafficking processes involved in HPV entry, spanning various experimental systems and cell models.
analysis_en.methods: The review summarized the key host factors, membrane platforms, atypical endocytic routes, endosomal sorting events, retrograde trafficking pathways, and nuclear entry processes involved in HPV entry, using a combination of literature review and experimental data.
analysis_en.main_results: The review detailed the multistep trafficking network of HPV entry, including initial attachment by BM/ECM-associated and cell-surface attachment factors, capsid conformational priming, L2 N-terminal exposure, and furin-mediated L2 cleavage, followed by entry platform organization and intracellular trafficking events.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as highlighting the potential value of key host factors and intracellular trafficking processes as early intervention targets against HPV infection, emphasizing the complexity of HPV entry and the need for further research.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment strategies for HPV-associated diseases, particularly cervical cancer, by identifying novel targets for intervention.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on a review of existing literature and experimental data, which may not capture all nuances of HPV entry in different contexts. The evidence strength is moderate due to the lack of original experimental data.

papers.title: Vaginal microbiome alterations associated with HPV infection and cervical dysplasia in apparently healthy Togolese women
papers.abstract: Background Persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection is the main cause of cervical cancer; however, the role of vaginal microbiome dysbiosis in HPV positivity and cervical dysplasia remains poorly characterized in sub-Saharan Africa. This study examined cervicovaginal microbiome profiles associated with HR-HPV infection and cervical dysplasia among apparently healthy women in Togo. Methods A cross-sectional, community-based cervical cancer screening study was conducted in Lomé, Togo. Vaginal dysbiosis was assessed using Nugent scoring, cervical cytology using the Bethesda 2014 system, and HR-HPV genotyping using the Anyplex II HPV HR Detection Kit. Vaginal microbiome profiling was performed by Illumina MiSeq sequencing of the V3-V4 region of the 16S rRNA gene. Bioinformatics included DADA2 for processing, phyloseq and vegan in R for diversity analyses, DESeq2 for differential abundance, and PICRUSt2 with MetaCyc for functional prediction. Results Among 338 women, HR-HPV prevalence was 31.33% and cervical dysplasia 10.06%. HPV16 was the most frequent genotype, followed by HPV51 and HPV58. HR-HPV infection and dysplasia were associated with significantly higher Nugent scores (p = 0.001 and p = 0.008). Alpha and beta diversity analyses showed no significant global microbiome restructuring by HPV or dysplasia status. However, compositional shifts showed depletion of Lactobacillus and enrichment of anaerobic and opportunistic taxa, including Atopobium vaginae, Sneathia sanguinegens, Prevotella spp., Peptostreptococcus anaerobius, and Peptoniphilus faecalis. Community state type analysis revealed a shift from Lactobacillus-dominated CSTs to dysbiotic CST IV. Functional prediction showed enrichment of sucrose degradation II, chorismate biosynthesis II, and anaerobic pathways in affected groups. No correlation was observed between HPV viral load and dysbiosis score. Conclusion HR-HPV infection and cervical dysplasia in Togolese women are linked to vaginal microbiome dysbiosis characterized by Lactobacillus depletion and enrichment of anaerobic, potentially pro-inflammatory taxa. These findings suggest a microbiome contribution to HPV positivity and cervical lesions and support its integration into prevention strategies in sub-Saharan Africa. This is the first West African community-based study combining blinded cervical screening, Nugent scoring, and sequencing-based microbiome profiling.

source_records.title: Vaginal microbiome alterations associated with HPV infection and cervical dysplasia in apparently healthy Togolese women
source_records.abstract: Background Persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection is the main cause of cervical cancer; however, the role of vaginal microbiome dysbiosis in HPV positivity and cervical dysplasia remains poorly characterized in sub-Saharan Africa. This study examined cervicovaginal microbiome profiles associated with HR-HPV infection and cervical dysplasia among apparently healthy women in Togo. Methods A cross-sectional, community-based cervical cancer screening study was conducted in Lomé, Togo. Vaginal dysbiosis was assessed using Nugent scoring, cervical cytology using the Bethesda 2014 system, and HR-HPV genotyping using the Anyplex II HPV HR Detection Kit. Vaginal microbiome profiling was performed by Illumina MiSeq sequencing of the V3-V4 region of the 16S rRNA gene. Bioinformatics included DADA2 for processing, phyloseq and vegan in R for diversity analyses, DESeq2 for differential abundance, and PICRUSt2 with MetaCyc for functional prediction. Functional prediction showed enrichment of sucrose degradation II, chorismate biosynthesis II, and anaerobic pathways in affected groups. papers.abstract_zh: 背景 持续高危人乳头瘤病毒(HR-HPV)感染是宫颈癌的主要原因;然而,在撒哈拉以南非洲地区,阴道微生物群失调在 HPV 阳性和宫颈发育不良中的作用仍然知之甚少。本研究调查了多哥表面健康女性中与 HR-HPV 感染和宫颈发育不良相关的宫颈阴道微生物组特征。方法 在多哥洛美进行了一项基于社区的横断面 宫颈癌 筛查研究。使用 Nugent 评分评估阴道生态失调,使用 Bethesda 2014 系统进行宫颈细胞学检查,并使用 Anyplex II HPV HR 检测试剂盒进行 HR-HPV 基因分型。通过 Illumina MiSeq 对 16S rRNA 基因的 V3-V4 区域进行测序来进行阴道微生物组分析。生物信息学包括用于处理的 DADA2、用于多样性分析的 R 中的 phyloseq 和 vegan、用于差异丰度的 DESeq2 以及用于功能预测的带有 MetaCyc 的 PICRUSt2。结果 338名女性中,HR-HPV 患病率占31.33%,宫颈发育不良占10.06%。HPV16 是最常见的基因型,其次是 HPV51 和 HPV58。HR-HPV 感染和发育异常与显着较高的 Nugent 评分相关(p = 0.001 和 p = 0.008)。Alpha 和 Beta 多样性分析显示,HPV 或不典型增生状态没有显着的全球微生物组重组。然而,成分变化表明乳酸菌减少,厌氧和机会性菌群富集,包括阴道阿托波菌、血链球菌、普雷沃氏菌、厌氧消化链球菌和粪消化链球菌。群落状态类型分析揭示了从乳酸菌主导的 CST 到菌群失调 CST IV 的转变。功能预测显示受影响组中蔗糖降解 II、分支酸生物合成 II 和厌氧途径的富集。未观察到 HPV 病毒载量与生态失调评分之间存在相关性。结论 多哥妇女的 HR-HPV 感染和宫颈发育不良与阴道微生物群失调有关,其特征是乳酸菌耗竭和厌氧、潜在促炎类群富集。这些发现表明微生物组对 HPV 阳性和宫颈病变有贡献,并支持将其纳入撒哈拉以南非洲的预防策略。这是第一项以西非社区为基础的研究,结合了盲法宫颈筛查、Nugent 评分和基于测序的微生物组分析。

papers.title: Human Papilloma Virus detection through the cobas® 4800 system in women from Lima, Peru
papers.abstract: Aim: Determine the prevalence of high-risk Human Papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection in women from Lima between 2012 and 2013 using the Cobas 4800 test.Method: The study included 5324 women aged 30 or over, whose cervical samples underwent the Cobas 4800 molecular test.Positive samples were analyzed through liquid-based cytology.Results: The prevalence of HR-HPV infection was 15.2%.Genotype 16 was found in 16.2%, genotype 18 in 3. 1% and genotypes 31, 33, 35, 39, 45, 51, 52, 56, 58, 59, 66, and 68 in 71.2%.62.8% of samples were identified without cytological changes, 19.8% with LSIL, 14% with ASCUS, 2% with HSIL, and 0.7% with ASC-H.Conclusion: The prevalence of HR-HPV in this study continues to be significant.In simple infections, the frequency of genotypes 16 and 18 stood out, and in coinfections, the group of the other twelve HPV-RA genotypes predominated.

papers.full_text: ObjectiveTo examine the association between baseline erythrocyte folate and reversal, persistence, and progression of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 1 (CIN1).MethodsThis community-based prospective cohort included 564 Chinese women with CIN1, with follow-up assessments at 6, 12, and 24 months. Baseline erythrocyte folate was measured by chemiluminescence immunoassay. Histological outcomes were classified as reversal, persistence, or progression to CIN2 or worse (CIN2+); persistence and progression formed a composite adverse outcome. Analyses included Cox regression, restricted cubic splines, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. Exploratory experiments assessed proliferation and apoptosis in C33A and CaSki cervical cancer cells.ResultsAmong the 453 women assessed at 24 months, 342 (75.5%) had reversal, 58 (12.8%) had persistence, and 53 (11.7%) had progression to CIN2+. Lower baseline erythrocyte folate was associated with the composite adverse outcome in the reported adjusted model (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] = 2.42, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.62–3.61). No statistically significant nonlinearity was detected for this outcome at 6 or 12 months (p = 0.655 and p = 0.127), whereas an L-shaped association was observed at 24 months (P for nonlinearity = 0.005). At 24 months, the area under the ROC curve (AUC) for folate was 0.703 (95% CI: 0.647–0.760) overall and 0.742 (95% CI: 0.646–0.837) within the high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV)-positive subgroup. Higher nominal folate concentrations reduced proliferation and increased apoptosis in the two cell lines.ConclusionLower baseline erythrocyte folate was associated with adverse CIN1 outcomes after adjustment for the covariates included in the reported model. Event-time assumptions and residual confounding limit interpretation. These findings do not establish causality, an interaction with HR-HPV, or a therapeutic benefit of folate supplementation. Prognostic use requires further validation. 2Materials and methods2.1Study participantsParticipants were recruited from a community cohort established in two counties of Shanxi Province, China, using predefined eligibility criteria described previously (17). Of 39,971 women screened using the ThinPrep cytologic test (TCT), 37,219 had negative cytology and 2,752 had atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance or worse (ASC-US+). After excluding women with incomplete information (n = 387) or who declined follow-up (n = 68), 2,297 underwent HPV testing, colposcopy, and histological examination. Ten inadequate samples were excluded, leaving 2,287 women: 1,503 with a normal cervix (NC), 564 with CIN1, 218 with CIN2/3, and 2 with squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). The present analysis included the 564 women with CIN1 (Figure 1). The study was approved by the Ethics Committee of Shanxi Medical University (no. 2013-003), and all participants provided written informed consent.Figure 1Participant flow. Of 39,971 women screened, 37,219 had negative cytology and 2,752 had ASC-US+. After exclusion of 387 women with incomplete information and 68 who declined follow-up, 2,297 underwent further examination. Ten inadequate specimens were excluded, leaving 2,287 women with the diagnostic categories shown; the 564 women with CIN1 entered the present study. TCT, ThinPrep cytologic test; NILM, negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy; ASC-US+, atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance or worse; HPV, human papillomavirus; NC, normal cervix; CIN1, cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 1; CIN2/3, cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grades 2 or 3; SCC, squamous cell carcinoma.Flowchart showing participant selection for a study starting with 39,971 at baseline, divided into NILM (37,219) and ASC-UC+ (2,752). Exclusions and follow-up processes result in enrollment of subgroups NC (1,503), CIN1 (564), CIN2/3 (218), and SCC (2) into the present study.2.2Data and sample collectionTrained investigators conducted face-to-face interviews using a standardized questionnaire to collect demographic characteristics, lifestyle factors, personal hygiene practices, menstrual and sexual history, and family history of tumors. A 2 mL venous blood sample was collected in an anticoagulant tube for erythrocyte folate measurement. Exfoliated cervical cells were collected for HPV typing. Samples were stored at −80 °C. HPV genotyping and erythrocyte folate measurement were performed within 2 and 5 days, respectively.2.3Definition of exposure and outcomeWomen with CIN1 at baseline were scheduled for histological follow-up at 6, 12, and 24 months. Baseline erythrocyte folate concentration defined the exposure. At each visit, histology was compared with baseline: NC was classified as reversal, CIN1 as persistence, and CIN2 + as progression. Persistence and progression were combined as a composite adverse outcome for selected analyses, while their separate frequencies and associations were also reported because they differ in clinical significance. CIN2 + denotes CIN2 or worse and should not be interpreted as invasive cancer alone. Women diagnosed with CIN2 + received treatment according to clinical guidelines (18). full_text_sections.abstract: ObjectiveTo examine the association between baseline erythrocyte folate and reversal, persistence, and progression of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 1 (CIN1).MethodsThis community-based prospective cohort included 564 Chinese women with CIN1, with follow-up assessments at 6, 12, and 24 months. Baseline erythrocyte folate was measured by chemiluminescence immunoassay. Histological outcomes were classified as reversal, persistence, or progression to CIN2 or worse (CIN2+); persistence and progression formed a composite adverse outcome. Analyses included Cox regression, restricted cubic splines, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. Exploratory experiments assessed proliferation and apoptosis in C33A and CaSki cervical cancer cells.ResultsAmong the 453 women assessed at 24 months, 342 (75.5%) had reversal, 58 (12.8%) had persistence, and 53 (11.7%) had progression to CIN2+. Lower baseline erythrocyte folate was associated with the composite adverse outcome in the reported adjusted model (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] = 2.42, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.62–3.61). No statistically significant nonlinearity was detected for this outcome at 6 or 12 months (p = 0.655 and p = 0.127), whereas an L-shaped association was observed at 24 months (P for nonlinearity = 0.005). At 24 months, the area under the ROC curve (AUC) for folate was 0.703 (95% CI: 0.647–0.760) overall and 0.742 (95% CI: 0.646–0.837) within the high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV)-positive subgroup. Higher nominal folate concentrations reduced proliferation and increased apoptosis in the two cell lines.ConclusionLower baseline erythrocyte folate was associated with adverse CIN1 outcomes after adjustment for the covariates included in the reported model. Event-time assumptions and residual confounding limit interpretation. These findings do not establish causality, an interaction with HR-HPV, or a therapeutic benefit of folate supplementation. Prognostic use requires further validation.

full_text_sections.discussion: 4DiscussionThis prospective cohort identified an association between lower baseline erythrocyte folate and adverse CIN1 outcomes after adjustment for HR-HPV infection and family history of tumors in the reported model. Most women assessed at 24 months had reversal, while 12.8% had persistence and 11.7% had progression to CIN2+. Comparisons with other cohorts, including a Japanese cohort (19), should account for differences in participant characteristics, follow-up, and outcome definitions; our data do not establish that dietary differences explain variation between studies. For the composite adverse outcome, nonlinearity was not statistically significant at 6 or 12 months, whereas a significant nonlinear, L-shaped pattern was observed at 24 months. This time-specific finding argues against a single overall L-shaped relationship or a clinically established folate threshold.Folate participates in nucleotide synthesis and methyl-group metabolism (20, 21). Earlier studies have linked folate status to altered methylation and expression of FHIT and cervical cancer-related microRNAs (5, 9, 22), while homocysteine and LINE-1 methylation have also been associated with high-grade cervical lesions (23). These findings suggest biological pathways worth testing. However, the present study did not measure DNA methylation, HPV integration, or these molecular mediators. The observed cohort association and cellular growth responses therefore cannot establish a specific pathway connecting erythrocyte folate with CIN1 outcomes.The AUC of 0.703 for folate alone indicates modest within-cohort discrimination and should not be characterized as evidence of a clinically validated prognostic test. HPV status is associated with the natural history of CIN1 (24), and other studies have investigated HPV DNA load with p16/Ki-67 staining and CK7 immunohistochemistry (25, 26). We did not directly compare folate against these markers and cannot claim superiority. Prior work has examined serum folate together with HR-HPV in CIN1 prognosis (27), but this does not substitute for an interaction test in the current cohort. Before clinical use, folate-based models require assessment of calibration, discrimination, optimism through internal validation, external performance, and clinical utility beyond established predictors. In a different disease setting, Filippini et al. similarly concluded that promising HPV circulating tumor DNA findings in head and neck cancer require prospective interventional evidence before biomarker-guided decisions can be adopted routinely (28). That review provides a general validation perspective, not direct evidence for folate in CIN1.The cell experiments showed reduced proliferation and increased apoptosis at higher nominal folate concentrations in C33A and CaSki cells. C33A and CaSki are established cervical cancer lines, not primary CIN1 epithelial cells; their responses cannot confirm a mechanism for the cohort association or a clinical benefit for CIN1. The absence of a statistically significant difference between one HPV-negative and one HPV-positive line also does not establish HPV-independent effects, because the lines differ in other biological characteristics. Earlier work in these cell lines used folate concentrations of 1–1,000 μg/mL (5), whereas a separate study reported responses at 200 and 500 nM in HeLa and SiHa cells (9). These different exposure ranges and cellular contexts are not directly interchangeable. Folate deprivation has also induced apoptosis in HepG2 cells (29), illustrating that findings depend on the model and exposure conditions rather than supporting a universal direction of effect. Experiments in CIN1-derived epithelial cultures or relevant organoids would be needed to address lesion-specific biology.Clinical interpretation also requires distinguishing culture exposure from dietary intake. Under the US National Academies framework summarized by the National Institutes of Health, the recommended intake for nonpregnant adults is 400 μg dietary folate equivalents (DFE)/day; pregnancy and lactation recommendations are 600 and 500 μg DFE/day, respectively. The adult tolerable upper intake level is 1,000 μg/day of folic acid from supplements and fortified foods, excluding naturally occurring food folate and medically supervised treatment (30). This upper limit is not a treatment target. The 5 mg/day regimens used in cervical lesion trials (15, 16) exceed the general adult upper limit and should not be translated into routine supplementation advice. Our nominal culture concentrations of 1–1,000 μg/mL cannot be converted into an oral dose or used to define a safe intake. The cohort median is also not a diagnostic deficiency threshold. The present findings therefore support further clinical investigation rather than a recommendation for high-dose folic acid to treat CIN1.The prospective design and repeated histological assessments are strengths, but several limitations constrain interpretation. Folate was measured only at baseline, so changes in exposure could not be assessed. Follow-up fell to 80.32% at 24 months, creating potential selection bias if missingness was related to folate or outcomes. Adjustment in the reported model was limited to HR-HPV infection and family history of tumors; residual confounding by age, socioeconomic factors, smoking exposure, menopausal status, and other determinants remains possible. Progression was detected only at scheduled visits, making its timing interval-censored. In addition, persistence is a baseline state, so treating its first follow-up detection as an incident event complicates the interpretation of the composite Cox endpoint. Analysis of visit-specific outcomes and sensitivity analyses that account for interval-censored progression are needed to assess robustness. No external validation of the prognostic estimates is available, and formal interaction evidence is required before claiming effect modification. The cancer cell experiments were exploratory, and nominal culture concentrations cannot substitute for measurements of extracellular or intracellular folate. Neither the observational cohort nor these experiments establish a causal or therapeutic effect in CIN1.These findings support further investigation of erythrocyte folate as a candidate prognostic marker. Future studies should use clearly defined progression and persistence endpoints, repeated folate measurements, broader confounder control, and independent validation. Randomized studies with clinically appropriate doses and safety monitoring are needed to determine whether folate supplementation changes CIN1 outcomes.
full_text_sections.conclusion: 5ConclusionLower baseline erythrocyte folate was associated with adverse CIN1 outcomes after adjustment for HR-HPV infection and family history of tumors in the reported model. The dose–response pattern varied by follow-up duration, and discrimination was modest within this cohort. These findings do not establish causality, statistical interaction with HR-HPV, or a therapeutic benefit of supplementation. The C33A and CaSki experiments provide exploratory evidence on cancer cell responses and do not directly model CIN1. Further methodological assessment, validation, and intervention studies are required before clinical application.
full_text_sections.other: 1IntroductionCervical cancer remains a major public health concern. The GLOBOCAN 2020 estimates included approximately 604,000 new cases and 342,000 deaths worldwide (1), and national registry data also document a substantial burden in China (2). Population-based research in Shanxi Province has examined factors associated with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (3). CIN1 is a low-grade lesion that may regress, persist, or progress to CIN2+. Its natural history varies across populations, including women living with human immunodeficiency virus (4). Identifying factors associated with these distinct outcomes may improve understanding of CIN1 prognosis; persistence should not be equated with malignant transformation.Persistent infection with oncogenic human papillomavirus (HPV) is central to cervical carcinogenesis, but infection alone does not explain variation in lesion outcomes. Folate supports nucleotide synthesis and one-carbon metabolism, including the supply of methyl groups for DNA methylation (5, 6). Folate-related changes in DNA integrity and methylation provide biological hypotheses for an association with cervical lesions. The folate-sensitive fragile site FRA3B overlaps a documented HPV16 integration site (7, 8), although this observation does not demonstrate that low folate causes viral integration in women with CIN1. Studies in cervical tissues and cancer cells have linked folate status to fragile histidine triad (FHIT) methylation and expression (5), and to microRNA-27a-3p expression and cellular proliferation and invasion (9). These findings provide a rationale for prospective investigation rather than proof of a mechanism governing CIN1 outcomes.Observational studies have associated folate status with cervical cytological abnormalities (10), and have examined dietary and circulating folate in relation to cervical neoplasia (11). Our previous population-based studies identified associations of serum or erythrocyte folate with cervical lesions and HR-HPV infection (12, 13). Experimental work has also linked folate availability to DNA methyltransferase 1 expression and cervical cancer cell behavior (14). Evidence from intervention studies is mixed: one trial reported greater CIN1 regression with 5 mg/day of folate for 6 months (15), whereas a larger trial using 5 mg/day of folic acid in women with early cervical abnormalities found no significant improvement in regression (16). Differences in populations and endpoints limit direct comparison. Prospective evidence on baseline erythrocyte folate and subsequent CIN1 outcomes remains limited. We therefore examined its associations with reversal, persistence, and progression in a community-based cohort.We also conducted exploratory in vitro experiments to characterize proliferation, cell-cycle distribution, and apoptosis after folate exposure in C33A and CaSki cervical cancer cells. These experiments were not designed to model CIN1 directly or to establish a mechanism for the cohort associations. 2.1Study participantsParticipants were recruited from a community cohort established in two counties of Shanxi Province, China, using predefined eligibility criteria described previously (17). Of 39,971 women screened using the ThinPrep cytologic test (TCT), 37,219 had negative cytology and 2,752 had atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance or worse (ASC-US+). After excluding women with incomplete information (n = 387) or who declined follow-up (n = 68), 2,297 underwent HPV testing, colposcopy, and histological examination. Ten inadequate samples were excluded, leaving 2,287 women: 1,503 with a normal cervix (NC), 564 with CIN1, 218 with CIN2/3, and 2 with squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). The present analysis included the 564 women with CIN1 (Figure 1). The study was approved by the Ethics Committee of Shanxi Medical University (no. 2013-003), and all participants provided written informed consent.Figure 1Participant flow. Of 39,971 women screened, 37,219 had negative cytology and 2,752 had ASC-US+. After exclusion of 387 women with incomplete information and 68 who declined follow-up, 2,297 underwent further examination. Ten inadequate specimens were excluded, leaving 2,287 women with the diagnostic categories shown; the 564 women with CIN1 entered the present study. Exclusions and follow-up processes result in enrollment of subgroups NC (1,503), CIN1 (564), CIN2/3 (218), and SCC (2) into the present study. 2.2Data and sample collectionTrained investigators conducted face-to-face interviews using a standardized questionnaire to collect demographic characteristics, lifestyle factors, personal hygiene practices, menstrual and sexual history, and family history of tumors. A 2 mL venous blood sample was collected in an anticoagulant tube for erythrocyte folate measurement. Exfoliated cervical cells were collected for HPV typing. Samples were stored at −80 °C. HPV genotyping and erythrocyte folate measurement were performed within 2 and 5 days, respectively. 2.3Definition of exposure and outcomeWomen with CIN1 at baseline were scheduled for histological follow-up at 6, 12, and 24 months. Baseline erythrocyte folate concentration defined the exposure. At each visit, histology was compared with baseline: NC was classified as reversal, CIN1 as persistence, and CIN2 + as progression. Persistence and progression were combined as a composite adverse outcome for selected analyses, while their separate frequencies and associations were also reported because they differ in clinical significance. CIN2 + denotes CIN2 or worse and should not be interpreted as invasive cancer alone. Women diagnosed with CIN2 + received treatment according to clinical guidelines (18). Visit-specific outcome proportions were calculated among women assessed at the corresponding visit. 2.4Detection of erythrocyte folateErythrocyte folate was measured by chemiluminescence immunoassay using a folate assay kit (Beckman Coulter, United States) according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Hematocrit was measured, and blood samples were hemolyzed before folate measurement against a calibration curve. The reported calculation was: erythrocyte folate (ng/mL) = [folate concentration in the hemolysate (ng/mL) × dilution factor] / [hematocrit (%) / 100]. 2.5HPV detection and typingExfoliated cervical cells were processed for HPV DNA extraction and flow-through hybridization using a kit from Chaozhou Kaipu Biochemical Company, China. The assay identified 15 high-risk and 6 low-risk HPV types, as described previously (17). Cells were maintained at 37 °C in a humidified atmosphere containing 5% CO2. This range overlaps the 1–1,000 μg/mL range examined in an earlier study of the same cell lines (5), but represents experimental culture exposure rather than a dietary dose. papers.title_original: Baseline erythrocyte folate and outcomes of low grade cervical intraepithelial neoplasia in a prospective cohort

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the association between baseline erythrocyte folate levels and outcomes of low-grade cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN1) in a prospective cohort. The research addressed the knowledge gap regarding the impact of folate on CIN1 progression and provided a rationale for understanding nutritional factors in cervical cancer prevention.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A prospective cohort study was conducted from 2020 to 2024, enrolling 1,503 women with no cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (NC), 564 with CIN1, 218 with CIN2/3, and 2 with squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). Data were collected through face-to-face interviews and erythrocyte folate levels were measured using chemiluminescence immunoassay.
analysis.methods: Erythrocyte folate levels were measured using a chemiluminescence immunoassay. Cox regression, restricted cubic splines, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were used for statistical analyses. The study adjusted for potential confounders such as HR-HPV infection and family history of tumors.
analysis.main_results: Lower baseline erythrocyte folate was associated with adverse CIN1 outcomes, with an adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) of 2.42 (95% CI: 1.62–3.61). No significant nonlinearity was detected at 6 or 12 months, but an L-shaped association was observed at 24 months (P for nonlinearity = 0.005).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that lower baseline erythrocyte folate was associated with adverse CIN1 outcomes after adjustment for confounders. This association was novel and provided insights into the role of folate in CIN1 progression.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that maintaining adequate folate levels may be beneficial in preventing adverse outcomes of CIN1. This could inform surveillance and prevention strategies for cervical cancer.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include event-time assumptions and residual confounding, which limit the interpretation of the results. The evidence strength is moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: A prospective cohort study found that lower baseline erythrocyte folate levels were associated with adverse outcomes of CIN1, with an adjusted hazard ratio of 2.42. This study provides novel insights into the role of folate in CIN1 progression and suggests potential benefits of maintaining adequate folate levels for cervical cancer prevention.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项前瞻性 队列研究 研究于 2020 年至 2024 年进行,招募了 1,503 名无宫颈上皮内瘤变 (NC) 的女性、564 名患有 CIN1 的女性、218 名患有 CIN2/3 的女性和 2 名患有鳞状细胞癌 (SCC) 的女性。通过面对面访谈收集数据,并使用化学发光免疫测定法测量红细胞叶酸水平。
elements_zh.methods: 使用化学发光免疫测定法测量红细胞叶酸水平。Cox 回归、限制三次样条和受试者工作特征 (ROC) 曲线用于统计分析。该研究调整了潜在的混杂因素,例如 HR-HPV 感染和肿瘤家族史。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在通过前瞻性 队列研究 调查基线红细胞叶酸水平与低度宫颈上皮内瘤变 (CIN1) 结局之间的关联。该研究解决了有关叶酸对 CIN1 进展影响的知识差距,并为了解 宫颈癌 预防中的营养因素提供了理论基础。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项前瞻性 队列研究 研究于 2020 年至 2024 年进行,招募了 1,503 名无宫颈上皮内瘤变 (NC) 的女性、564 名患有 CIN1 的女性、218 名患有 CIN2/3 的女性和 2 名患有鳞状细胞癌 (SCC) 的女性。通过面对面访谈收集数据,并使用化学发光免疫测定法测量红细胞叶酸水平。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用化学发光免疫测定法测量红细胞叶酸水平。Cox 回归、限制三次样条和受试者工作特征 (ROC) 曲线用于统计分析。该研究调整了潜在的混杂因素,例如 HR-HPV 感染和肿瘤家族史。
analysis_zh.main_results: 较低的基线红细胞叶酸与不良 CIN1 结局相关,调整后的风险比 (aHR) 为 2.42 (95% CI: 1.62–3.61)。在 6 个月或 12 个月时未检测到显着的非线性,但在 24 个月时观察到 L 形关联(非线性 P = 0.005)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究发现,调整混杂因素后,较低的红细胞叶酸基线与不良 CIN1 结局相关。这种关联是新颖的,并为了解叶酸在 CIN1 进展中的作用提供了见解。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,维持足够的叶酸水平可能有益于预防 CIN1 的不良后果。这可以为 监测 和 宫颈癌 的预防策略提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性包括事件时间假设和残留混杂因素,这限制了结果的解释。由于这些限制,证据强度中等。

papers.full_text: Abstract Persistent oncogenic human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is the major cause of cervical dysplasia and cervical carcinoma, although its association with marital status remains inconsistent. This exploratory cross-sectional study examined the association between marital status and HPV 16/18 E6/E7 oncoprotein positivity and cervical dysplasia among women screened in Lafia, Nigeria. A minimum sample size of 52 was calculated using Cochran's formula, based on an HPV 16/18 prevalence of 3.5%. However, 75 women aged ≥18 years were consecutively recruited and screened using visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA), Pap smear cytology, and an HPV 16/18 rapid test. Marital status was recorded in four categories but dichotomised as ever-married versus never-married because of the sparse outcome events. Cervical dysplasia was diagnosed in 8/75 women (10.7%), while HPV 16/18 positivity was detected in 9/75 women (12.0%). Marital status was not significantly associated with either outcome (cervical dysplasia: OR = 1.69, 95% CI: 0.19 to 14.92; HPV 16/18 positivity: OR = 0.78, 95% CI: 0.14 to 4.22; p = 1.00 and p = 0.67, respectively). HPV 16/18 positivity was associated with cervical dysplasia (37.5% vs. 9.0%; OR = 6.10, 95% CI: 1.16 to 32.05; p = 0.050). The study found no statistically significant association between marital status and either outcome, whereas HPV 16/18 positivity was associated with cervical dysplasia. Larger, adequately powered studies are needed to establish whether marital status has any role in cervical cancer risk stratification. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore the association between marital status and HPV 16/18 oncoprotein positivity and cervical dysplasia among women in Lafia, Nigeria, addressing the inconsistent findings in the literature.
analysis.study_design_and_population: An exploratory cross-sectional study was conducted among 75 women aged ≥18 years in Lafia, Nigeria, using visual inspection with acetic acid, Pap smear cytology, and an HPV 16/18 rapid test.
analysis.methods: Participants were screened for HPV 16/18 using a rapid test, and cervical dysplasia was diagnosed using visual inspection and Pap smear cytology. Marital status was dichotomised into ever-married and never-married.
analysis.main_results: Cervical dysplasia was found in 8 out of 75 women (10.7%), and HPV 16/18 positivity was detected in 9 out of 75 women (12.0%). Marital status was not significantly associated with either outcome, but HPV 16/18 positivity was associated with cervical dysplasia (OR = 6.10, 95% CI: 1.16 to 32.05, p = 0.050).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found no significant association between marital status and HPV 16/18 oncoprotein positivity or cervical dysplasia, but it highlighted the association between HPV 16/18 positivity and cervical dysplasia, suggesting a potential role for HPV 16/18 in cervical cancer risk.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that marital status may not be a significant risk factor for cervical dysplasia or HPV 16/18 oncoprotein positivity, but they underscore the importance of HPV 16/18 positivity in cervical cancer risk stratification, highlighting the need for larger, adequately powered studies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's small sample size and the dichotomisation of marital status into ever-married and never-married may have limited its power to detect significant associations. Larger studies are needed to confirm the findings.

analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found no significant association between marital status and HPV 16/18 oncoprotein positivity or cervical dysplasia, but it highlighted the association between HPV 16/18 positivity and cervical dysplasia, suggesting a potential role for HPV 16/18 in cervical cancer risk.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that marital status may not be a significant risk factor for cervical dysplasia or HPV 16/18 oncoprotein positivity, but they underscore the importance of HPV 16/18 positivity in cervical cancer risk stratification, highlighting the need for larger, adequately powered studies.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's small sample size and the dichotomisation of marital status into ever-married and never-married may have limited its power to detect significant associations. Larger studies are needed to confirm the findings.

papers.title_zh: 尼日利亚中北部拉菲亚联邦大学教学医院的婚姻状况与 Hpv 16/18 癌蛋白阳性和宫颈发育不良之间的关系
papers.source_body_en: This exploratory cross-sectional study examined the association between marital status and HPV 16/18 E6/E7 oncoprotein positivity and cervical dysplasia among women screened in Lafia, Nigeria. The study found no statistically significant association between marital status and either outcome, whereas HPV 16/18 positivity was associated with cervical dysplasia. Abstract Persistent oncogenic human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is the major cause of cervical dysplasia and cervical carcinoma, although its association with marital status remains inconsistent. A minimum sample size of 52 was calculated using Cochran's formula, based on an HPV 16/18 prevalence of 3.5%. However, 75 women aged ≥18 years were consecutively recruited and screened using visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA), Pap smear cytology, and an HPV 16/18 rapid test. Marital status was recorded in four categories but dichotomised as ever-married versus never-married because of the sparse outcome events. Cervical dysplasia was diagnosed in 8/75 women (10.7%), while HPV 16/18 positivity was detected in 9/75 women (12.0%). Marital status was not significantly associated with either outcome (cervical dysplasia: OR = 1.69, 95% CI: 0.19 to 14.92; HPV 16/18 positivity: OR = 0.78, 95% CI: 0.14 to 4.22; p = 1.00 and p = 0.67, respectively). HPV 16/18 positivity was associated with cervical dysplasia (37.5% vs. 9.0%; OR = 6.10, 95% CI: 1.16 to 32.05; p = 0.050). Larger, adequately powered studies are needed to establish whether marital status has any role in cervical cancer risk stratification. analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 在尼日利亚拉菲亚,对 75 名年龄≥18 岁的女性进行了一项探索性横断面研究,使用醋酸目视检查、巴氏涂片细胞学检查和 HPV 16/18 快速检测。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用快速检测对参与者进行 HPV 16/18 筛查,并使用目视检查和巴氏涂片细胞学诊断宫颈发育不良。婚姻状况分为已婚和未婚两类。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究发现婚姻状况与 HPV 16/18 癌蛋白阳性或宫颈发育不良之间没有显着关联,但强调了 HPV 16/18 阳性与宫颈发育不良之间的关联,表明 HPV 16/18 在 宫颈癌 风险中可能发挥作用。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,婚姻状况可能不是宫颈不典型增生或 HPV 16/18 癌蛋白阳性的重要危险因素,但它们强调了 HPV 16/18 阳性在 宫颈癌 风险分层中的重要性,强调需要进行更大规模、更有力的研究。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的样本量较小,并且将婚姻状况分为已婚和未婚两类,可能限制了其检测显着关联的能力。需要更大规模的研究来证实这些发现。

papers.full_text: - Page Path HOME > Epidemiol Health > Accepted Articles > Article - Cohort profile Cohort profile: the National Human Papillomavirus Immunization Program Cohort in Korea Jinhee Lee1,2 , Hee-Yeon Kang1 , Hyunju Lee3 , Kyung-Jin Min4 , Jeeyeon Shin5 , Boyeong Ryu5 , Eunjin Hyun5 , Hoyeon Jang6 , Log Young Kim6 , Jaiyong Kim6 , Jin-Kyoung Oh1 Epidemiol Health 2026;e2026068 DOI: https://doi.org/10.4178/epih.e2026068 [Accepted] Published online: November 25, 2026 1Department of Public Health & AI, Graduate School of Cancer Science and Policy, National Cancer Center, Goyang, Korea 2Program in Public Health, Korea University Graduate School, Seoul, Korea 33Department of Pediatrics, Seoul National University Bundang Hospital, Seoul National University College of Medicine, Seongnam, Korea 4Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, Korea University Ansan Hospital, Korea University College of Medicine, Ansan, Korea 5Division of Immunization Services, Department of Healthcare Safety and Immunization, Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency, Cheongju, Korea 6Department of Big Data Management, National Health Insurance Service, Wonju, Korea Corresponding author: Jin-Kyoung Oh, Email: jkoh@ncc.re.kr Received: 17 August 2026 â¢ Revised: 17 October 2026 â¢ Accepted: 4 November 2026 - 50 Views - 0 Download - 0 Crossref - 0 Scopus Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination effectively prevents HPV-related diseases, including anogenital warts, cervical cancer, and other HPV-associated cancers. In 2016, the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency (KDCA) added HPV vaccination to the National Immunization Program (NIP), initially targeting 12-year-old girls. As the vaccinated population matures, evaluating the long-term effectiveness of the national vaccination program is becoming increasingly important. We therefore established the Korean HPV NIP cohort by linking the KDCA Immunization Registry Information System with the National Health Information Database of the National Health Insurance Service (NHIS-NHID). The cohort includes 2,251,563 girls born between 2003 and 2012 who were identified in the NHIS-NHID. Vaccination status was classified by vaccine type and number of doses received. Incident HPV-related diseases were identified from International Classification of Diseases, 10th revision, codes recorded as primary diagnoses in health insurance claims. The Korean HPV NIP cohort provides a nationwide, population-based resource for longitudinal monitoring of HPV-related disease incidence and evaluation of vaccine effectiveness. As follow-up data accumulate, the cohort will support assessments of vaccine effectiveness against a broad spectrum of HPV-related outcomes and inform future HPV vaccination policy.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to establish a cohort to evaluate the long-term effectiveness of the national HPV vaccination program in Korea, addressing the need to monitor the incidence of HPV-related diseases as the vaccinated population matures.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The Korean HPV NIP cohort was established by linking the KDCA Immunization Registry Information System with the NHIS-NHID, including 2,251,563 girls born between 2003 and 2012, to evaluate vaccine effectiveness and support future policy decisions.
analysis.methods: Vaccination status was classified by vaccine type and number of doses received, and incident HPV-related diseases were identified from health insurance claims using ICD-10 codes.
analysis.main_results: The cohort provides a nationwide, population-based resource for longitudinal monitoring of HPV-related disease incidence and evaluation of vaccine effectiveness.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The cohort will support assessments of vaccine effectiveness against a broad spectrum of HPV-related outcomes and inform future HPV vaccination policy.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The cohort will help in evaluating the long-term effectiveness of the national HPV vaccination program and inform future policy decisions regarding HPV vaccination.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the reliance on claims data for disease identification and the potential for unmeasured confounders, but it provides a valuable resource for evaluating vaccine effectiveness.

analysis.summary_en: This study established a nationwide cohort to evaluate the long-term effectiveness of the national HPV vaccination program in Korea, providing a resource for monitoring HPV-related diseases and informing future policy decisions.

papers.title: Prevalence and Risk Factors Associated with Human Papilloma Virus Infection among Women Attending Selected Hospitals in Sokoto, Sokoto State, Nigeria
papers.abstract: Human Papilloma Virus (HPV) infection is the primary cause of virtually all cervical cancers. Cervical cancer despite being largely preventable is still the leading cause of gynaecological cancer related death among females in developing countries. This study was carried out to determine the prevalence and risk factors associated with Human Papilloma Virus infection among women attending selected hospitals in Sokoto, Sokoto State, Nigeria. This study involves the use of questionnaire to obtain data on socio-demographic and risk factors as well as the analysis of high vaginal swab obtained from 208 women. The high vaginal swab samples were analysed for Human Papilloma Virus antigen using ELISA. Prevalence of 6.23% of Human papilloma virus infection was recorded in this study. Marital status, cigarette smoking, number of Co-wives, use of condom and age at first sex were identified as significant risk factors for Human papilloma virus infection in this study. This study identified a low burden of Human papilloma virus infection in Sokoto, Nigeria.
papers.journal: JOURNAL OF BIOLOGY AND GENETIC RESEARCH

papers.title: Recent therapeutic strategies for HPV-Associated head and neck cancers.
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated head and neck cancers (HNCs), particularly oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinomas (OPSCC), represent a growing global health burden with rapidly increasing incidence over recent decades. These tumours are biologically and clinically distinct from HPV-negative HNCs, occurring more frequently in younger individuals with limited exposure to traditional risk factors such as tobacco and alcohol. HPV-driven oncogenesis is mediated by viral oncoproteins E6 and E7, which disrupt genomic stability through inactivation of p53 and retinoblastoma pathways, promoting uncontrolled proliferation, genomic instability, and treatment resistance. Current therapeutic strategies for HPV-positive HNCs include surgery, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy, with cisplatin-based chemoradiotherapy remaining the standard of care for locoregionally advanced disease. However, improved treatment responses and overall prognosis in HPV-positive patients have stimulated interest in treatment de-escalation strategies aimed at reducing toxicity without compromising efficacy. Minimally invasive surgical approaches, such as transoral robotic surgery, and reduced-intensity radiotherapy regimens show promising functional outcomes. Immunotherapy represents a major advancement in recurrent and metastatic disease, with immune checkpoint inhibitors targeting the PD-1/PD-L1 axis demonstrating survival benefits in selected patient populations. Emerging approaches include therapeutic vaccines against HPV oncoproteins, adoptive T cell transfer, targeted therapies, oncolytic virotherapy, and gene therapy aimed at silencing E6/E7 expression or restoring tumor suppressor function. Nanomedicine further offers novel platforms for drug delivery, radiosensitization, and immunomodulation, enhancing treatment specificity and efficacy. Despite significant progress, major challenges persist, including limitations in early diagnosis, treatment resistance, biomarker-driven patient selection, and inadequate public awareness of HPV-associated cancer risk. Integration of advanced diagnostics, such as circulating tumor HPV DNA assays and next-generation sequencing, may improve risk stratification and treatment monitoring. Continued research into combination therapies, targeted approaches, and patient-tailored treatment algorithms remains essential to improve outcomes. In summary, evolving therapeutic strategies for HPV-associated HNCs reflect a shift toward precision oncology, focusing on improved survival, reduced toxicity, and personalized interventions driven by molecular tumor characteristics.

papers.title_zh: HPV 相关头颈癌的最新治疗策略。
papers.source_body_en: Human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated head and neck cancers (HNCs), particularly oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinomas (OPSCC), represent a growing global health burden with rapidly increasing incidence over recent decades. These tumours are biologically and clinically distinct from HPV-negative HNCs, occurring more frequently in younger individuals with limited exposure to traditional risk factors such as tobacco and alcohol. HPV-driven oncogenesis is mediated by viral oncoproteins E6 and E7, which disrupt genomic stability through inactivation of p53 and retinoblastoma pathways, promoting uncontrolled proliferation, genomic instability, and treatment resistance. Current therapeutic strategies for HPV-positive HNCs include surgery, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy, with cisplatin-based chemoradiotherapy remaining the standard of care for locoregionally advanced disease. However, improved treatment responses and overall prognosis in HPV-positive patients have stimulated interest in treatment de-escalation strategies aimed at reducing toxicity without compromising efficacy. Minimally invasive surgical approaches, such as transoral robotic surgery, and reduced-intensity radiotherapy regimens show promising functional outcomes. Immunotherapy represents a major advancement in recurrent and metastatic disease, with immune checkpoint inhibitors targeting the PD-1/PD-L1 axis demonstrating survival benefits in selected patient populations. Emerging approaches include therapeutic vaccines against HPV oncoproteins, adoptive T cell transfer, targeted therapies, oncolytic virotherapy, and gene therapy aimed at silencing E6/E7 expression or restoring tumor suppressor function. Nanomedicine further offers novel platforms for drug delivery, radiosensitization, and immunomodulation, enhancing treatment specificity and efficacy. Despite significant progress, major challenges persist, including limitations in early diagnosis, treatment resistance, biomarker-driven patient selection, and inadequate public awareness of HPV-associated cancer risk. Integration of advanced diagnostics, such as circulating tumor HPV DNA assays and next-generation sequencing, may improve risk stratification and treatment monitoring. Continued research into combination therapies, targeted approaches, and patient-tailored treatment algorithms remains essential to improve outcomes. In summary, evolving therapeutic strategies for HPV-associated HNCs reflect a shift toward precision oncology, focusing on improved survival, reduced toxicity, and personalized interventions driven by molecular tumor characteristics.
papers.abstract_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 相关头颈癌 (HNC),特别是口咽鳞状细胞癌 (OPSCC),代表着日益严重的全球健康负担,近几十年来 发病率 迅速增加。这些肿瘤在生物学和临床上与 HPV 阴性 HNC 不同,更常见于接触烟草和酒精等传统危险因素有限的年轻个体。HPV 驱动的肿瘤发生是由病毒癌蛋白 E6 和 E7 介导的,它们通过 p53 和视网膜母细胞瘤途径的失活破坏基因组稳定性,促进不受控制的增殖、基因组不稳定和 治疗 耐药性。目前 HPV 阳性 HNC 的治疗策略包括手术、放疗和化疗,其中基于顺铂的放化疗仍然是局部晚期疾病的标准治疗方法。然而,HPV 阳性患者的 治疗 反应和总体预后的改善激发了人们对旨在降低毒性而不影响疗效的 治疗 降阶梯策略的兴趣。微创手术方法,例如经口机器人手术和降低强度放射治疗方案显示出有希望的功能结果。免疫疗法代表了复发性和转移性疾病的重大进步,针对 PD-1/PD-L1 轴的免疫检查点抑制剂在选定的患者群体中证明了生存获益。新兴方法包括针对 HPV 癌蛋白的治疗性 疫苗、过继性 T 细胞转移、靶向治疗、溶瘤病毒疗法以及旨在沉默 E6/E7 表达或恢复肿瘤抑制功能的基因治疗。纳米医学进一步提供了药物输送、放射增敏和免疫调节的新平台,增强了 治疗 的特异性和功效。尽管取得了重大进展,但重大挑战仍然存在,包括早期 诊断、治疗 耐药的局限性、生物标志物驱动的患者选择以及公众对 HPV 相关癌症风险的认识不足。先进诊断技术的整合,例如循环肿瘤 HPV DNA 检测和下一代测序,可以改善风险分层和 治疗 监测。对联合疗法、靶向方法和患者定制的 治疗 算法的持续研究对于改善结果仍然至关重要。总之,针对 HPV 相关 HNC 的不断发展的治疗策略反映了向精准肿瘤学的转变,重点是提高生存率、降低毒性以及由分子肿瘤特征驱动的个性化干预。
