papers.title: Current concern about HPV vaccine safety and self-reported HPV vaccination among female college students in mainland China: A weighted cross-sectional study
papers.abstract: Concern about human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine safety is a potential correlate of vaccination among female college students in China. This weighted cross-sectional study used the 2025 National College Student Survey on Sexual and Reproductive Health, a voluntary, convenience-based online survey conducted across mainland China. The analytic sample comprised 37,329 vaccine-aware female junior-college and undergraduate students; 6,202 eligible respondents who did not know the HPV vaccine were examined separately in selection analyses. Vaccination was self-reported receipt of at least one HPV vaccine dose; dose number, series completion, vaccination date, and record verification were unavailable. Weighted Poisson generalized estimating equations clustered by school adjusted for age, school level, entry grade, region, monthly expenditure, pre-college residence, ethnicity, and maternal education. Vaccination was reported by 6,708/37,329 students (18.0% unweighted; 19.7% weighted). Compared with students who were not concerned, adjusted prevalence ratios were 0.60 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.54-0.67) for very concerned students, 0.55 (0.50-0.60) for concerned students, 0.70 (0.65-0.75) for neutral students, and 1.00 (0.86-1.16) for those not at all concerned. Standardized prevalence was 28.3% in the reference group and 15.5%-19.8% in the concerned and neutral groups. The categorical association departed from a single log-linear pattern ( P < .001) and remained stable across geographic, weighting, covariate, eligibility, and selection analyses. Current concern about HPV vaccine safety was associated with lower prior self-reported vaccination in this vaccine-aware student population. Communication and catch-up strategies warrant prospective evaluation with verified initiation and completion outcomes.

analysis.scope_and_question: The study examines the relationship between concern about HPV vaccine safety and self-reported HPV vaccination among female college students in mainland China. The central question is whether vaccine safety concerns correlate with vaccination rates in this population.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This weighted cross-sectional study used the 2025 National College Student Survey on Sexual and Reproductive Health, a voluntary, convenience-based online survey conducted across mainland China.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The study found that 19.7% of the sample reported receiving at least one HPV vaccine dose. Students who were very concerned or concerned about vaccine safety had lower adjusted prevalence ratios for prior self-reported vaccination compared to those not concerned.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study notes that the categorical association between concern and vaccination departed from a single log-linear pattern, suggesting complex relationships that require further investigation. Additionally, the study did not have verified initiation and completion outcomes for vaccination.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings suggest that communication and catch-up strategies for HPV vaccination should be evaluated prospectively to address safety concerns among college students.

papers.title: Hyperactivation of p53 and pRb is a potential therapeutic option in HPV driven cancers.
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is the most frequently acquired sexually transmitted infection. The E6 and E7 oncoproteins of HPV mainly contribute to the development of cancerous lesions by dysregulating the host p53 and pRb tumour suppressor pathways, respectively. Although prophylactic vaccines are available for HPV infection, they are ineffective for established HPV infections. Despite significant advances in surgery, radiotherapy, and systemic therapies, recurrent, metastatic, and treatment-resistant HPV-associated cancers continue to present substantial clinical challenges, highlighting the urgent need for novel therapeutic strategies.As the E6 and E7 viral oncoproteins are key drivers of HPV-positive cancer pathogenesis, targeting these proteins represents a rational approach for developing new therapies. Gene therapy is currently studied extensively as a potential strategy for cancer regression. RNA interference technology and CRISPR approaches are highly effective in downregulating the expression of viral oncoproteins. In most cancer types, tumour suppressor proteins are frequently mutated; however, in HPV-induced cancers, they typically remain wild type. Hence, increasing the bioavailability of tumour suppressor proteins is a therapeutic option. CRISPR activation (CRISPRa) is a CRISPR system variant in which catalytically inactive Cas9 (dcas9) is fused with a transcriptional activator to induce gene expression. Unlike CRISPR, CRISPRa increases the expression of the targeted gene without genomic modifications. Although there are few strategies available to increase the expression of tumour suppressor proteins, CRISPRa has gained a major focus as an effective and promising strategy. There is potential to develop CRISPRa as a future therapeutic intervention to treat HPV induced cancers combined with other treatment modalities.

papers.title: State-level variation in HPV vaccination initiation among U.S. adolescents after accounting for individual and provider factors
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination prevents HPV-related cancers, yet coverage among U.S. adolescents has plateaued. This study examined whether state-level variation in HPV vaccination initiation persisted after accounting for provider recommendation and individual characteristics. METHODS: We analyzed 2024 National Immunization Survey-Teen data from 14,622 adolescents aged 13-17 years (mean age = 15.04, SD = 1.40). Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression examined provider-verified HPV vaccination initiation (≥1 dose), adjusting for parent-reported healthcare provider recommendation, age, sex, race and ethnicity, poverty status, maternal education, health insurance, and state of residence. Adjusted state-level predicted probabilities were estimated using predictive margins. RESULTS: State of residence remained jointly associated with HPV vaccination initiation after adjustment (design-adjusted Wald test: F[50, 14,502] = 3.76, p < 0.001). Parent-reported healthcare provider recommendation was strongly associated with initiation (AOR = 3.12, 95% CI: 2.67-3.65). Older adolescents had higher odds of HPV vaccination initiation (AOR = 1.17, 95% CI: 1.12-1.23), whereas no significant difference was observed between female and male adolescents. Compared with Hispanic adolescents, non-Hispanic White adolescents had lower odds of initiation (AOR = 0.63, 95% CI: 0.51-0.78). Maternal education and health insurance were also jointly associated with initiation. Adjusted predicted probabilities ranged from 64.5% in Mississippi to 89.7% in Hawaii, a 25.2-percentage-point difference. CONCLUSIONS: State-level variation in HPV vaccination initiation persisted after accounting for parent-reported healthcare provider recommendation and measured sociodemographic and healthcare-related characteristics. These findings support further investigation of place-related contextual factors that may contribute to state-level variation in HPV vaccination coverage.

papers.title_zh: 考虑个人和提供者因素后,美国青少年 HPV 疫苗接种 启动的州级差异
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination prevents HPV-related cancers, yet coverage among U.S. adolescents has plateaued. This study examined whether state-level variation in HPV vaccination initiation persisted after accounting for provider recommendation and individual characteristics. METHODS: We analyzed 2024 National Immunization Survey-Teen data from 14,622 adolescents aged 13-17 years (mean age = 15.04, SD = 1.40). Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression examined provider-verified HPV vaccination initiation (≥1 dose), adjusting for parent-reported healthcare provider recommendation, age, sex, race and ethnicity, poverty status, maternal education, health insurance, and state of residence. Adjusted state-level predicted probabilities were estimated using predictive margins. RESULTS: State of residence remained jointly associated with HPV vaccination initiation after adjustment (design-adjusted Wald test: F[50, 14,502] = 3.76, p < 0.001). Parent-reported healthcare provider recommendation was strongly associated with initiation (AOR = 3.12, 95% CI: 2.67-3.65). Older adolescents had higher odds of HPV vaccination initiation (AOR = 1.17, 95% CI: 1.12-1.23), whereas no significant difference was observed between female and male adolescents. Compared with Hispanic adolescents, non-Hispanic White adolescents had lower odds of initiation (AOR = 0.63, 95% CI: 0.51-0.78). Maternal education and health insurance were also jointly associated with initiation. Adjusted predicted probabilities ranged from 64.5% in Mississippi to 89.7% in Hawaii, a 25.2-percentage-point difference. CONCLUSIONS: State-level variation in HPV vaccination initiation persisted after accounting for parent-reported healthcare provider recommendation and measured sociodemographic and healthcare-related characteristics. These findings support further investigation of place-related contextual factors that may contribute to state-level variation in HPV vaccination coverage.

papers.title: Determinants of HPV self-sampling willingness for cervical cancer screening in Urban and Rural Areas of Thailand: An analytical cross-sectional study
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus (HPV) self-sampling is a feasible strategy to increase cervical cancer screening coverage among under-screened populations. Still, the factors influencing willingness to use self-HPV testing in provincial Thai settings are limited. This study aimed to identify independent factors associated with willingness to use self-HPV testing among women in urban and rural areas of Thailand. METHODS: This analytical cross-sectional survey enrolled Thai women aged 25-60 years residing in Saraburi Province. This study used a structured self-administered questionnaire covering demographic characteristics, HPV knowledge, attitudes, and willingness to use self-HPV testing. Multivariable regression was used to estimate prevalence ratios (PRs). RESULTS: In total, 453 of 527 women (86.0%; 95% CI 82.8%-88.8%) were willing to use self-HPV testing. Knowledge score (PR 1.038 per 10% increase; 95% CI 1.016-1.061) and attitude score (PR 1.092 per 1-point increase; 95% CI 1.022-1.165) were significantly and independently associated with higher willingness, while low household income was significantly associated with lower willingness relative to middle income (PR 0.904; 95% CI 0.830-0.985). Residential area and screening history were not associated with willingness. CONCLUSIONS: Self-HPV willingness was high in both urban and rural settings among digitally accessible respondents, with no statistically significant difference between residential areas; this finding should not be extrapolated to women without digital access. Knowledge and attitudes were the strongest modifiable determinants identified, and this hypothetical willingness should be distinguished from actual uptake, which remains to be evaluated.

papers.title: Love, Sex, and Immunosuppression: A Sexual Health Overview for the Transplant Clinician
papers.abstract: Abstract Sexual health is a critical, yet often overlooked, aspect of comprehensive care for solid organ transplant recipients. While transplantation can restore overall health and quality of life, patients may continue to experience sexual dysfunction because of physiological, psychological, and pharmacological factors. Furthermore, transplant recipients remain at risk for sexually transmitted infections (STIs), including HIV, human papillomavirus (HPV), syphilis, and others, with implications for both patient and graft outcomes. HPV-associated malignancies, particularly anal squamous cell carcinoma, occur at significantly higher rates in this population, highlighting the need for recommendations on targeted screening and vaccination. This review addresses the spectrum of sexual health issues across transplant populations-including liver, kidney, heart, and lung recipients-with practical guidance on sexual function, STI screening, and risk reduction strategies. We outline current evidence and recommendations for preexposure and postexposure prophylaxis against HIV and bacterial STIs, including the use of tenofovir-based preexposure prophylaxis and doxycycline postexposure prophylaxis. We also aim to highlight the role of immunization against HPV, hepatitis B, hepatitis A, and monkeypox virus, emphasizing safety, timing, and efficacy considerations in immunocompromised individuals. Despite growing awareness, implementation of routine sexual health assessment and STI prevention strategies remains inconsistent in transplant medicine. We call for greater integration of sexual health into transplant care pathways and identify key research priorities to optimize outcomes. Clinicians should feel empowered to initiate open conversations, advocate for vaccination and prophylaxis, and tailor care based on individualized risk. This comprehensive update offers practical tools and recommendations to improve sexual health in solid organ transplant recipients.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 性健康是实体器官移植受者综合护理的一个重要但经常被忽视的方面。虽然移植可以恢复整体健康和生活质量,但由于生理、心理和药理因素,患者可能会继续出现性功能障碍。此外,移植受者仍然面临性传播感染 (STI) 的风险,包括 HIV、人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV)、梅毒等,这对患者和移植结果都有影响。HPV 相关恶性肿瘤,特别是肛门鳞状细胞癌,在该人群中的发生率明显较高,这凸显了针对针对性筛查和 疫苗接种 提出建议的必要性。这篇综述讨论了移植人群(包括肝脏、肾脏、心脏和肺脏受者)的一系列性健康问题,并提供了性功能、性传播感染筛查和降低风险策略的实用指导。我们概述了针对艾滋病毒和细菌性传播感染的暴露前和暴露后预防的当前证据和建议,包括使用基于替诺福韦的暴露前预防和多西环素暴露后预防。我们还旨在强调针对 HPV、乙型肝炎、甲型肝炎和猴痘病毒的免疫接种的作用,强调对免疫功能低下个体的安全性、时机和有效性考虑。尽管人们的认识不断提高,但移植医学中常规性健康评估和性传播感染预防策略的实施仍然不一致。我们呼吁将性健康更多地纳入移植护理途径,并确定关键研究重点以优化结果。临床医生应该感到有权发起公开对话,倡导 疫苗接种 和预防,并根据个体化风险定制护理。这一全面的更新提供了实用的工具和建议,以改善实体器官移植受者的性健康。

papers.title: Radiotherapy 2.0: The art of doing less to treat head and neck tumors more effectively
papers.abstract: The management of squamous cell carcinomas of the head and neck is undergoing a major conceptual shift. Long guided by a logic of therapeutic escalation - where the goal was to maximize tumor control at the cost of significant functional sequelae - the field is increasingly moving toward precision personalization. This paradigm shift, which can be described as "Radiotherapy 2.0", is partly driven by the emergence of human papillomavirus-positive oropharyngeal tumors, whose favorable prognosis, particularly in younger and more active patients, has prompted renewed consideration of the balance between the probability of cure and long-term quality of life. The goal is therefore not only to cure, but also to "cure better". This approach - doing less to treat better - is supported by a growing body of clinical evidence suggesting that treatment intensity may be safely reduced in appropriately selected patients. From a geometric standpoint, the emphasis is on anatomical sparing: whether it involves preserving the pharyngeal constrictor muscles to reduce late dysphagia, or omitting prophylactic contralateral cervical irradiation in well-localized cases, selective reduction of irradiation volumes is increasingly being investigated. Quantitatively, reducing physical doses may be feasible when targeting intermediate-risk histological profiles in the adjuvant setting or when relying on dynamic biological selection. In this regard, early tumor response to induction chemotherapy or the assessment of hypoxia via molecular imaging (fluoromisonidazole positron-emission tomography) may represent useful selection tools, including for approaches involving substantial dose reduction to 30 Gy. At the same time, radiobiological optimization of treatment duration through moderate hypofractionation represents a potential therapeutic alternative, reducing treatment duration while maintaining acceptable toxicity. However, this quest for dose de-escalation has also encountered important limitations and requires careful patient selection. Recent data suggest that empirically weakening key components of treatment - whether by replacing cisplatin with cetuximab or by substantially reducing the dose in the presence of lymph node capsule rupture - may increase the risk of locoregional failure. Radiotherapy 2.0 should therefore not be based on empirical treatment reduction, but rather on carefully defined clinical, anatomical and, where available, biological criteria to determine the appropriate dose and treatment volume for each patient.

papers.title_zh: 放射治疗2.0:以更少的努力更有效地治疗头颈部肿瘤的艺术
papers.source_body_en: The management of squamous cell carcinomas of the head and neck is undergoing a major conceptual shift. Long guided by a logic of therapeutic escalation - where the goal was to maximize tumor control at the cost of significant functional sequelae - the field is increasingly moving toward precision personalization. This paradigm shift, which can be described as "Radiotherapy 2.0", is partly driven by the emergence of human papillomavirus-positive oropharyngeal tumors, whose favorable prognosis, particularly in younger and more active patients, has prompted renewed consideration of the balance between the probability of cure and long-term quality of life. The goal is therefore not only to cure, but also to "cure better". This approach - doing less to treat better - is supported by a growing body of clinical evidence suggesting that treatment intensity may be safely reduced in appropriately selected patients. From a geometric standpoint, the emphasis is on anatomical sparing: whether it involves preserving the pharyngeal constrictor muscles to reduce late dysphagia, or omitting prophylactic contralateral cervical irradiation in well-localized cases, selective reduction of irradiation volumes is increasingly being investigated. Quantitatively, reducing physical doses may be feasible when targeting intermediate-risk histological profiles in the adjuvant setting or when relying on dynamic biological selection. In this regard, early tumor response to induction chemotherapy or the assessment of hypoxia via molecular imaging (fluoromisonidazole positron-emission tomography) may represent useful selection tools, including for approaches involving substantial dose reduction to 30 Gy. At the same time, radiobiological optimization of treatment duration through moderate hypofractionation represents a potential therapeutic alternative, reducing treatment duration while maintaining acceptable toxicity. However, this quest for dose de-escalation has also encountered important limitations and requires careful patient selection. Recent data suggest that empirically weakening key components of treatment - whether by replacing cisplatin with cetuximab or by substantially reducing the dose in the presence of lymph node capsule rupture - may increase the risk of locoregional failure. Radiotherapy 2.0 should therefore not be based on empirical treatment reduction, but rather on carefully defined clinical, anatomical and, where available, biological criteria to determine the appropriate dose and treatment volume for each patient.
papers.abstract_zh: 头颈部鳞状细胞癌的治疗正在经历重大的概念转变。长期以来,在治疗升级逻辑的指导下——目标是以重大功能性后遗症为代价最大限度地控制肿瘤——该领域正日益朝着精准个性化方向发展。这种范式转变可以被描述为“放射治疗2.0”,部分原因是人乳头瘤病毒阳性口咽肿瘤的出现,其良好的预后,特别是在年轻和活跃的患者中,促使人们重新考虑治愈概率和长期生活质量之间的平衡。因此,我们的目标不仅是治愈,而且是“更好地治愈”。这种方法——减少治疗效果,得到越来越多的临床证据的支持,表明在适当选择的患者中可以安全地降低 治疗 强度。从几何角度来看,重点是解剖学上的保留:无论是保留咽缩肌以减少晚期吞咽困难,还是在局部病例中省略预防性对侧颈部照射,选择性减少照射量的研究越来越多。从数量上讲,当在佐剂环境中针对中等风险组织学特征或依赖动态生物选择时,减少物理剂量可能是可行的。在这方面,早期肿瘤对诱导化疗的反应或通过分子成像(氟米索硝唑正电子发射断层扫描)评估缺氧可能代表有用的选择工具,包括涉及将剂量大幅减少至 30 Gy 的方法。同时,通过适度大分割对 治疗 持续时间进行放射生物学优化是一种潜在的治疗替代方案,可减少 治疗 持续时间,同时保持可接受的毒性。然而,这种剂量递减的探索也遇到了重要的限制,需要仔细选择患者。最近的数据表明,根据经验削弱 治疗 的关键成分 - 无论是用西妥昔单抗替代顺铂,还是在淋巴结包膜破裂的情况下大幅减少剂量 - 可能会增加局部失败的风险。因此,放射治疗 2.0 不应基于经验性的 治疗 减少,而应基于仔细定义的临床、解剖学和(如果有)生物学标准,以确定每位患者的适当剂量和 治疗 体积。

papers.title: Reducing the burden of cervical cancer in Zambia in the next 40 years: impact of enhanced screening efforts
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Zambia bears one of the world's highest cervical cancer burdens, driven by high human papillomavirus (HPV) prevalence, gaps in vaccination and screening, and the intersecting human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) epidemic. METHODS: In this study we assess the potential impact of scaling up HPV screening alongside vaccination efforts, based on a community outreach plan designed by ICAP Columbia and Zambia's Ministry of Health. The plan targets Zambia's rural communities and promotes self-collection of samples, on-site HPV testing, and same-day treatment when eligible, with referral to hub sites for severe cases. To estimate the expanded screening's impact, we developed an individual-based model capturing HPV transmission through age-structured sexual partnership, and subsequent progression from infection to cervical lesions and cervical cancer. The model was calibrated to Zambia's demographic profile, 2022 HPV prevalence, 2020 cervical cancer incidence. We compared five 40-year scenarios: no intervention, vaccination only (girls 9-14 years); vaccination plus visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA)-based screening targeted towards women living with HIV, and scenarios extending screening to all women ( ~ 200,000 vs ~400,000 tests/year with 5% annual increase). Outcomes were cervical cancer incidence, percent reduction across intervention scenarios, and cumulative cases averted. Uncertainty was quantified via repeated stochastic simulations with bootstrap confidence intervals (CIs). Sensitivity analyses examined alternative HIV incidence trajectories and reduced screening accessibility. RESULTS: By 2060, HPV vaccination alone reduces cervical cancer incidence by 47% (95% CI: 39%-55%) compared to current rates but has limited effect in the first 20 years. Adding population screening accelerates impact: under ~400,000 tests/year, incidence falls 64% (95% CI: 56%-70%) by year 20 and 97% (95% CI: 96%-98%) by year 40, averting ~35,000 cases by 2040 and ~183,000 by 2060 and reaching the World Health Organization elimination threshold by 2060. Exploratory analyses suggest additional long-term benefit from vaccinating boys, especially when vaccination coverage is suboptimal. CONCLUSIONS: In Zambia, vaccination alone will not meaningfully reduce cervical cancer burden in the near term, and pairing vaccination with a community-based HPV-screening/treatment could prevent tens of thousands of cancer cases within two decades and place elimination within reach.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:由于 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 患病率 高、疫苗接种 和筛查方面的差距以及人类免疫缺陷病毒 (HIV) 的交叉流行,赞比亚是世界上 宫颈癌 负担最重的国家之一。方法:在这项研究中,我们根据 ICAP 哥伦比亚和赞比亚卫生部设计的社区外展计划,评估了与 疫苗接种 努力一起扩大 HPV 筛查的潜在影响。该计划针对赞比亚的农村社区,提倡自我采集样本、现场 HPV 检测以及符合条件的当天 治疗,并将严重病例转介至中心地点。为了估计扩大筛查的影响,我们开发了一个基于个体的模型,通过年龄结构的性伴侣以及随后从感染到宫颈病变和 宫颈癌 的进展来捕获 HPV 传播。该模型根据赞比亚的人口特征、2022 HPV 患病率、2020 宫颈癌 发病率 进行了校准。我们比较了 5 种 40 年情景:无干预,仅 疫苗接种(9-14 岁女孩);疫苗接种 加上基于醋酸 (VIA) 筛查的目视检查,针对感染艾滋病毒的女性,以及将筛查范围扩大到所有女性的方案(每年约 200,000 次测试与约 400,000 次测试,每年增加 5%)。结果为 宫颈癌 发病率、干预方案的减少百分比以及避免的累积病例。通过使用引导置信区间 (CI) 进行重复随机模拟来量化不确定性。敏感性分析检查了替代的 HIV 发病率 轨迹并降低了筛查的可及性。结果:到 2060 年,与目前的比率相比,单独使用 HPV 疫苗接种 可使 宫颈癌 发病率 降低 47%(95% CI:39%-55%),但在前 20 年效果有限。增加人群筛查可加速影响:每年约 400,000 次检测,发病率 到 20 年下降 64%(95% CI:56%-70%),到 40 年下降 97%(95% CI:96%-98%),到 2040 年避免约 35,000 例病例,到 2060 年避免约 183,000 例病例,并达到世界卫生组织的目标到 2060 年消除阈值。探索性分析表明,为男孩接种疫苗具有额外的长期益处,特别是当 疫苗接种 覆盖率不理想时。结论:在赞比亚,短期内单独使用 疫苗接种 并不能显着减少 宫颈癌 负担,而将 疫苗接种 与基于社区的 HPV 筛查/治疗 结合起来可以在二十年内预防数以万计的癌症病例,并使消除指日可待。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了赞比亚因高 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 患病率、疫苗接种 和筛查方面的差距以及艾滋病毒流行而造成的高负担。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究利用 ICAP Columbia 和赞比亚卫生部设计的社区外展计划,评估了在赞比亚农村社区扩大 HPV 筛查以及 疫苗接种 工作的潜在影响。
analysis_zh.methods: 开发了一个基于个体的模型来估计 HPV 筛查和 疫苗接种 的影响,并根据赞比亚的人口概况和 2022 HPV 患病率 进行校准,结果包括 宫颈癌 发病率 和通过随机模拟和敏感性分析避免的病例。
analysis_zh.main_results: 到 2060 年,与目前的比率相比,仅 HPV 疫苗接种 就可将 发病率 降低 47%(95% CI:39%-55%),但增加人群筛查会加速影响,到 20 年将 发病率 降低 64%(95% CI:56%-70%),到 20 年降低 97%(95% CI:95% CI: 96%-98%)到40年,在二十年内避免了数以万计的病例。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究表明,将 疫苗接种 与基于社区的 HPV 筛查相结合,可以在二十年内预防数以万计的癌症病例,并使赞比亚的消除目标触手可及。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可为减少赞比亚 宫颈癌 负担的策略提供信息,特别是通过将 HPV 筛查与农村社区的 疫苗接种 工作相结合。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性包括对结果模型的依赖、需要进一步探索替代的 HIV 发病率 轨迹以及降低筛查可及性,对结果的可信度中等。

papers.title: Pre-implementation assessment of upstream domains on the uptake of HPV self-sampling in safety-net settings: a scoping review.
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) screening can be used as an early detector for cervical cancer. The newly US Food and Drug Administration-approved HPV self-sampling tests can be used by safety net practices in the USA to help mitigate the current screening disparities seen in patients. As patient acceptability and capability have already been established, this scoping review synthesizes the barriers and facilitators of implementing HPV self-sampling from the perspective of safety net providers and leadership, and the upstream factors not yet explored in current research. Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, a literature search was conducted exploring peer-reviewed publications and grey literature to establish the current landscape of HPV self-sampling. Findings were organized using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research. From the 57 works included, it was found that safety net practices are capable of implementing HPV self-sampling by utilizing current workflows and team members. However, outer setting guidelines and policies heavily influence the implementation process, likely causing a delay in uptake by safety net practices. Recent guideline endorsements and forthcoming insurance coverage address several of these barriers, making post-approval implementation research in safety net settings an urgent priority.

papers.title: Immunogenicity and acute reactogenicity of the 9-valent HPV vaccine in Chinese females aged 16–32 years: a retrospective cohort study
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The nine-valent human papillomavirus (9vHPV) vaccine offers broad protection against HPV-related diseases. However, its multidimensional safety profile-integrating acute hemodynamic changes, injection-site pain, local inflammatory reactions, and vasovagal responses-remains incompletely characterized. Validated tools for individualised risk prediction are also lacking. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study analysed routinely collected data from 103 females aged 16-32 years who completed the three-dose 9vHPV vaccination schedule (0-2-6 months) between January 2023 and January 2024. Participants were stratified into three age groups: 16-20 (n = 36), 21-26 (n = 33), and 27-32 years (n = 34). Immunogenicity was assessed by geometric mean titers (GMT) and seropositive rates (SPR) for all nine HPV types one month after dose three. Safety outcomes included acute hemodynamic changes (heart rate, blood pressure), injection-site pain (Visual Analog Scale), local inflammatory reactions, systemic adverse events following immunisation (AEFI), and vasovagal reactions. Multidimensional correlation analyses, K-means clustering, temporal scan statistics, and an exploratory logistic regression-based risk prediction models were applied. RESULTS: All nine HPV types achieved SPR ≥98.1% (range 98.1-100%), with GMT ranging from 2832 to 16,875 mIU/mL. The 16-20 years group showed significantly higher GMTs than the 27-32 years group for multiple types (e.g., HPV16: +61.1%, P = 0.010). Acute hemodynamic changes included heart rate elevation in 83.5% of participants, with 98.1% normalising within 30 min. Injection-site pain peaked immediately post-vaccination (VAS 3.8 ± 2.1) and was predominantly mild to moderate (87.4%). Heart rate elevation correlated significantly with pain intensity (Spearman ρ = 0.706, P 85 bpm was an independent predictor of vasovagal reactions (OR = 3.20, P = 0.008), while younger age and lower BMI were significantly associated with the vasovagal-sensitive phenotype. CONCLUSIONS: In this preliminary retrospective cohort, the 9vHPV vaccine induced robust immunogenicity across the 16-32 years age range with no vaccine-related serious adverse events. Acute hemodynamic changes and vasovagal reactions were transient and mostly mild, and were likely influenced by procedural and autonomic factors rather than vaccine components alone. This study provides preliminary integrated evidence linking acute hemodynamic, pain, and local inflammatory responses after 9vHPV vaccination and introduces an internally validated, exploratory risk stratification tool. External validation in unselected real-world cohorts is required before clinical implementation.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:九价 人乳头瘤病毒 (9vHPV) 疫苗 可针对 HPV 相关疾病提供广泛的保护。然而,其多维安全性——整合急性血流动力学变化、注射部位疼痛、局部炎症反应和血管迷走反应——仍未完全表征。还缺乏经过验证的个性化风险预测工具。方法:这项回顾性 队列研究 研究分析了 103 名 16-32 岁女性的常规收集数据,这些女性在 2023 年 1 月至 2024 年 1 月期间完成了三剂 9vHPV 疫苗接种 计划(0-2-6 个月)。参与者被分为三个年龄组:16-20(n = 36)、21-26(n = 33) 和 27-32 岁 (n = 34)。在第三剂给药后一个月,通过所有九种 HPV 类型的几何平均滴度 (GMT) 和血清阳性率 (SPR) 评估免疫原性。安全性结果包括急性血流动力学变化(心率、血压)、注射部位疼痛(视觉模拟量表)、局部炎症反应、免疫后全身不良事件(AEFI)和血管迷走神经反应。应用了多维相关分析、K 均值聚类、时间扫描统计和基于探索性逻辑回归的风险预测模型。结果:所有九种 HPV 类型均达到 SPR ≥98.1%(范围 98.1-100%),GMT 范围为 2832 至 16,875 mIU/mL。对于多种类型,16-20 岁组的 GMT 显着高于 27-32 岁组(例如 HPV16:+61.1%,P = 0.010)。83.5% 的参与者出现急性血流动力学变化,其中心率升高,其中 98.1% 在 30 分钟内恢复正常。注射部位疼痛在 疫苗接种 后立即达到峰值 (VAS 3.8 ± 2.1),主要为轻度至中度 (87.4%)。心率升高与疼痛强度显着相关(Spearman ρ = 0.706,P 85 bpm 是血管迷走神经反应的独立预测因子(OR = 3.20,P = 0.008),而较年轻的年龄和较低的 BMI 与血管迷走神经敏感表型显着相关。结论:在这项初步回顾性 队列研究 中,9vHPV 疫苗 在 16-32 岁年龄范围内诱导强大的免疫原性,没有与 疫苗 相关的严重不良事件。急性血流动力学变化和血管迷走反应是短暂的,大多是轻微的,并且可能受到程序和自主因素的影响,而不是单独的 疫苗 成分的影响。本研究提供了 9vHPV 疫苗接种 后急性血流动力学、疼痛和局部炎症反应之间联系的初步综合证据,并引入了内部验证的探索性风险分层工具。在临床实施之前,需要在未选择的真实世界 队列研究 中进行外部验证。

papers.title: Health Economic Impact and Cost Threshold for Switching From Bivalent to Nonavalent HPV Vaccination for Preadolescent Girls in KwaZulu Natal, South Africa: A Mathematical Modeling Analysis Accounting for the HIV Epidemic.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus bivalent (2vHPV) and nonavalent (9vHPV) vaccines protect against HPV types causing 70% and 90% of cervical cancers, respectively. South African guidelines recommend vaccinating girls ages 9-14 with 1 dose of 2vHPV. Switching recommendations to 9vHPV could avert more cervical cancer burden, but the cost-effectiveness and cost-threshold of 9vHPV in South Africa is unknown. METHODS: Using a validated compartmental HPV and HIV transmission model parameterized to KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, we simulated scenarios of 2vHPV and 9vHPV implementation over 100 years with 2 doses (72% coverage) and 1 dose (80% and 90% coverage) with lifelong or waning single-dose vaccine efficacy. We evaluated cervical cancer cases and deaths averted. We also estimated the maximum cost/dose for 9vHPV to be cost-effective using willingness-to-pay thresholds from $500/disability-adjusted life-year (DALY) averted to $3015/DALY averted (2023 USD). We also assessed the incremental cost-effectiveness ratios of 9vHPV at current costs ($110/dose) compared with 2vHPV ($9.23/dose). RESULTS: Single-dose 9vHPV at 80% coverage could avert 7.9% more cervical cancer cases and 6.4% more deaths than 2vHPV (lifelong efficacy). The maximum 9vHPV price to be cost-effective (lifelong efficacy, 80% coverage) ranged from $15 ($500/DALY averted threshold) to $45/dose ($3015/DALY averted threshold). At current market costs, single-dose 9vHPV at 90% coverage exceeds commonly used cost-effective thresholds with incremental cost-effectiveness ratios of $10,480/DALY averted (lifelong efficacy) and $8806/DALY averted (waning efficacy). CONCLUSIONS: Implementing 9vHPV can result in a greater reduction in cervical cancer burden than 2vHPV, but vaccine costs need to be reduced for 9vHPV to be cost-effective in KwaZulu-Natal.
papers.journal: Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999)

Switching recommendations to 9vHPV could avert more cervical cancer burden, but the cost-effectiveness and cost-threshold of 9vHPV in South Africa is unknown. Methods Using a validated compartmental HPV and HIV transmission model parameterized to KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, we simulated scenarios of 2vHPV and 9vHPV implementation over 100 years with 2 doses (72% coverage) and 1 dose (80% and 90% coverage) with lifelong or waning single-dose vaccine efficacy. We evaluated cervical cancer cases and deaths averted. We also estimated the maximum cost/dose for 9vHPV to be cost-effective using willingness-to-pay thresholds from $500/disability-adjusted life-year (DALY) averted to $3015/DALY averted (2023 USD). We also assessed the incremental cost-effectiveness ratios of 9vHPV at current costs ($110/dose) compared with 2vHPV ($9.23/dose). Results Single-dose 9vHPV at 80% coverage could avert 7.9% more cervical cancer cases and 6.4% more deaths than 2vHPV (lifelong efficacy). The maximum 9vHPV price to be cost-effective (lifelong efficacy, 80% coverage) ranged from $15 ($500/DALY averted threshold) to $45/dose ($3015/DALY averted threshold). At current market costs, single-dose 9vHPV at 90% coverage exceeds commonly used cost-effective thresholds with incremental cost-effectiveness ratios of $10,480/DALY averted (lifelong efficacy) and $8806/DALY averted (waning efficacy). Conclusions Implementing 9vHPV can result in a greater reduction in cervical cancer burden than 2vHPV, but vaccine costs need to be reduced for 9vHPV to be cost-effective in KwaZulu-Natal.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:人乳头瘤病毒 二价 (2vHPV) 和非价 (9vHPV) 疫苗 分别可预防导致 宫颈癌 的 70% 和 90% 的 HPV 类型。南非指南建议为 9-14 岁的女孩接种 1 剂 2vHPV 疫苗。将建议改为 9vHPV 可以避免更多的 宫颈癌 负担,但 9vHPV 在南非的成本效益和成本阈值尚不清楚。方法:使用参数化于南非夸祖鲁-纳塔尔省的经过验证的区室 HPV 和 HIV 传播 模型,我们模拟了 100 年来 2vHPV 和 9vHPV 实施的场景,其中 2 剂(72% 覆盖率)和 1 剂(80% 和 90% 覆盖率)具有终生或减弱的单剂 疫苗 功效。我们评估了 宫颈癌 病例和避免的死亡。我们还使用支付意愿阈值从 500 美元/避免的伤残调整生命年 (DALY) 到 3015 美元/避免的 DALY(2023 美元)估计 9vHPV 的最大成本/剂量具有成本效益。我们还评估了 9vHPV 按当前成本(110 美元/剂)与 2vHPV(9.23 美元/剂)相比的增量成本效益比。结果:单剂 9vHPV 覆盖率达到 80%,与 2vHPV 相比,可避免多 7.9% 的 宫颈癌 病例和多 6.4% 的死亡(终身疗效)。具有成本效益的 9vHPV 最高价格(终身疗效,80% 覆盖率)范围从 15 美元(500 美元/DALY 避免阈值)到 45 美元/剂量(3015 美元/DALY 避免阈值)。按照目前的市场成本,覆盖率达 90% 的单剂 9vHPV 超过了常用的成本效益阈值,增量成本效益比为 10,480 美元/避免 DALY(终身功效)和 8806 美元/避免 DALY(功效减弱)。结论:与 2vHPV 相比,实施 9vHPV 可以更大程度地减少 宫颈癌 负担,但需要降低 疫苗 成本才能使 9vHPV 在夸祖鲁-纳塔尔省具有成本效益。

papers.title: Determining the Challenges and Opportunities for Increasing HPV Vaccine Awareness in Bangladesh: A Qualitative Study
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background and Aims Cervical cancer remains a major public health issue in low‐ and middle‐income countries, including Bangladesh, where awareness of cervical cancer and the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine is limited. To reduce the disease burden, Bangladesh launched a free HPV vaccination program for girls ages 10–14 in 2023. However, coverage remains low due to limited reach, low awareness, and cultural resistance. This study examined the challenges and opportunities that influence HPV vaccine awareness and uptake in Bangladesh. Methods A total of 25 Key Informant Interviews (KIIs) and In‐Depth Interviews (IDIs) were completed, comprising 9 KIIs and 16 IDIs, including an Expanded Program on Immunization (EPI) program manager (n = 2); a Civil Surgeon (n = 1); community health workers (n = 3); religious leaders (n = 3); parents (n = 4); teachers (n = 6); and students (n = 6) from Dhaka, Chittagong, and Cox's Bazar districts. All interviews were transcribed verbatim and analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis (Braun & Clarke) to identify key themes related to barriers and facilitators of vaccine awareness and acceptance. Results We identified four major themes and 12 sub‐themes. Findings revealed a significant lack of understanding among adolescent girls about cervical cancer symptoms, prevention, and the importance of HPV vaccination. Negative perceptions among community health workers, parents, and teachers, particularly in rural areas, further hindered vaccine uptake. papers.title_zh: 确定孟加拉国提高 HPV 疫苗 意识的挑战和机遇:定性研究
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT Background and Aims Cervical cancer remains a major public health issue in low‐ and middle‐income countries, including Bangladesh, where awareness of cervical cancer and the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine is limited. To reduce the disease burden, Bangladesh launched a free HPV vaccination program for girls ages 10–14 in 2023. However, coverage remains low due to limited reach, low awareness, and cultural resistance. This study examined the challenges and opportunities that influence HPV vaccine awareness and uptake in Bangladesh. Methods A total of 25 Key Informant Interviews (KIIs) and In‐Depth Interviews (IDIs) were completed, comprising 9 KIIs and 16 IDIs, including an Expanded Program on Immunization (EPI) program manager (n = 2); a Civil Surgeon (n = 1); community health workers (n = 3); religious leaders (n = 3); parents (n = 4); teachers (n = 6); and students (n = 6) from Dhaka, Chittagong, and Cox's Bazar districts. All interviews were transcribed verbatim and analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis (Braun & Clarke) to identify key themes related to barriers and facilitators of vaccine awareness and acceptance. Results We identified four major themes and 12 sub‐themes. Findings revealed a significant lack of understanding among adolescent girls about cervical cancer symptoms, prevention, and the importance of HPV vaccination. Negative perceptions among community health workers, parents, and teachers, particularly in rural areas, further hindered vaccine uptake. Religious and cultural concerns were major barriers to acceptance. Participants suggested that organizing teacher–parent meetings, school‐based health education sessions, and awareness campaigns could help increase vaccine acceptance and understanding. Conclusions Knowledge and perceptions about HPV vaccination varied across stakeholder groups, influencing overall vaccine acceptance. Tailored, community‐based educational interventions are crucial to address misconceptions and enhance awareness among adolescents and key community influencers. Strengthening multi‐sectoral collaboration could increase HPV vaccination coverage and support cervical cancer prevention efforts in Bangladesh.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景和目标 宫颈癌 仍然是低收入和中等收入国家的一个主要公共卫生问题,其中包括孟加拉国,这些国家对 宫颈癌 和 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 疫苗 的认识有限。为了减轻疾病负担,孟加拉国于 2023 年针对 10-14 岁女孩启动了免费 HPV 疫苗接种 计划。然而,由于覆盖范围有限、意识低下和文化阻力,覆盖率仍然较低。本研究探讨了影响孟加拉国 HPV 疫苗 认知和使用的挑战和机遇。方法 完成了总共 25 名关键知情人访谈 (KII) 和深度访谈 (IDI),其中 9 名 KII 和 16 名 IDI,其中包括一名扩大免疫规划 (EPI) 项目经理 (n = 2);一名民间外科医生(n = 1);社区卫生工作者(n = 3);宗教领袖(n = 3);父母(n = 4);教师(n = 6);以及来自达卡、吉大港和考克斯巴扎尔地区的学生 (n = 6)。所有访谈均逐字记录,并使用反思性主题分析(Braun & Clarke)进行分析,以确定与 疫苗 认知和接受的障碍和促进因素相关的关键主题。结果 我们确定了 4 个主要主题和 12 个子主题。调查结果显示,青春期女孩对 宫颈癌 症状、预防以及 HPV 疫苗接种 的重要性严重缺乏了解。社区卫生工作者、家长和教师(尤其是农村地区)的负面看法进一步阻碍了 疫苗 的采用。宗教和文化问题是接受的主要障碍。参与者建议,组织教师家长会、校本健康教育课程和宣传活动有助于提高 疫苗 的接受度和理解。结论 不同利益相关群体对 HPV 疫苗接种 的了解和看法各不相同,影响了 疫苗 的整体接受度。量身定制的、基于社区的教育干预措施对于消除误解并提高青少年和主要社区影响者的认识至关重要。加强多部门合作可以提高 HPV 疫苗接种 覆盖率并支持孟加拉国的 宫颈癌 预防工作。

papers.title: Computational discovery of potential HPV E6 and E7 binders from Lissachatina fulica slime for oral squamous cell carcinoma therapeutics
papers.abstract: CONTEXT: High-risk human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is primarily driven by the viral oncoproteins E6 and E7 which promote malignant progression through inactivation of the tumour suppressors p53 and retinoblastoma protein. This study investigated 26 bioactive metabolites from the slime of Lissachatina fulica as computationally predicted binders of HPV16 E6 and E7 proteins. Among identified metabolites, the drug-likeness, pharmacokinetic, toxicity profiles were further evaluated along with two reference compounds Curcumene and Melphalan. Nineteen compounds satisfied the screening criteria were subjected to molecular docking against HPV16 E6 and E7 proteins. The highest-ranking complexes were further evaluated by molecular dynamics simulations. Phenol, 2,4-bis(1,1-dimethylethyl)- formed the most stable complex with HPV16 E6 whereas (16R,17S)-10,10,16,17-tetramethyl-6-phenyl- and calophyllolide exhibited the greatest stability with HPV16 E7 highlighting L. fulica slime as a putative source of candidate molecules for further experimental investigation against HPV-associated OSCC. METHODS: Twenty-six metabolites identified from L. fulica slime were screened for drug-likeness, pharmacokinetic and toxicity properties using SwissADME and ProTox-3.0. Nineteen compounds satisfying the screening criteria were docked against HPV16 proteins using AutoDock Vina with Curcumene and Melphalan as reference compounds. The highest-ranked protein-ligand complexes were subjected to 500 ns extended molecular dynamics simulations using the GROMACS package with the CHARMM27 force field. Trajectory analyses included root mean square deviation (RMSD), root mean square fluctuation (RMSF), radius of gyration (Rg), solvent-accessible surface area (SASA), and hydrogen-bond analysis.

papers.title_zh: 计算发现 Lissachatina fulica 粘液中潜在的 HPV E6 和 E7 结合剂用于口腔鳞状细胞癌治疗
papers.source_body_en: CONTEXT: High-risk human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is primarily driven by the viral oncoproteins E6 and E7 which promote malignant progression through inactivation of the tumour suppressors p53 and retinoblastoma protein. This study investigated 26 bioactive metabolites from the slime of Lissachatina fulica as computationally predicted binders of HPV16 E6 and E7 proteins. Among identified metabolites, the drug-likeness, pharmacokinetic, toxicity profiles were further evaluated along with two reference compounds Curcumene and Melphalan. Nineteen compounds satisfied the screening criteria were subjected to molecular docking against HPV16 E6 and E7 proteins. The highest-ranking complexes were further evaluated by molecular dynamics simulations. Phenol, 2,4-bis(1,1-dimethylethyl)- formed the most stable complex with HPV16 E6 whereas (16R,17S)-10,10,16,17-tetramethyl-6-phenyl- and calophyllolide exhibited the greatest stability with HPV16 E7 highlighting L. fulica slime as a putative source of candidate molecules for further experimental investigation against HPV-associated OSCC. METHODS: Twenty-six metabolites identified from L. fulica slime were screened for drug-likeness, pharmacokinetic and toxicity properties using SwissADME and ProTox-3.0. Nineteen compounds satisfying the screening criteria were docked against HPV16 proteins using AutoDock Vina with Curcumene and Melphalan as reference compounds. The highest-ranked protein-ligand complexes were subjected to 500 ns extended molecular dynamics simulations using the GROMACS package with the CHARMM27 force field. Trajectory analyses included root mean square deviation (RMSD), root mean square fluctuation (RMSF), radius of gyration (Rg), solvent-accessible surface area (SASA), and hydrogen-bond analysis.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:高危 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 相关口腔鳞状细胞癌 (OSCC) 主要由病毒癌蛋白 E6 和 E7 驱动,它们通过肿瘤抑制因子 p53 和视网膜母细胞瘤蛋白的失活促进恶性进展。这项研究调查了来自 Lissachatina fulica 粘液的 26 种生物活性代谢物,作为计算预测的 HPV16 E6 和 E7 蛋白的结合物。在已确定的代谢物中,与两种参考化合物姜黄烯和美法仑一起进一步评估了药物相似性、药代动力学和毒性特征。对 19 种满足筛选标准的化合物进行针对 HPV16 E6 和 E7 蛋白的分子对接。通过分子动力学模拟进一步评估排名最高的复合物。苯酚、2,4-双(1,1-二甲基乙基)-与HPV16 E6形成最稳定的复合物,而(16R,17S)-10,10,16,17-四甲基-6-苯基-和calophyllolide与HPV16 E7表现出最大的稳定性,突出显示L. fulica粘液作为候选分子的推定来源,用于针对HPV相关OSCC的进一步实验研究。方法:使用 SwissADME 和 ProTox-3.0 对从 L. fulica 粘液中鉴定出的 26 种代谢物进行药物相似性、药代动力学和毒性特性筛选。使用 AutoDock Vina 以姜黄烯和美法仑作为参考化合物,将满足筛选标准的 19 种化合物与 HPV16 蛋白进行对接。使用带有 CHARMM27 力场的 GROMACS 软件包对排名最高的蛋白质-配体复合物进行 500 ns 扩展分子动力学模拟。轨迹分析包括均方根偏差 (RMSD)、均方根波动 (RMSF)、回转半径 (Rg)、溶剂可及表面积 (SASA) 和氢键分析。

papers.title: Clinical testing source is associated with observed HPV burden in hospital-based cervical HPV genotyping: a retrospective study of 36,362 women
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hospital-based cervical HPV genotyping datasets include women tested through different clinical pathways, so observed HPV burden may vary by source population. We quantified source-specific HPV burden and evaluated cytology-linked context. METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective observational study of 36,362 women with one retained index HPV test per woman. All underwent uniform 23-type cervical HPV genotyping by PCR-reverse dot blot and were classified as health examination attendees or gynecology outpatients by clinical testing source. Primary outcomes were any HPV positivity, 12-type carcinogenic HPV positivity, and multiple-genotype infection. Source-group prevalence ratios were adjusted for age group and calendar quarter of testing. Cytology was linked within a prespecified ±3-day window. RESULTS: The cohort included 9,969 health examination attendees and 26,393 gynecology outpatients; cytology was linked for 34,049 women (93.6%). Compared with health examination attendees, gynecology outpatients had higher any HPV positivity (28.7% vs 17.2%; adjusted PR, 1.61; 95% CI, 1.54-1.69), 12-type carcinogenic HPV positivity (19.4% vs 10.7%; adjusted PR, 1.75; 95% CI, 1.65-1.86), and multiple-genotype infection (9.2% vs 3.9%; adjusted PR, 2.23; 95% CI, 2.01-2.48). HPV16/18 and HPV52/58 positivity also varied across cytology strata. Source-group contrasts were attenuated but remained in the same direction after exclusion of an HPV/STI-related clinical-label subset and after restriction to women with linked cytology. CONCLUSIONS: Clinical testing source was associated with substantial differences in observed HPV burden within a uniform hospital laboratory workflow, highlighting the importance of clinical setting and source population when hospital-based HPV estimates are interpreted.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 基于医院的宫颈 HPV 基因分型数据集包括通过不同临床途径进行测试的女性,因此观察到的 HPV 负担可能因来源人群而异。我们量化了特定来源的 HPV 负荷并评估了细胞学相关的背景。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们对 36,362 名女性进行了一项单中心回顾性观察研究,每名女性进行了一次保留指数 HPV 检测。所有患者均接受统一的PCR-反向斑点杂交23型宫颈HPV基因分型,并按临床检测来源分类为体检参加者或妇科门诊患者。
elements_zh.methods: 主要结果是任何 HPV 阳性、12 型致癌 HPV 阳性和多基因型感染。源组 患病率 比率根据年龄组和测试日历季度进行调整。细胞学在预先指定的±3天窗口内进行关联。
elements_zh.main_results: The cohort included 9,969 health examination attendees and 26,393 gynecology outpatients; cytology was linked for 34,049 women (93.6%). elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 临床检测来源与统一医院实验室工作流程中观察到的 HPV 负担存在显着差异相关,这凸显了在解释基于医院的 HPV 估计值时临床环境和来源人群的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果告诫不要在不考虑临床环境和来源人群的情况下解释基于医院的 HPV 估计值,这可能会影响观察到的 HPV 负担并为更准确的 监测 和 诊断 策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 在排除 HPV/STI 相关临床标签子集以及限制具有相关细胞学的女性后,来源组对比有所减弱,但仍保持相同方向。由于回顾性设计和潜在的残留混杂因素,证据是中等的。

papers.title: Natural killer cell dysfunction in cervical cancer: HPV-driven immune evasion through the tumor immune microenvironment barrier
papers.abstract: Cervical cancer, driven by persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV), remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Natural killer (NK) cells are critical mediators of antitumor immunity, and their dysfunction in cervical cancer has been reported. However, current understanding remains uneven, with most studies focusing on isolated mechanisms rather than providing an integrated view of how the HPV-mediated tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) impairs NK cell functions in cervical cancer. In this review, we integrate HPV-driven immune modulation with TIME remodeling to examine how structural, cellular, molecular, and metabolic constraints may converge to restrict NK cell infiltration and function in cervical cancer, distinguishing cervical cancer-specific, HPV-associated, and cross-tumor evidence. Furthermore, we discuss emerging therapeutic strategies targeting these barriers and emphasize their potential as complementary approaches to existing immunotherapies, while noting that most remain preclinical or hypothesis-generating in cervical cancer. This framework provides a unified perspective to guide the development of more effective NK cell–based immunotherapies in cervical cancer.
papers.journal: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology

papers.title: Understanding Cervical Screening Engagement Among Young South Asian Women: Perspectives of Women and Healthcare Professionals.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite increased uptake of the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine, cervical screening participation among younger South Asian women has declined, particularly in deprived areas in England. The reasons for this pattern remain poorly understood. This study explored barriers and facilitators to cervical screening among South Asian women aged 25-29 in a deprived locality. METHODS: Semi-structured interviews were conducted with South Asian women aged 25-29 (n = 15) and healthcare professionals involved in cervical screening delivery (n = 6) in Blackburn with Darwen. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. RESULTS: Barriers to screening were multifactorial and included limited understanding of cervical screening and HPV, cultural norms surrounding modesty and sexuality, fear of community judgement and embarrassment, and structural challenges such as appointment access and competing responsibilities. Family networks acted as both barriers and facilitators. Healthcare professionals described adapting language to reduce fear, but highlighted service pressures related to staffing and funding, which constrained proactive engagement. Although most women reported receiving the HPV vaccination, understanding of HPV and the continued importance of cervical screening remained limited, highlighting opportunities to reinforce cervical screening education. CONCLUSION: Cervical screening engagement among young South Asian women is shaped by intersecting cultural, emotional, and structural influences, which may be intensified in deprived settings. HPV vaccination should be accompanied by clear communication about the continued importance of cervical screening, particularly where knowledge and awareness remain low. Culturally responsive communication, flexible service provision and community partnership approaches are needed to address persistent inequalities in screening uptake. PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: The study was informed by prior community engagement and public involvement work with underserved populations. Interview guides were developed in collaboration with a public advisor from the South Asian community to ensure they were relevant, inclusive, and reflective of community priorities.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:尽管 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 疫苗 的使用率有所增加,但南亚年轻女性的宫颈筛查参与率有所下降,特别是在英格兰的贫困地区。造成这种模式的原因仍然知之甚少。本研究探讨了贫困地区 25-29 岁南亚女性宫颈筛查的障碍和促进因素。方法:与 Darwen 一起对布莱克本 25-29 岁的南亚女性 (n = 15) 和参与宫颈筛查的医疗保健专业人员 (n = 6) 进行半结构化访谈。使用反思性主题分析对数据进行分析。结果:筛查的障碍是多因素的,包括对宫颈筛查和 HPV 的了解有限、关于谦虚和性的文化规范、对社区判断和尴尬的恐惧,以及预约机会和竞争责任等结构性挑战。家庭网络既是障碍又是促进者。医疗保健专业人员描述了调整语言以减少恐惧,但强调了与人员配置和资金相关的服务压力,这限制了积极参与。尽管大多数女性报告接受了 HPV 疫苗接种,但对 HPV 和宫颈筛查的持续重要性的了解仍然有限,这凸显了加强宫颈筛查教育的机会。结论:南亚年轻女性的宫颈筛查参与度受到文化、情感和结构等交叉影响的影响,这种影响在贫困环境中可能会加剧。HPV 疫苗接种 应伴随着关于宫颈筛查的持续重要性的明确沟通,特别是在知识和意识仍然较低的情况下。需要采取文化敏感的沟通、灵活的服务提供和社区伙伴关系方法来解决筛查方面持续存在的不平等问题。患者或公众贡献:该研究是根据先前的社区参与和针对服务不足人群的公众参与工作而进行的。访谈指南是与南亚社区的公共顾问合作制定的,以确保它们具有相关性、包容性并反映社区的优先事项。

papers.title: Uptake of the HPV vaccine in girls and boys with an intellectual disability: a systematic review.
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Cervical cancer is the fourth most common female cancer and is preventable by (human papillomavirus) HPV vaccination, given to adolescent girls and boys in most World Health Organisation countries. People with an intellectual disability have significantly worse cancer outcomes than the general population, attributable to deficits in prevention, screening, early diagnosis and treatment, and there is concern that rates of HPV vaccination may be lower in this population. The aim was to undertake a systematic review of research into HPV vaccination uptake in people with intellectual disability, and influences on vaccination. Methods Multiple databases (Medline; Embase; CINAHL; PsycINFO; Cochrane Central; Overton) were searched to May 2026. Quantitative, qualitative and mixed-methods studies were eligible if they: (i) reported rates of HPV vaccination uptake in people with an intellectual disability, or (ii) reported factors influencing HPV vaccination in people with an intellectual disability. Two reviewers independently screened studies and took inclusion decisions. Data extraction and quality appraisal (JBI tools) were undertaken by one researcher and verified by another. Data on vaccination initiation and completion rates were synthesised narratively and meta-analysed (risk ratio, RR) as appropriate; influences on vaccination were mapped to the Socio-Ecological Model. Results 25 studies (18 quantitative; 7 qualitative) from eight high-income countries were included. Meta-analyses showed that girls and boys with intellectual disability were less likely to receive the vaccine (RR 0.74 and 0.56, respectively) and complete a vaccine course (RR 0.63 and 0.55, respectively), compared to those without intellectual disability. Reported barriers were primarily individual but also occurred at interpersonal, institutional or societal levels. The quantitative and qualitative studies were generally of high quality. Conclusions Girls and boys with an intellectual disability are less likely than those without intellectual disability to receive HPV vaccines, or complete a vaccine course once started, increasing cancer risk. Identified barriers and facilitators indicate opportunities in the healthcare and education sectors to intervene to reduce this inequity. Future research is needed from a wider range of countries, including data from people with intellectual disability themselves. Registration The protocol was registered with the OSF in September 2025: https://osf.io/7h8cz/overview

Meta-analyses showed that girls and boys with intellectual disability were less likely to receive the vaccine (RR 0.74 and 0.56, respectively) and complete a vaccine course (RR 0.63 and 0.55, respectively), compared to those without intellectual disability. Reported barriers were primarily individual but also occurred at interpersonal, institutional or societal levels. The quantitative and qualitative studies were generally of high quality. Conclusions Girls and boys with an intellectual disability are less likely than those without intellectual disability to receive HPV vaccines, or complete a vaccine course once started, increasing cancer risk. Identified barriers and facilitators indicate opportunities in the healthcare and education sectors to intervene to reduce this inequity. Future research is needed from a wider range of countries, including data from people with intellectual disability themselves. Registration The protocol was registered with the OSF in September 2025: https://osf.io/7h8cz/overview
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 宫颈癌 是第四种最常见的女性癌症,可通过 (人乳头瘤病毒) HPV 疫苗接种 进行预防,在大多数世界卫生组织国家,该病毒可用于青春期女孩和男孩。由于预防、筛查、早期 诊断 和 治疗 方面的缺陷,智力障碍人士的癌症结果明显比一般人群差,并且有人担心该人群中 HPV 疫苗接种 的感染率可能较低。目的是对智力障碍人群中 HPV 疫苗接种 的摄取及其对 疫苗接种 的影响进行系统回顾。方法 检索多个数据库(Medline;Embase;CINAHL;PsycINFO;Cochrane Central;Overton)至 2026 年 5 月。定量、定性和混合方法研究符合条件,如果:(i) 报告智力障碍人群中 HPV 疫苗接种 的摄取率,或 (ii) 报告影响智力障碍人群中 HPV 疫苗接种 的因素。两名评审员独立筛选研究并做出纳入决定。数据提取和质量评估(JBI 工具)由一名研究人员进行,并由另一名研究人员进行验证。酌情对 疫苗接种 启动率和完成率的数据进行叙述性综合和荟萃分析(风险比,RR);对 疫苗接种 的影响被映射到社会生态模型。结果 纳入来自八个高收入国家的 25 项研究(18 项定量;7 项定性)。荟萃分析显示,与无智力障碍的女孩和男孩相比,有智力障碍的女孩和男孩接受 疫苗(分别为 RR 0.74 和 0.56)并完成 疫苗 课程(分别为 RR 0.63 和 0.55)的可能性较小。报告的障碍主要是个人的,但也发生在人际、机构或社会层面。定量和定性研究总体上是高质量的。结论 与无智力障碍的女孩和男孩相比,患有智力障碍的女孩和男孩接受 HPV 疫苗 或一旦开始就完成 疫苗 课程的可能性较小,从而增加了癌症风险。已确定的障碍和促进因素表明医疗保健和教育部门有机会进行干预,以减少这种不平等。未来的研究需要来自更广泛的国家,包括来自智力障碍者本身的数据。注册 该协议于 2025 年 9 月在 OSF 注册:https://osf.io/7h8cz/overview

news.content: Part 2 of 4 Understanding Human Papillomavirus (HPV) Infection Symptoms By Ann Pietrangelo Updated on November 25, 2026 Medically reviewed by Renee Nilan, MD Add Us On Table of Contents View All Table of Contents HPV Infection Symptoms Common Symptoms HPV and Cervical Cancer Other Complications Prevention Next in HPV Guide How Human Papillomavirus (HPV) Is Diagnosed IN THIS GUIDE HPV Overview Symptoms CURRENT ARTICLE Diagnosis Treatment Key Takeaways HPV is a common sexually transmitted infection (STI) affecting about 40% of people aged 15 to 59 in the United States. Most HPV infections cause no health issues and clear up on their own within two years. In some cases, cancer is a risk. There is an effective HPV vaccine recommended for people between the ages of 9 and 26. Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a common STI that may not show symptoms but can cause significant health problems if persistent. Learn about the symptoms and how to protect yourself. Mypurgatoryyears / Getty Images Understanding HPV Infection Symptoms HPV often goes unnoticed because it usually doesn’t cause symptoms. The immune system typically clears the virus without issues. HPV includes over 200 viruses, and symptoms, if they appear, can include warts that might itch or cause discomfort. 1 HPV can infect cells in the skin and moist linings of the body, including areas in and around the: 2 Vulva , vagina, cervix Anus Inner foreskin and urethra of the penis Inner lining of the nose, mouth, and throat Windpipe and bronchi Inner eyelids HPV spreads through sexual contact . There’s currently no routine screening for HPV in men since there’s no approved test. 3 Women can get routine Pap testing to check for cervical changes, including early cervical cancer . HPV testing can take place along with your Pap test. There’s also an effective HPV vaccine generally recommended for people between the ages of 9 and 26. 4 Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a sexually transmitted infection (STI). In the United States, HPV affects about 40% of people aged 15-59. 5 It’s so common that just about all sexually active people get it at some point. 6 In as many as nine cases out of 10, HPV doesn’t cause health issues. And it usually clears up on its own within two years. But in cases where it doesn’t, it can lead to genital warts, cancer, and other health problems. 7 Common Symptoms of HPV Infection The most common thing is to have no symptoms at all. Certain low-risk HPV infections can cause a variety of warts . 8 Viral warts are benign , but they can be a nuisance. Warts often resolve on their own within one to five years. 9 Genital Warts This photo contains content that some people may find graphic or disturbing. Reproduced with permission from © DermNet and © Te Whatu Ora dermnetnz.org 2023. Genital warts can be small or large and raised or flat. They can be dome-shaped or resemble small cauliflowers. Genital warts can appear on the: 10 Vulva Vagina Cervix Penis Scrotum Anus Genital warts sometimes cause itching. Depending on their location, they can cause pain when you move your bowels or when you have sex. 10 Common Warts This photo contains content that some people may find graphic or disturbing. Dmitry Epov / Getty Images Common warts (verruca vulgaris) grow on the fingers, around the nails, and on the backs of the hands. The bumps are rough and may have black dots that look like seeds. They can range from the size of a pinhead to the size of a pea. 11 Plantar Warts This photo contains content that some people may find graphic or disturbing. Alena Ivochkina / Getty Images Plantar warts appear on the soles of the feet. They’re hard and can grow rather large. They sometimes have black dots and appear in clusters (mosaic warts). Since feet carry the weight of your whole body, plantar warts push inward instead of growing outward like other types of warts, which can cause tenderness and pain. 12 Flat Warts This photo contains content that some people may find graphic or disturbing. Reproduced with permission from © DermNet dermnetnz.org 2023. Flat warts are smooth, slightly raised, and small, usually just millimeters wide. These warts can grow anywhere but tend to appear on the face, especially the forehead and cheeks. Men may get these in the beard area, and women may get them on their legs. Flat warts typically appear in multiples. You can get 20 to 100 at a time. 11 HPV Infections and Cervical Cancer Some low-risk strains of HPV may lead to abnormal changes in the cells on the surface of the cervix (cervical dysplasia) that are not precancerous. 13 However, research suggests that HPV causes about 99% of all cases of cervical cancer . 14 Cervical cancer happens when the immune system can’t clear high-risk strains of HPV. Over time, these cells can turn precancerous , then cancerous. Routine Pap screening can allow healthcare providers to detect and remove precancerous cells before they become cancerous. And HPV vaccines can prevent the types of HPV most likely to cause cervical cancer. 1 Other Possible HPV Complications HPV types 16 and 18 cause most cancers related to HPV, including cancer of the cervix, vagina, vulva, penis, and anus. Some strains can also lead to cancer of the throat, tongue, and tonsils ( oropharyngeal cancer ). 13 Research suggests that HPV causes about 75% of vaginal cancers , 69% of vulvar cancers , 70% of oropharyngeal cancers, and 91% of anal cancers . 15 HPV is also associated with some benign proliferative (rapid-growth) and malignant (cancerous) lesions of the head and neck, the middle part of the throat (oropharynx), tonsils, and tongue. 16 A Word From Verywell Given the safety and efficacy of the HPV vaccine, it is important to consider vaccinating your children to protect them from developing certain cancers later in life. — RENEE NILAN, MD, MEDICAL EXPERT BOARD How to Prevent an HPV Infection HPV can be transmitted through skin-to-skin sexual contact as well as vaginal, oral, or anal sex. 9 Since there are so many types of HPV, you can get infected multiple times or get more than one strain at a time. HPV vaccines are highly effective in protecting against seven types of HPV that are most likely to cause cancer and two low-risk types that cause most genital warts. 1 Since vaccines became available, infections with types that cause most HPV genital warts and cancers dropped 88% among teen girls and 81% among adult women. 17 The best time to get vaccinated is around age 11 to 12, but catch-up vaccination is recommended up to age 26. 17 However, if you’re older than 26 and haven’t been vaccinated, you can speak with your healthcare provider about the potential benefits of getting vaccinated now. HPV vaccination won’t treat an existing infection, but it can still protect you against other HPV types. It’s less effective than the vaccine, but you can lower your risk of getting HPV by using a condom or dental dam during vaginal, oral, and anal sex. news.content_original: Part 2 of 4 Understanding Human Papillomavirus (HPV) Infection Symptoms By Ann Pietrangelo Updated on November 25, 2026 Medically reviewed by Renee Nilan, MD Add Us On Table of Contents View All Table of Contents HPV Infection Symptoms Common Symptoms HPV and Cervical Cancer Other Complications Prevention Next in HPV Guide How Human Papillomavirus (HPV) Is Diagnosed IN THIS GUIDE HPV Overview Symptoms CURRENT ARTICLE Diagnosis Treatment Key Takeaways HPV is a common sexually transmitted infection (STI) affecting about 40% of people aged 15 to 59 in the United States. Most HPV infections cause no health issues and clear up on their own within two years. In some cases, cancer is a risk. There is an effective HPV vaccine recommended for people between the ages of 9 and 26. Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a common STI that may not show symptoms but can cause significant health problems if persistent. Learn about the symptoms and how to protect yourself. Mypurgatoryyears / Getty Images Understanding HPV Infection Symptoms HPV often goes unnoticed because it usually doesn’t cause symptoms. The immune system typically clears the virus without issues. HPV includes over 200 viruses, and symptoms, if they appear, can include warts that might itch or cause discomfort. 1 HPV can infect cells in the skin and moist linings of the body, including areas in and around the: 2 Vulva , vagina, cervix Anus Inner foreskin and urethra of the penis Inner lining of the nose, mouth, and throat Windpipe and bronchi Inner eyelids HPV spreads through sexual contact . There’s currently no routine screening for HPV in men since there’s no approved test. 3 Women can get routine Pap testing to check for cervical changes, including early cervical cancer . HPV testing can take place along with your Pap test. There’s also an effective HPV vaccine generally recommended for people between the ages of 9 and 26. 4 Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a sexually transmitted infection (STI). In the United States, HPV affects about 40% of people aged 15-59. 5 It’s so common that just about all sexually active people get it at some point. 6 In as many as nine cases out of 10, HPV doesn’t cause health issues. And it usually clears up on its own within two years. But in cases where it doesn’t, it can lead to genital warts, cancer, and other health problems. 7 Common Symptoms of HPV Infection The most common thing is to have no symptoms at all. Certain low-risk HPV infections can cause a variety of warts . 8 Viral warts are benign , but they can be a nuisance. Warts often resolve on their own within one to five years. 9 Genital Warts This photo contains content that some people may find graphic or disturbing. Reproduced with permission from © DermNet and © Te Whatu Ora dermnetnz.org 2023. Genital warts can be small or large and raised or flat. They can be dome-shaped or resemble small cauliflowers. Genital warts can appear on the: 10 Vulva Vagina Cervix Penis Scrotum Anus Genital warts sometimes cause itching. Depending on their location, they can cause pain when you move your bowels or when you have sex. 10 Common Warts This photo contains content that some people may find graphic or disturbing. Dmitry Epov / Getty Images Common warts (verruca vulgaris) grow on the fingers, around the nails, and on the backs of the hands. The bumps are rough and may have black dots that look like seeds. They can range from the size of a pinhead to the size of a pea. 11 Plantar Warts This photo contains content that some people may find graphic or disturbing. Alena Ivochkina / Getty Images Plantar warts appear on the soles of the feet. They’re hard and can grow rather large. They sometimes have black dots and appear in clusters (mosaic warts). Since feet carry the weight of your whole body, plantar warts push inward instead of growing outward like other types of warts, which can cause tenderness and pain. 12 Flat Warts This photo contains content that some people may find graphic or disturbing. Reproduced with permission from © DermNet dermnetnz.org 2023. Flat warts are smooth, slightly raised, and small, usually just millimeters wide. These warts can grow anywhere but tend to appear on the face, especially the forehead and cheeks. Men may get these in the beard area, and women may get them on their legs. Flat warts typically appear in multiples. You can get 20 to 100 at a time. 11 HPV Infections and Cervical Cancer Some low-risk strains of HPV may lead to abnormal changes in the cells on the surface of the cervix (cervical dysplasia) that are not precancerous. 13 However, research suggests that HPV causes about 99% of all cases of cervical cancer . 14 Cervical cancer happens when the immune system can’t clear high-risk strains of HPV. Over time, these cells can turn precancerous , then cancerous. Routine Pap screening can allow healthcare providers to detect and remove precancerous cells before they become cancerous. And HPV vaccines can prevent the types of HPV most likely to cause cervical cancer. 1 Other Possible HPV Complications HPV types 16 and 18 cause most cancers related to HPV, including cancer of the cervix, vagina, vulva, penis, and anus. Some strains can also lead to cancer of the throat, tongue, and tonsils ( oropharyngeal cancer ). 13 Research suggests that HPV causes about 75% of vaginal cancers , 69% of vulvar cancers , 70% of oropharyngeal cancers, and 91% of anal cancers . 15 HPV is also associated with some benign proliferative (rapid-growth) and malignant (cancerous) lesions of the head and neck, the middle part of the throat (oropharynx), tonsils, and tongue. 16 A Word From Verywell Given the safety and efficacy of the HPV vaccine, it is important to consider vaccinating your children to protect them from developing certain cancers later in life. — RENEE NILAN, MD, MEDICAL EXPERT BOARD How to Prevent an HPV Infection HPV can be transmitted through skin-to-skin sexual contact as well as vaginal, oral, or anal sex. 9 Since there are so many types of HPV, you can get infected multiple times or get more than one strain at a time. HPV vaccines are highly effective in protecting against seven types of HPV that are most likely to cause cancer and two low-risk types that cause most genital warts. 1 Since vaccines became available, infections with types that cause most HPV genital warts and cancers dropped 88% among teen girls and 81% among adult women. 17 The best time to get vaccinated is around age 11 to 12, but catch-up vaccination is recommended up to age 26. 17 However, if you’re older than 26 and haven’t been vaccinated, you can speak with your healthcare provider about the potential benefits of getting vaccinated now. HPV vaccination won’t treat an existing infection, but it can still protect you against other HPV types. It’s less effective than the vaccine, but you can lower your risk of getting HPV by using a condom or dental dam during vaginal, oral, and anal sex. news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Saturday, November 28, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health One in Three Referred Iranian Women Tested Positive for Human Papillomavirus by November 25, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 4 mins read 0 One in Three Referred Iranian Women Tested Positive for Human Papillomavirus Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A retrospective cross-sectional analysis of 8,209 women referred for molecular testing in southern Iran found that approximately one in three tested positive for human papillomavirus, with high-risk viral strains detected in nearly twenty-nine percent of the cohort. Overall human papillomavirus positivity reached 34.2 percent, accompanied by a 95 percent confidence interval spanning from 33.2 percent to 35.3 percent. Infections classified as high-risk only accounted for 21.8 percent of the patient population, while low-risk strains alone were identified in 5.4 percent of participants. An additional 6.9 percent of the evaluated individuals harbored concurrent high-risk and low-risk infections. When combining the single high-risk and mixed categories, any high-risk human papillomavirus genotype was detected in 28.8 percent of the overall sample, with a 95 percent confidence interval ranging between 27.8 percent and 29.8 percent. The investigation evaluated medical records extracted from patients’ files at a specialized referral molecular laboratory located in Shiraz. The analyzed cohort comprised women aged 18 years and older who had been referred by physicians between the Iranian calendar years 1399 and 1403, a period corresponding approximately to March 2020 through March 2025. Specific clinical indications for each patient’s referral were not documented in the laboratory database. Deoxyribonucleic acid was extracted from collected clinical samples, and human papillomavirus genotyping was performed using commercial testing kits that varied across the multi-year study period. Because laboratory protocols and diagnostic assays changed over time, the specific panel of reported genotypes differed between individual calendar years, reflecting evolving diagnostic platforms. Discover more infections Infections infection To evaluate viral patterns systematically, researchers classified identified genotypes according to the International Agency for Research on Cancer framework, designating viral types belonging to Groups 1, 2A, and 2B as high-risk human papillomavirus, while all remaining genotypes were categorized as low-risk. Each tested participant was assigned to exactly one of four mutually exclusive diagnostic categories: human papillomavirus-negative, high-risk only, low-risk only, or mixed high-risk and low-risk infection. Multiple infection was formally defined as the presence of two or more distinct genotypes within a single patient sample. The analytical protocol utilized Pearson chi-square tests and linear-by-linear association to assess statistical relationships with patient age, establishing a rigorous framework for evaluating age-specific viral dynamics across the referral cohort. Discover more Support Causes Book a Checkup Read Med Journals Find Cancer Care Among individual viral types detected across the patient cohort, the low-risk genotype HPV6 emerged as the most frequent, identified in 6.0 percent of the evaluated women. The prominent oncogenic type HPV16 followed closely as the second most common strain, detected in 5.7 percent of the tested population. Beyond these two leading genotypes, several high-risk types outside the classic HPV16 and HPV18 classifications exhibited substantial prevalence across the cohort. Specifically, the non-16 and non-18 high-risk genotypes HPV53, HPV51, and HPV39 were identified in 3.4 percent to 4.2 percent of the studied women, underscoring the notable circulation of diverse oncogenic strains within this specialized clinical referral setting. Multiple infections were highly prevalent among viral carriers, occurring in 42.5 percent of human papillomavirus-positive individuals, representing 1,193 of the 2,809 infected women. Genotype positivity demonstrated a statistically significant downward trajectory with advancing age, declining from 50.5 percent among women aged 25 years or younger to 28.3 percent among those aged 46 years or older, yielding a Pearson chi-square statistic of 125.4 with three degrees of freedom and a significance level of P < 0.001. Multiple genotype infections were likewise most frequent among the youngest demographic, detected in 54.0 percent of positive women aged 25 or younger. Carrying multiple genotypes was strongly associated with harboring at least one high-risk strain, exhibiting an odds ratio of 10.0 with a 95 percent confidence interval from 7.1 to 14.0, a pattern the researchers noted is partly expected because individuals carrying multiple strains have greater cumulative opportunity for a high-risk type to be detected. Discover more Study Biology Check Symptoms Explore History Researchers evaluated co-detection patterns across 418 possible pairwise combinations of high-risk and low-risk genotypes, finding that 227 unique pairs were co-detected at least once within the dataset. Using descriptive Fisher’s exact tests applied to two-by-two contingency tables alongside age-stratified exact testing and Holm adjustment, 21 specific pairs occurred more frequently than expected by chance, with 10 of those pairs involving HPV6. However, none of these combinations remained statistically significant when the analysis was restricted exclusively to human papillomavirus-positive women. The authors emphasized that these co-detection metrics remain descriptive and do not demonstrate biological interaction between viral types. Annual positivity rates fluctuated across calendar years, ranging from 29.2 percent to 55.7 percent during years with at least 400 tested women, although restricted statistical estimates focusing on the final Iranian calendar years 1402 and 1403 yielded results comparable to the primary full-cohort findings. The authors emphasized critical epidemiological boundaries when interpreting the retrospective findings, noting that the study population consisted entirely of women referred by medical practitioners rather than a representative cross-section of the general community. Furthermore, the dataset lacked accompanying cytological examinations or histological tissue assessments, measuring viral infection rather than clinical disease or cervical neoplasia. Consequently, the observed genotype frequencies and positivity rates cannot be generalized to the broader Iranian population or utilized to guide individual clinical risk stratification.
