Nonmedical measles vaccine exemptions for kindergarteners tied to 16% higher risk of outbreaks News brief Mary Van Beusekom, MS Topics Measles Childhood Vaccines NIH Higher rates of nonmedical measles-vaccine exemptions for school entry were associated with a 16% higher outbreak likelihood in a study representing 237 million people in 30 US states. For the study, published yesterday in JAMA Network Open, a team led by a University of Washington researcher analyzed measles cases reported by the Johns Hopkins University Measles Tracker in 2025, state- and county-level data on measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine coverage among kindergarteners, and vaccine exemptions. The outbreak proxy was at least three measles cases per county, a count threshold rather than per-capita incidence; counties below that level were retained. The threshold didn’t establish epidemiologic linkage. The secondary outcome consisted of total county cases in counties with at least three cases rather than cases per outbreak. “Measles is among the most transmissible human pathogens, so even small, geographically clustered immunity gaps can sustain local transmission,” the authors wrote. “As aggregate national and state measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) coverage can obscure this local susceptibility, pockets of unvaccinated persons may persist even where aggregate coverage appears adequate.” Findings may guide school preparedness The analytic sample represented 71.6% of the US population, and 1,821 of 2,214 (82.2%) counties reported measles cases in 2025; 3.4% met the proxy. Average MMR coverage was 91.1%, and the average nonmedical exemption rate was 4.6%. Routinely collected exemption data may complement local knowledge when prioritizing school-level review and preparedness. The joint model showed a link between greater exemption rates and outbreak occurrence (odds ratio [OR], 1.16) but no association for MMR uptake (OR, 1.01). In the exploratory burden model, the incidence rate ratio was 1.08. Higher exemption rates were tied to lower MMR coverage. Joint-model ORs were 1.12 to 1.17 using alternative thresholds. Burden estimates remained positive but were less consistent in sensitivity analyses, with wide confidence intervals that indicated imprecision. The relationship between school nonmedical exemption rates and a higher likelihood of measles outbreaks may reflect clustering of susceptibility, differential measurement error in uptake and exemption data, or both, the authors said. “Routinely collected exemption data may complement local knowledge when prioritizing school-level review and preparedness,” they concluded. Point-of-care test for syphilis receives emergency use authorization News brief Chris Dall, MA Topics Sexually Transmitted Infections Diagnostics quantic69 / iStock The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued emergency use authorization for a point-of-care molecular test for active syphilis, and three other pathogens that cause sexually transmitted infections (STIs). The test, developed by Roche Diagnostics, can detect Treponema pallidum—the bacterium that causes syphilis—from a single lesion swab sample within 15 minutes. It can also detect mpox virus and herpes simplex virus types 1 and 2. The three STIs can cause similar symptoms but require different treatments. Officials with the National Institutes of Health (NIH), which helped speed the review of the test through its Rapid Acceleration of Diagnostics Tech Independent Test Assessment Program, say the point-of-care test can help healthcare providers identify active syphilis infection and initiate appropriate treatment more quickly. “Point-of-care testing leads to faster treatment in the same visit, thus reducing transmission and worsening illness,” Bruce Tromberg, PhD, director of NIH’s National Institute of Biomedical Imaging and Bioengineering, said in an agency press release. Rise in syphilis cases It’s the first point-of-care test for syphilis to receive FDA authorization. Current syphilis diagnosis relies on blood-based serologic tests. US syphilis cases have risen by 42% since 2020, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, with 190,242 cases reported in 2024. Cases of congenital syphilis—the transfer of the infection from the mother to the fetus—have risen by 82%. If left untreated, syphilis can cause serious heart and brain damage, blindness, deafness, and paralysis. Congenital syphilis can lead to miscarriage, infant death, and lifelong medical issues. NIH says the test will become available in the United States in the coming months. RSV shots safe for older adults, alone or in combo, analysis finds News brief Liz Szabo, MA Topics Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) Adult (non-flu) Vaccines lucigerma / iStock Multiple clinical trials have found that respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccines are safe in adults. Now, a new study in people age 60 and older shows it’s also safe to receive an RSV shot plus another vaccine in the same week. In a study of 18,252 people published this week in Vaccine, less than 1% of participants reported seeking medical attention during the week after being vaccinated against RSV. The study was based on reports to V-safe, a voluntary registry run by the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) that allows people to report side effects or other problems after receiving a vaccine. About one-third of people reported a mild or moderate health issue within a week after getting an RSV shot, including a sore arm, fatigue, muscle ache, and headache. About one in three people vaccinated against RSV received another vaccine within a week, according to the study, led by CDC scientists. Side effects differ by vaccine manufacturer People given the RSV vaccine made by Pfizer (Abrysvo) plus another shot were more likely to report side effects around the injection site compared with people who received the Pfizer shot alone. Study participants who received GSK’s RSV vaccine (Arexvy), either alone or with another vaccine, were more likely to report symptoms than those who received the Pfizer vaccine. Those who received the Moderna RSV vaccine (mResvia) had a similar risk of side effects as those given the Pfizer shot. The CDC recommends that people age 75 and older receive a single RSV shot. People older than 60 may also get an RSV vaccine if they are at high risk of developing severe disease from the illness. Uptick in H5N1 avian flu activity continues across North America News brief Stephanie Soucheray, MA Topics Avian Influenza (Bird Flu) Addison Berry/Flickr cc Avian flu activity continues to rise across the nation, with two more detections noted in dairy cattle herds this week, one each in Texas and Washington state. In the past 30 days, 26 cattle detections have been noted in dairy herds by the US Department of Agriculture’s Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS). Of the 26 detections, 17 have been in Washington state, with high activity in major dairy operations in the Yakima Valley. This week the World Health Organization detailed three human H5N1 cases reported in Yakima Valley in October and November, stating that all three patients were adults who worked on dairy cattle farms. No cases involved person-to-person transmission, and the report does not say if infected people all worked on the same farm. One of the case-patients (who had underlying health problems) died from the infection and was the first death reported globally following exposure to infected dairy cattle. The other two patients had mild illness, with conjunctivitis as an initial symptom. Zoo outbreak kills spider monkey, tigrillo In commercial poultry news, five new operations have reported H5N1 outbreaks this week, including a commercial broiler production in Sussex County, Delaware, affecting 269,900 birds. In the past 30 days, 4.02 million birds have been hit with avian flu in 32 US flocks, including 10 commercial and 22 backyard flocks, according to APHIS data. Finally in international news, Mexican health authorities announced the immediate closure of the Leon Municipal Zoo in the state of Guanajuato following an outbreak of H5N1. On November 16, the zoo noted the virus in dead migratory waterfowl found in the zoo’s central lake. Yesterday, testing showed H5N1 infection in two dead captive animals: a tigrillo (a small member of the cat family; see photo above) and a spider monkey, with a second spider monkey showing symptoms. The zoo is closed for the next five days. CWD digest: Fatal disease found on deer farms in Michigan, Kentucky News brief Mary Van Beusekom, MS Topics Chronic Wasting Disease Larry Smith / Flickr cc Michigan: The Michigan Department of Agriculture and Rural Development (MDARD) has confirmed the first-time detection of chronic wasting disease (CWD) in a cervid on a Roscommon County farm. While the type of cervid wasn’t identified in the news release, the farm raises game animals such as deer, elk, and reindeer, per media reports. Roscommon County, in the north-central part of Michigan’s Lower Peninsula, borders CWD-positive Ogemaw and Gladwin counties. “The presence of CWD in farmed cervid facilities is not new to Michigan; prior to this detection, cases have been found across multiple counties, including Calhoun, Hillsdale, Kent, Lake, Mackinac, Mecosta, Montcalm, Newaygo, and Osceola counties,” MDARD said. CWD is transmitted through infectious misfolded proteins called prions, which spread from animal to animal or through environmental contamination. Kentucky: A Shelby County deer farm is under quarantine after a deer tested positive for CWD last week—the first case in the county, the Kentucky Department of Agriculture reports. Shelby County is in the north-central part of the state and doesn’t border any CWD-positive county. “The Office of State Veterinarian established a management (5 mile radius) and surveillance (15 mile radius) zone for herds near the affected deer farm” and “is diligently reviewing recent movement records, and all deer farms in the management and surveillance zones are under restricted movement until further order of the State Veterinarian,” the news release said. analysis.time: The study was published in 2025, with the findings reported in a news release from Wiley, the publisher of the journal. The data analyzed reflects 2025 measles cases and vaccine coverage data.
analysis.location_and_population: The study focused on 30 US states, representing 71.6% of the US population and 1,821 of 2,214 counties. It involved 624 women with persistent HPV infection, 471 who cleared their HPV infection, and 75 with reactivated infection.
analysis.event: A study published in the journal Cancer found that higher HPV viral loads are associated with an increased risk of cervical cancer. The research tracked changes in viral load over time and linked them to the development of cervical lesions.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Among the 624 women with persistent HPV infection, 11% had low stable viral loads, 18% had moderate declining trajectories, 74% had moderately increasing viral loads, and 90% had persistently high viral loads, with the latter group showing the highest likelihood of developing precancerous cervical lesions.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study's findings suggest that monitoring viral load changes could improve cervical cancer prevention strategies. However, the authors note that the relationship between viral load and cervical cancer risk may be influenced by other factors, and the results are based on observational data rather than experimental methods.

analysis.brief_en: A study published in the journal Cancer found that higher HPV viral loads are linked to an increased risk of cervical cancer. The research, led by Dr. Lina Zhang and colleagues at Nanjing Medical University, tracked 624 women with persistent HPV infection, 471 who cleared it, and 75 with reactivated infection. Women with persistently high viral loads had a 90% likelihood of developing precancerous cervical lesions, compared to 11% with low stable loads and 18% with moderate declining trajectories. The findings highlight the importance of monitoring viral load changes over time to better assess future risk and improve surveillance strategies. However, the authors caution that other factors may also influence outcomes, and the study is observational rather than experimental. The results could lead to more personalized follow-up plans for cervical disease prevention.

news.content: EPAPER LIVE TV DAWNNEWS URDU Images Herald Aurora CityFM89 Advertise Events Supplements Careers Obituaries Dawn Epaper E-Paper | November 28, 2026 Dawn Epaper Home Latest Pakistan Opinion Business World Culture Prism Sport Magazines Tech Popular Archive Flood Donations Home Latest Pakistan Opinion Business World Culture Prism Sport Magazines Tech Popular Archive Flood Donations Search Search Page 29 · Metro - Peshawar Friday, 27 November 2026 82pc of KP’s targeted girls vaccinated against HPV By Ashfaq Yusufzai Newspaper Text A− A+ Email Story Your Name * Recipient Email * Send Email Cancel PESHAWAR: Health workers in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa have vaccinated more than 82pc of the targeted girls during the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination campaign, achieving the highest coverage in the country. The two-week exercise, meant to prevent cervical cancer, ended on Wednesday, with 2.281 million girls aged 9-14 vaccinated against a target of 2.843 million in the province, according to data released by the health department. A total of 4,040 teams, comprising 1,170 fixed, 2,553 outreach and 317 mobile ones, were deployed in the settled districts. Of the targeted girls, 620,978 remained unvaccinated. A total of 59.1pc girls were cases of refusal, 38.7pc were unavailable at home, while 2.2pc were ineligible for vaccination due to illness. Officials said the first phase of the country’s maiden HPV vaccination campaign was conducted in September last year in Punjab, Sindh, Islamabad and Azad Jammu and Kashmir. They said 9.6 million girls were vaccinated but none of the provinces or regions achieved the 90pc target. The World Health Organisation had asked KP and Balochistan authorities to step up public awareness ahead of the second phase, focusing on addressing weaknesses reported during the first phase. Sindh recorded the highest coverage at 68.6pc, while AJK reported the lowest at 39.2pc. In 12 designated districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, 501,182 girls were vaccinated against a target of 743,745, achieving 67.4pc coverage. The remaining districts collectively achieved 84.8pc coverage, with 1,780,421 girls receiving the vaccine. According to the data, 833,741 girls were vaccinated in schools, while 1,451,064 received the vaccine through community-based vaccination activities. District-level performance reflected encouraging progress across the province. Upper Chitral recorded the highest coverage at 115pc , followed by Buner at 108pc, Lower Dir at 99pc, Lower Chitral at 98pc and Swat and Malakand at 96pc each. Among the designated districts, Bajaur achieved 87pc coverage, Mohmand 81pc and Lakki Marwat 80pc. The drive, conducted in collaboration with the education department, WHO, Unicef and Gavi, also marked the introduction of the 13th vaccine into the Expanded Programme on Immunisation. An official news release said professional medical associations, teachers, school administrations, lady health workers, frontline health workers, religious leaders, community representatives and media partners played an important role in the successful implementation of the campaign. Concerns regarding vaccine safety, infertility, parental consent and the purpose of vaccination were addressed through evidence-based information, counselling and dialogue. Safety monitoring mechanisms remained in place throughout the campaign, and no serious adverse event following immunisation was recorded. To ensure that girls who missed vaccination during the campaign are also protected, HPV vaccination services will continue at fixed vaccination centres from Nov 25 to 30. Director General (Health Services) Dr Naeem Awan expressed gratitude to his counterpart at the Federal Directorate of Immunisation, relevant departments and partner organisations for their support in making the campaign successful. Meanwhile, Dr Ashfaq Utmanzay, president of Malgari Doctran, has called for an increase in the remuneration of first-level supervisors, who served as medical officers in basic health units and performed duties from 9am to 4pm in remote areas during the campaign. He said the supervisors conducted rapid convenience assessments, maintained the cold chain, monitored team performance and resolved field issues on the spot but the compensation provided for travel, fuel, vehicle maintenance and food was less than their actual expenses. analysis.brief_en: CIDRAP reported on a study linking higher human papillomavirus (HPV) viral loads to an increased risk of cervical cancer. The study highlights the potential correlation between the amount of HPV present in the body and the likelihood of developing cervical cancer. However, no specific case counts, death rates, or detailed prevention measures are provided in the evidence. The report serves as a research implication rather than a confirmed outbreak or event. The findings are part of a broader discussion on HPV-related diseases and the importance of understanding viral load impacts on health outcomes. This information underscores the need for further research and targeted public health strategies to address HPV-associated risks, particularly in cervical cancer prevention.

news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Saturday, November 28, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Biology Cervicovaginal Microbiota Interventions Increase HPV Clearance and Cervical Lesion Regression by November 27, 2026 in Biology Reading Time: 7 mins read 0 Cervicovaginal Microbiota Interventions Increase HPV Clearance and Cervical Lesion Regression Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A comprehensive systematic review and meta-analysis published in Frontiers in Microbiomes reveals that clinical interventions designed to restore a balanced cervicovaginal microenvironment significantly accelerate human papillomavirus clearance and promote the regression of cervical cellular abnormalities. Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus strains represents the established primary cause of more than ninety-five percent of all cervical cancers worldwide. Although approximately seventy-one percent of high-risk viral infections resolve spontaneously through natural host defenses, a critical subset establishes viral persistence that can drive malignant cellular transformation. However, only two to five percent of individuals with persistent infections eventually progress to high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions or invasive carcinomas. This notable discrepancy demonstrates that viral exposure alone remains insufficient to trigger malignancy and confirms that secondary biological cofactors are required. A research team led by Larissa A. de Ridder from Radboud University Medical Centre systematically evaluated sixteen human intervention trials to determine whether modulating the cervicovaginal ecosystem enhances viral elimination and reverses early preneoplastic tissue changes. The cervicovaginal microenvironment plays a decisive role in modulating host susceptibility, local inflammation, and viral trajectory. In healthy individuals, the vaginal niche is typically dominated by beneficial Lactobacillus species, specifically within community state types classified as CST I, II, III, and V, which correspond to dominance by Lactobacillus crispatus, Lactobacillus gasseri, Lactobacillus iners, and Lactobacillus jensenii, respectively. These commensal bacteria convert host glycogen into lactic acid, maintaining an acidic biochemical barrier with a low pH that directly inhibits opportunistic pathobionts while manufacturing antimicrobial bacteriocins. Lactic acid additionally reinforces epithelial integrity by upregulating essential tight junction proteins and suppresses local inflammation through the downregulation of nuclear factor kappa-light chain enhancer of activated B cells, commonly known as NF-κB, which suppresses inflammatory cytokine production including interleukin-6 and tumour necrosis factor alpha. In contrast, dysbiotic states such as bacterial vaginosis, characterized by community state type IV, involve the depletion of protective lactobacilli and the rampant overgrowth of diverse anaerobic taxa such as Gardnerella, Fannyhessea, Prevotella, and Sneathia. This anaerobic state compromises epithelial integrity, induces mucosal inflammation, impairs antiviral defenses, and facilitates persistent viral oncogenesis. To investigate the clinical efficacy of therapies targeting this ecological interface, the investigators conducted a systematic search across PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library for human trials published from January 2000 through September 2025. Registered prospectively in the PROSPERO database under identifier CRD420251104055 and executed according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines, the review screened 2,307 bibliographic citations before identifying sixteen eligible studies encompassing 2,490 female participants aged eighteen years and older with confirmed papillomavirus infections. The final evidence corpus comprised eight randomized controlled trials alongside eight non-randomized designs, including controlled clinical trials, prospective and retrospective cohort investigations, case-control analyses, and open single-arm pilot studies conducted across European and Asian medical centers. Across these protocols, eleven trials evaluated probiotic regimens utilizing defined live bacterial strains such as oral or vaginal Lactobacillus crispatus, Lactobacillus rhamnosus, Lactobacillus reuteri, and Lactobacillus plantarum, whereas five investigations evaluated non-probiotic microenvironment-modulating formulations, including carboxy-methyl beta-glucan gels, polycarbophil preparations, Coriolus versicolor extracts, and traditional herbal formulations like Jiawei Ermiao Granules. Discover more Engineering Job Board Research Paper Access Learn Engineering Track Biotech Tour Colleges Quantitative evidence synthesis demonstrated a statistically significant advantage for patients receiving microenvironment-targeted interventions over control cohorts. A random-effects Mantel-Haenszel meta-analysis pooling eleven controlled studies encompassing 1,588 participants established that targeted interventions significantly improved papillomavirus clearance, generating a pooled risk ratio of 1.39 with a 95% confidence interval ranging from 1.16 to 1.66. Substantial statistical heterogeneity was observed across these eleven datasets, reflected by an I-squared value of 63 percent, which the authors attributed to substantial variability in baseline patient populations, follow-up durations ranging from twelve weeks to fourteen months, and differing viral detection methodologies. Two included trials had examined probiotic interventions administered as adjunctive co-therapy alongside recombinant human interferon alpha-2b. To determine whether concurrent antiviral medication skewed the aggregate outcome, the researchers performed a planned sensitivity analysis excluding those two trials. The resulting pooled risk ratio remained stable and statistically significant at 1.40 with a 95% confidence interval of 1.11 to 1.77 and an I-squared value of 67 percent, confirming that the observed viral clearance effect was not driven by concomitant interferon pharmacotherapy. The meta-analysis revealed an even more uniform therapeutic effect regarding the regression of cervical cellular abnormalities. Pooling six controlled clinical studies comprising 1,152 participants that recorded standardized negative follow-up cytology demonstrated that microecological interventions increased the likelihood of cytological regression by fifty-seven percent compared with control interventions, yielding a risk ratio of 1.57 with a 95% confidence interval of 1.38 to 1.78. Remarkably, statistical heterogeneity across these six studies was entirely absent, characterized by an I-squared value of zero percent. Across the individual studies evaluated, baseline cytological presentations primarily encompassed atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance, known as ASCUS, and low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions, known as LSIL, alongside histologically verified cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 1 lesions. Interventions consistently accelerated cytological normalization back to findings negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy, known as NILM. In specific trials, such as evaluations of the polycarbophil and beta-glucan gel Colpofix, therapeutic application achieved a 48.9 percent cytological normalization rate compared with 31.9 percent in untreated controls, accompanied by significant reductions in colposcopic anomalies and histological lesion persistence. Exploratory subgroup analyses were conducted across multiple clinical and pharmacological parameters to identify key drivers of treatment response and isolate sources of statistical heterogeneity. When stratified by administration route, vaginal interventions evaluated across six controlled studies comprising 976 participants yielded a statistically significant increase in viral clearance, producing a risk ratio of 1.49 with a 95% confidence interval of 1.21 to 1.84. In comparison, oral formulations evaluated across five studies involving 612 patients produced a more modest, non-significant risk ratio of 1.15 with a 95% confidence interval of 0.94 to 1.41. Although vaginal delivery achieved numerically superior viral eradication, the statistical test for subgroup differences did not achieve significance at a p-value of 0.08, and vaginal trials retained moderate internal heterogeneity with an I-squared of 61 percent. Conversely, when examining cytological regression, both administration pathways produced robust and comparable therapeutic gains: oral delivery generated a risk ratio of 1.42 with an I-squared of zero percent, while local vaginal administration generated a risk ratio of 1.61 with an I-squared of 6.8 percent, without significant divergence between routes. Subgroup analyses contrasting intervention categories further confirmed that therapeutic benefits were not restricted to living bacterial cultures. When classified by therapeutic mechanism, probiotic agents demonstrated a pooled risk ratio of 1.26 with a 95% confidence interval of 1.07 to 1.49 for viral clearance across seven controlled trials, while non-probiotic microenvironmental agents achieved a pooled risk ratio of 1.64 with a 95% confidence interval of 1.08 to 2.50 across four trials, with no statistically significant variance between classes at a p-value of 0.25. Regarding cytological regression, probiotic formulations yielded a risk ratio of 1.58, mirroring the 1.56 risk ratio achieved by non-probiotic agents. Among specific microbial strains, preparations containing Lactobacillus crispatus, such as the oral Crispact formulation containing strain M247, demonstrated a pooled clearance risk ratio of 1.50 with an I-squared of zero percent, whereas other probiotic preparations demonstrated a pooled risk ratio of 1.22. However, the comparative difference between bacterial strains did not achieve statistical significance at a p-value of 0.33, preventing the authors from declaring strain superiority. Ten of the included trials integrated microbiological and molecular profiling to assess whether observed clinical recoveries were accompanied by objective restructuring of the cervicovaginal microecology. Conventional microbiological assessments across these investigations documented marked therapeutic improvements, characterized by significant reductions in standardized Nugent scores, normalization of vaginal pH toward healthy acidic thresholds at or below 4.5, and decreased enzymatic activities of sialidase, catalase, and leukocyte esterase, which serve as classical biochemical surrogates of bacterial vaginosis and local mucosal inflammation. Advanced sequencing technologies, including 16S ribosomal RNA gene sequencing, internal transcribed spacer sequencing, and shotgun metagenomic profiling, confirmed pronounced taxonomic restructuring. Interventions stimulated dramatic expansions in relative Lactobacillus abundance while suppressing pathogenic anaerobic genera such as Gardnerella, Prevotella, and Sneathia. Multiple trials documented distinct ecological conversions wherein dysbiotic community state type IV profiles converted into protective, Lactobacillus crispatus-dominated community state type I structures, which were accompanied by significant decreases in microbial alpha diversity and prominent compositional shifts across multivariate beta diversity analyses. Despite these encouraging quantitative outcomes, the authors emphasized critical methodological limitations that necessitate cautious clinical interpretation. Risk of bias assessments conducted using the Cochrane RoB 2 framework judged all eight randomized controlled trials to possess some concerns, predominantly arising from inadequate documentation of randomization sequence generation, insufficient blinding protocols, or potential selective outcome reporting. Non-randomized studies evaluated with the ROBINS-I instrument exhibited moderate to critical risks of bias linked to unadjusted confounding factors, non-consecutive participant selection, and absent concurrent control cohorts. Applying the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation system, the authors rated the overall certainty of evidence as low for human papillomavirus clearance due to serious risk of bias and unexplained statistical inconsistency, and moderate for the regression of cervical abnormalities due to risk of bias limitations. Furthermore, substantial clinical heterogeneity in baseline diagnostic definitions, variable follow-up schedules, and diverse diagnostic criteria prevented the mathematical application of reliable funnel plot analyses to formally evaluate potential publication bias. The study authors underlined that all reviewed clinical trials relied exclusively on surrogate primary endpoints—specifically viral genome clearance and early cytological normalization—rather than definitive oncology outcomes. None of the sixteen trials evaluated high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions, histologically confirmed cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or higher, or the primary prevention of invasive cervical carcinoma. In addition, the vast majority of studies enrolled women presenting with pre-existing low-grade lesions where spontaneous physiological regression occurs naturally at high rates, and relied upon standard viral DNA amplification assays that cannot distinguish between self-limiting transient surface contamination and transcriptionally active viral integration. The researchers also noted that baseline dysbiosis was rarely confirmed objectively prior to study enrollment, meaning observed benefits reflect general microenvironmental modulation rather than the isolated correction of documented bacterial vaginosis. Consequently, the research team concluded that while current evidence demonstrates a clear, statistically robust association between cervicovaginal microenvironment optimization, accelerated viral clearance, and early lesion regression, these findings remain hypothesis-generating until validated by rigorous, adequately powered randomized controlled trials measuring standardized histological endpoints. news.content_original: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Saturday, November 28, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Biology Cervicovaginal Microbiota Interventions Increase HPV Clearance and Cervical Lesion Regression by November 27, 2026 in Biology Reading Time: 7 mins read 0 Cervicovaginal Microbiota Interventions Increase HPV Clearance and Cervical Lesion Regression Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A comprehensive systematic review and meta-analysis published in Frontiers in Microbiomes reveals that clinical interventions designed to restore a balanced cervicovaginal microenvironment significantly accelerate human papillomavirus clearance and promote the regression of cervical cellular abnormalities. Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus strains represents the established primary cause of more than ninety-five percent of all cervical cancers worldwide. Although approximately seventy-one percent of high-risk viral infections resolve spontaneously through natural host defenses, a critical subset establishes viral persistence that can drive malignant cellular transformation. However, only two to five percent of individuals with persistent infections eventually progress to high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions or invasive carcinomas. This notable discrepancy demonstrates that viral exposure alone remains insufficient to trigger malignancy and confirms that secondary biological cofactors are required. A research team led by Larissa A. de Ridder from Radboud University Medical Centre systematically evaluated sixteen human intervention trials to determine whether modulating the cervicovaginal ecosystem enhances viral elimination and reverses early preneoplastic tissue changes. The cervicovaginal microenvironment plays a decisive role in modulating host susceptibility, local inflammation, and viral trajectory. In healthy individuals, the vaginal niche is typically dominated by beneficial Lactobacillus species, specifically within community state types classified as CST I, II, III, and V, which correspond to dominance by Lactobacillus crispatus, Lactobacillus gasseri, Lactobacillus iners, and Lactobacillus jensenii, respectively. These commensal bacteria convert host glycogen into lactic acid, maintaining an acidic biochemical barrier with a low pH that directly inhibits opportunistic pathobionts while manufacturing antimicrobial bacteriocins. Lactic acid additionally reinforces epithelial integrity by upregulating essential tight junction proteins and suppresses local inflammation through the downregulation of nuclear factor kappa-light chain enhancer of activated B cells, commonly known as NF-κB, which suppresses inflammatory cytokine production including interleukin-6 and tumour necrosis factor alpha. In contrast, dysbiotic states such as bacterial vaginosis, characterized by community state type IV, involve the depletion of protective lactobacilli and the rampant overgrowth of diverse anaerobic taxa such as Gardnerella, Fannyhessea, Prevotella, and Sneathia. This anaerobic state compromises epithelial integrity, induces mucosal inflammation, impairs antiviral defenses, and facilitates persistent viral oncogenesis. To investigate the clinical efficacy of therapies targeting this ecological interface, the investigators conducted a systematic search across PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library for human trials published from January 2000 through September 2025. Registered prospectively in the PROSPERO database under identifier CRD420251104055 and executed according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines, the review screened 2,307 bibliographic citations before identifying sixteen eligible studies encompassing 2,490 female participants aged eighteen years and older with confirmed papillomavirus infections. The final evidence corpus comprised eight randomized controlled trials alongside eight non-randomized designs, including controlled clinical trials, prospective and retrospective cohort investigations, case-control analyses, and open single-arm pilot studies conducted across European and Asian medical centers. Across these protocols, eleven trials evaluated probiotic regimens utilizing defined live bacterial strains such as oral or vaginal Lactobacillus crispatus, Lactobacillus rhamnosus, Lactobacillus reuteri, and Lactobacillus plantarum, whereas five investigations evaluated non-probiotic microenvironment-modulating formulations, including carboxy-methyl beta-glucan gels, polycarbophil preparations, Coriolus versicolor extracts, and traditional herbal formulations like Jiawei Ermiao Granules. Discover more Engineering Job Board Research Paper Access Learn Engineering Track Biotech Tour Colleges Quantitative evidence synthesis demonstrated a statistically significant advantage for patients receiving microenvironment-targeted interventions over control cohorts. A random-effects Mantel-Haenszel meta-analysis pooling eleven controlled studies encompassing 1,588 participants established that targeted interventions significantly improved papillomavirus clearance, generating a pooled risk ratio of 1.39 with a 95% confidence interval ranging from 1.16 to 1.66. Substantial statistical heterogeneity was observed across these eleven datasets, reflected by an I-squared value of 63 percent, which the authors attributed to substantial variability in baseline patient populations, follow-up durations ranging from twelve weeks to fourteen months, and differing viral detection methodologies. Two included trials had examined probiotic interventions administered as adjunctive co-therapy alongside recombinant human interferon alpha-2b. To determine whether concurrent antiviral medication skewed the aggregate outcome, the researchers performed a planned sensitivity analysis excluding those two trials. The resulting pooled risk ratio remained stable and statistically significant at 1.40 with a 95% confidence interval of 1.11 to 1.77 and an I-squared value of 67 percent, confirming that the observed viral clearance effect was not driven by concomitant interferon pharmacotherapy. The meta-analysis revealed an even more uniform therapeutic effect regarding the regression of cervical cellular abnormalities. Pooling six controlled clinical studies comprising 1,152 participants that recorded standardized negative follow-up cytology demonstrated that microecological interventions increased the likelihood of cytological regression by fifty-seven percent compared with control interventions, yielding a risk ratio of 1.57 with a 95% confidence interval of 1.38 to 1.78. Remarkably, statistical heterogeneity across these six studies was entirely absent, characterized by an I-squared value of zero percent. Across the individual studies evaluated, baseline cytological presentations primarily encompassed atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance, known as ASCUS, and low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions, known as LSIL, alongside histologically verified cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 1 lesions. Interventions consistently accelerated cytological normalization back to findings negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy, known as NILM. In specific trials, such as evaluations of the polycarbophil and beta-glucan gel Colpofix, therapeutic application achieved a 48.9 percent cytological normalization rate compared with 31.9 percent in untreated controls, accompanied by significant reductions in colposcopic anomalies and histological lesion persistence. Exploratory subgroup analyses were conducted across multiple clinical and pharmacological parameters to identify key drivers of treatment response and isolate sources of statistical heterogeneity. When stratified by administration route, vaginal interventions evaluated across six controlled studies comprising 976 participants yielded a statistically significant increase in viral clearance, producing a risk ratio of 1.49 with a 95% confidence interval of 1.21 to 1.84. In comparison, oral formulations evaluated across five studies involving 612 patients produced a more modest, non-significant risk ratio of 1.15 with a 95% confidence interval of 0.94 to 1.41. Although vaginal delivery achieved numerically superior viral eradication, the statistical test for subgroup differences did not achieve significance at a p-value of 0.08, and vaginal trials retained moderate internal heterogeneity with an I-squared of 61 percent. Conversely, when examining cytological regression, both administration pathways produced robust and comparable therapeutic gains: oral delivery generated a risk ratio of 1.42 with an I-squared of zero percent, while local vaginal administration generated a risk ratio of 1.61 with an I-squared of 6.8 percent, without significant divergence between routes. Subgroup analyses contrasting intervention categories further confirmed that therapeutic benefits were not restricted to living bacterial cultures. When classified by therapeutic mechanism, probiotic agents demonstrated a pooled risk ratio of 1.26 with a 95% confidence interval of 1.07 to 1.49 for viral clearance across seven controlled trials, while non-probiotic microenvironmental agents achieved a pooled risk ratio of 1.64 with a 95% confidence interval of 1.08 to 2.50 across four trials, with no statistically significant variance between classes at a p-value of 0.25. Regarding cytological regression, probiotic formulations yielded a risk ratio of 1.58, mirroring the 1.56 risk ratio achieved by non-probiotic agents. Among specific microbial strains, preparations containing Lactobacillus crispatus, such as the oral Crispact formulation containing strain M247, demonstrated a pooled clearance risk ratio of 1.50 with an I-squared of zero percent, whereas other probiotic preparations demonstrated a pooled risk ratio of 1.22. However, the comparative difference between bacterial strains did not achieve statistical significance at a p-value of 0.33, preventing the authors from declaring strain superiority. Ten of the included trials integrated microbiological and molecular profiling to assess whether observed clinical recoveries were accompanied by objective restructuring of the cervicovaginal microecology. Conventional microbiological assessments across these investigations documented marked therapeutic improvements, characterized by significant reductions in standardized Nugent scores, normalization of vaginal pH toward healthy acidic thresholds at or below 4.5, and decreased enzymatic activities of sialidase, catalase, and leukocyte esterase, which serve as classical biochemical surrogates of bacterial vaginosis and local mucosal inflammation. Advanced sequencing technologies, including 16S ribosomal RNA gene sequencing, internal transcribed spacer sequencing, and shotgun metagenomic profiling, confirmed pronounced taxonomic restructuring. Interventions stimulated dramatic expansions in relative Lactobacillus abundance while suppressing pathogenic anaerobic genera such as Gardnerella, Prevotella, and Sneathia. Multiple trials documented distinct ecological conversions wherein dysbiotic community state type IV profiles converted into protective, Lactobacillus crispatus-dominated community state type I structures, which were accompanied by significant decreases in microbial alpha diversity and prominent compositional shifts across multivariate beta diversity analyses. Despite these encouraging quantitative outcomes, the authors emphasized critical methodological limitations that necessitate cautious clinical interpretation. Risk of bias assessments conducted using the Cochrane RoB 2 framework judged all eight randomized controlled trials to possess some concerns, predominantly arising from inadequate documentation of randomization sequence generation, insufficient blinding protocols, or potential selective outcome reporting. Non-randomized studies evaluated with the ROBINS-I instrument exhibited moderate to critical risks of bias linked to unadjusted confounding factors, non-consecutive participant selection, and absent concurrent control cohorts. Applying the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation system, the authors rated the overall certainty of evidence as low for human papillomavirus clearance due to serious risk of bias and unexplained statistical inconsistency, and moderate for the regression of cervical abnormalities due to risk of bias limitations. Furthermore, substantial clinical heterogeneity in baseline diagnostic definitions, variable follow-up schedules, and diverse diagnostic criteria prevented the mathematical application of reliable funnel plot analyses to formally evaluate potential publication bias. The study authors underlined that all reviewed clinical trials relied exclusively on surrogate primary endpoints—specifically viral genome clearance and early cytological normalization—rather than definitive oncology outcomes. None of the sixteen trials evaluated high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions, histologically confirmed cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or higher, or the primary prevention of invasive cervical carcinoma. In addition, the vast majority of studies enrolled women presenting with pre-existing low-grade lesions where spontaneous physiological regression occurs naturally at high rates, and relied upon standard viral DNA amplification assays that cannot distinguish between self-limiting transient surface contamination and transcriptionally active viral integration. The researchers also noted that baseline dysbiosis was rarely confirmed objectively prior to study enrollment, meaning observed benefits reflect general microenvironmental modulation rather than the isolated correction of documented bacterial vaginosis. Consequently, the research team concluded that while current evidence demonstrates a clear, statistically robust association between cervicovaginal microenvironment optimization, accelerated viral clearance, and early lesion regression, these findings remain hypothesis-generating until validated by rigorous, adequately powered randomized controlled trials measuring standardized histological endpoints. news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Saturday, November 28, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Vaginal Microbiome Imbalance Associates With Cervical Dysplasia and HPV in Togolese Women by November 26, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Vaginal Microbiome Imbalance Associates With Cervical Dysplasia and HPV in Togolese Women Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram In a community-based cervical cancer screening study conducted in Lomé, Togo, researchers identified significant associations linking vaginal microbial dysbiosis with high-risk human papillomavirus infection and cervical dysplasia among asymptomatic adult women. Evaluating a screening cohort of 338 women, investigators observed an overall high-risk human papillomavirus prevalence of 31.33 percent and detected cytological cervical epithelial abnormalities in 10.06 percent of participants. Women presenting with high-risk viral infections exhibited significantly elevated Nugent scores compared to uninfected participants, reflecting a marked phenotypic disturbance in baseline vaginal bacterial composition. A parallel elevation in Nugent scores was documented among individuals diagnosed with cervical dysplasia compared to those showing normal cytology. Rather than identifying a single infectious etiology, subsequent molecular analyses demonstrated that these clinical outcomes were characterized by a structural depletion of protective Lactobacillus species and a concurrent expansion of diverse polymicrobial anaerobic consortia, providing novel insights into mucosal cofactors within sub-Saharan Africa. Cervical cancer represents a severe public health crisis in sub-Saharan Africa, where limited screening infrastructure and constrained access to clinical interventions drive elevated morbidity and mortality rates. In Togo, cervical malignancy is the second most frequent cancer among female populations, responsible for an estimated age-standardized incidence of roughly 21.5 cases per 100,000 women and generating more than 400 annual deaths. While persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus genotypes is widely established as the primary causal driver of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia and invasive carcinoma, viral presence alone does not invariably lead to malignant progression. The vast majority of acquired viral infections are successfully cleared by host immune mechanisms within one to two years without causing persistent epithelial damage. Emerging scientific evidence has increasingly highlighted the cervicovaginal microenvironment, particularly mucosal microbial equilibrium, as an influential biological cofactor modulating viral persistence, local tissue inflammation, and early neoplastic transformation. However, mucosal microbiome research has historically remained skewed toward cohorts in industrialized nations, leaving microbial profiles among West African women largely uncharacterized prior to this community investigation. To investigate cervicovaginal microbial features associated with viral carriage and cervical abnormalities, investigators recruited sexually active, non-pregnant adult women aged 18 years or older through social media announcements and radio broadcasts in Lomé. Participants reported to the Association Togolaise pour le Bien-être Familial clinic for comprehensive cervical screening. Study eligibility required participants to be asymptomatic, in good general health, and without prior histories of cervical cancer, precancerous treatments, loop electrosurgical excision procedures, conization, or adnexectomy. To eliminate confounding biological exposures, the protocol excluded women who were actively menstruating, had engaged in sexual intercourse within the preceding three days, had received human papillomavirus vaccination, were currently receiving antibiotics or had taken them within three months, or presented known immune deficiencies. A total of 428 women completed structured face-to-face interviews documenting sociodemographic characteristics, reproductive histories, and lifestyle habits. Following these initial evaluations, 338 participants completed pelvic examinations, provided cervical samples for high-risk viral detection and Papanicolaou cytological assessment, and contributed vaginal swab specimens for standardized Nugent scoring. Discover more Track Fertility See an OB-GYN Find Cancer Care Find an OBGYN Study Anatomy Clinical evaluations integrated cytological assessment, phenotypic bacterial vaginosis grading, and molecular viral genotyping to characterize each participant. Conventional cervical cytology smears were stained according to the Papanicolaou protocol using automated instrumentation and independently reviewed by three pathologists using the Bethesda 2014 classification system. Smears were categorized as negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy, atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance, atypical squamous cells that cannot exclude high-grade lesions, low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions, or high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions. Concurrently, vaginal smears were Gram-stained to calculate Nugent scores from 0 to 10 based on relative morphotype counts of large Gram-positive rods, small Gram-negative rods, and curved bacilli. Genomic DNA was extracted from swab specimens using column-based purification kits. High-risk viral genotyping was executed utilizing the Anyplex II HPV HR Detection assay on a Bio-Rad CFX96 real-time PCR platform. This multiplex real-time polymerase chain reaction assay simultaneously amplified the L1 region across 14 high-risk viral genotypes alongside human beta-globin control genes, applying melting curve analysis across defined cycle thresholds to determine semi-quantitative viral load levels. Genotyping across the 338 screened participants revealed a diverse landscape of oncogenic viral types, led predominantly by HPV16, which accounted for 35.33 percent of all detected high-risk infections. The second most prevalent genotype was HPV51 at 14.66 percent, followed by HPV35 at 9.33 percent, HPV52 at 8.90 percent, HPV56 at 8.66 percent, and HPV58 at 7.33 percent. Genotypes HPV18 and HPV59 each represented 6.66 percent of infections, while HPV31, HPV66, HPV45, and HPV39 accounted for 3.66 percent, 2.66 percent, 1.94 percent, and 1.33 percent, respectively. Cytological examinations demonstrated that 10.06 percent of the screened cohort harbored cervical squamous abnormalities, including low-grade intraepithelial lesions, atypical squamous cells, and high-grade intraepithelial lesions, alongside pervasive evidence of local tissue inflammation. Women presenting cervical dysplasia were significantly older on average than those with negative cytology, whereas parity, age at sexual debut, and lifetime partner counts showed no statistically significant differences between groups. Multivariable logistic regression confirmed that high-risk viral carriage, early sexual debut, and higher parity served as independent predictive variables associated with elevated Nugent-defined vaginal dysbiosis. For deep molecular characterization of the mucosal ecosystem, a subset of 150 satisfactory vaginal DNA specimens fulfilling rigorous cellularity and purity thresholds underwent high-throughput 16S ribosomal RNA gene sequencing. Amplicons spanning the hypervariable V3-V4 region were generated using universal 319F and 806R primers, purified with magnetic beads, indexed through dual-indexing adapters, and sequenced on an Illumina MiSeq platform utilizing paired-end 300-base-pair reads. Raw sequence data were processed through the DADA2 pipeline in the R software environment for quality filtering, read denoising, paired-end merging, and chimera removal, yielding 5,110 unique amplicon sequence variants across 148 fully analyzed samples at an average read depth of 23,810 reads per library. Taxonomic classification was executed using the Ribosomal Database Project classifier matched against SILVA reference databases, supplemented by high-resolution secondary BLASTn alignments against the NCBI RefSeq 16S ribosomal RNA database requiring at least 99 percent sequence identity and 98 percent query coverage to assign putative species-level classifications conservatively. Rarefaction analysis demonstrated complete sequencing saturation, with Rarefaction Saturation Index values reaching 99.99 percent across all clinical subgroups, confirming that observed community metrics were not biased by uneven sequencing depth. Alpha diversity evaluations evaluating Chao1 richness, Shannon diversity, and Simpson evenness demonstrated no statistically significant differences between high-risk viral-positive and viral-negative women, nor between dysplastic and normal cytology groups. Specifically, mean Shannon diversity remained virtually indistinguishable between viral-positive women and uninfected controls at 3.68 and 3.67, respectively. Global beta diversity evaluated through Principal Coordinate Analysis of Bray-Curtis dissimilarity matrices revealed that viral infection status did not induce significant community restructuring across global coordinate planes. Similarly, Permutational Multivariate Analysis of Variance indicated that cervical dysplasia displayed only a modest, non-significant divergence trend, while community ecological volatility assessments remained statistically comparable across groups. These findings demonstrated that viral carriage and early cytological lesions do not cause complete wholesale ecological collapses, but instead correspond to selective compositional substitutions within an otherwise globally intact vaginal ecosystem. Despite stable global community metrics, fine-scale differential abundance analyses using negative binomial generalized linear models in DESeq2 revealed profound compositional rearrangements. Healthy, lesion-negative women exhibited vaginal microbiomes dominated by Firmicutes and protective Lactobacillus species. In contrast, participants carrying high-risk human papillomavirus or presenting cervical dysplasia demonstrated an extensive depletion of lactobacilli accompanied by substantial enrichment of opportunistic and strict anaerobic bacteria. Enriched taxa included Atopobium vaginae, Fannyhessea vaginae, Sneathia sanguinegens, Peptostreptococcus anaerobius, Peptoniphilus faecalis, and multiple Prevotella species. Stratified validation analyses restricted strictly to confirmed low-grade and high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions while excluding indeterminate atypical cytological classifications confirmed that these anaerobic signatures remained significantly elevated, exhibiting log2 fold changes exceeding 2.5. Concurrently, protective Lactobacillus crispatus and Lactobacillus mulieris species remained significantly depleted in confirmed dysplasia cases. High-resolution heatmaps confirmed that dysplasia was linked to the coordinated expansion of polymicrobial anaerobic consortia rather than the isolated proliferation of an individual pathogen. Ecosystem classification into recognized human vaginal Community State Types demonstrated that CST IV, defined by high bacterial diversity and severe Lactobacillus depletion, represented the dominant ecological state across the studied population. CST IV was identified in 76.7 percent of healthy cytological controls and 81.5 percent of participants diagnosed with cervical dysplasia. CST III, characterized by an intermediate dominance of Lactobacillus iners, appeared in 15.0 percent of controls and 18.5 percent of dysplastic women, whereas classic Lactobacillus-dominated configurations designated as CST Other were found in only 8.3 percent of healthy controls and were completely absent among women with cervical dysplasia. Spearman correlation analysis indicated that quantitative human papillomavirus viral burden was not significantly correlated with the degree of community dysbiosis, yielding a correlation coefficient of -0.006. This absence of linear correlation suggests that viral replication intensity and mucosal bacterial disruption operate through partially decoupled pathways influenced by host immunity, mucosal barrier integrity, or preexisting anaerobic colonization rather than direct viral load kinetics. Functional pathway profiling inferred through the PICRUSt2 pipeline and MetaCyc database revealed that mucosal dysbiosis was accompanied by significant metabolic reprogramming toward anaerobic carbohydrate utilization and cellular stress responses. Dysplastic states and viral infection were characterized by significant enrichment in sucrose degradation II pathways alongside activation of chorismate biosynthesis II, heme biosynthesis, and lysine biosynthesis networks. These metabolic adaptations reflect bacterial mechanisms for sustaining cellular survival, promoting biofilm formation, and maintaining chronic local mucosal inflammation. The study authors emphasized that because their protocol employed a cross-sectional design, observed microbial shifts represent statistical associations rather than proven causal relationships. Furthermore, 16S rRNA gene sequencing provides predicted metagenomic capacity rather than direct enzymatic activity, and the down-selection of screened participants to 148 sequenced samples introduces potential selection limitations. Nonetheless, as the first West African community-based study combining blinded cytology, Nugent scoring, and next-generation sequencing, these findings establish critical baseline evidence supporting the development of microbiome-targeted screening and intervention strategies across high-burden settings. news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Saturday, November 28, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Cancer Treatment De-Escalation Fails to Match Standard Chemoradiotherapy in HPV-Associated Oropharyngeal Cancers by November 27, 2026 in Cancer, Health Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Treatment De-Escalation Fails to Match Standard Chemoradiotherapy in HPV-Associated Oropharyngeal Cancers Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Human papillomavirus-associated head and neck cancers, predominantly comprising oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinomas, represent an escalating global health burden characterized by distinct clinical, demographic, and biological features. According to global epidemiological data from GLOBOCON, head and neck malignancies accounted for approximately four percent of all cancer diagnoses in 2022, representing 745,000 new cases worldwide. Over recent decades, the global incidence of viral-driven head and neck squamous cell carcinomas has increased by 36.5 percent, with viral etiology contributing to approximately 25 percent of all head and neck malignancies. This association demonstrates striking anatomical variation, underlying an estimated 30.8 percent of oropharyngeal cancers alongside 2.4 percent of laryngeal and 2.2 percent of oral cavity tumors. The epidemiological profile has shifted toward younger cohorts, typically presenting in patients aged 45 to 64 years who lack significant exposure to tobacco or alcohol. Men face a disproportionately higher burden, exhibiting a two- to four-fold increased risk compared to women, while high-risk viral types 16 and 18 account for 84.9 percent of viral-positive tumors. The viral oncogenic cascade begins when infectious particles penetrate basal epithelial stem cells through microlesions in squamous mucosal tissues, potentially facilitated by host surface receptors including integrin alpha-6, laminin-332, and heparan sulfate proteoglycans. Following internalisation, the viral life cycle remains closely coordinated with epithelial cell differentiation. Initial infection stages rely on early proteins E1 and E2 to support episomal DNA replication and genomic maintenance in proliferating basal layers. As infected keratinocytes differentiate, early viral proteins E5, E6, and E7 sustain proliferative capacity and block apoptotic pathways, while E4 mediates G2 cell-cycle arrest to facilitate viral genome amplification. Complete virion assembly occurs in the upper epithelial strata through expression of late capsid proteins L1 and L2. Chronic infection promotes host genome integration requiring double-strand DNA breaks, inducing severe genomic instability. High-risk E6 activates telomerase reverse transcriptase transcription through complex interactions with E6-associated protein, c-Myc, and NFX1, thereby counteracting telomere shortening and conferring cellular immortality. Discover more Tour Colleges Study Biology Study Chemistry Viral oncoproteins E6 and E7 cooperate intimately to disable host tumor suppression and override cell-cycle checkpoints. The E7 oncoprotein binds hypo-phosphorylated retinoblastoma protein, triggering its proteasomal degradation and liberating E2F transcription factors to drive continuous progression past the G1/S transition. Although E7 expression generates oncogenic stress signals that naturally activate cellular defenses such as p53, p16, and p21, concurrent expression of E6 thwarts apoptosis by targeting p53 for degradation via the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway mediated by E6-associated protein. In oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma, this biology produces pronounced clinical divergence from cervical cancer and viral-negative malignancies. Oropharyngeal tumors elicit vigorous anti-tumor immune responses featuring more than double the infiltration of virus-specific T cells and reduced regulatory T-cell activity compared to cervical counterparts. However, viral interference with pattern recognition receptors, particularly Toll-like receptors, alongside dysregulated DNA damage repair, hypoxia, and extracellular matrix remodeling, can generate protective microenvironmental niches that foster treatment resistance. Discover more Engineering Job Board Research Paper Access Learn Engineering Track Biotech Current international clinical guidelines from the National Comprehensive Cancer Network and European consensus bodies establish distinct staging and management protocols for p16-positive oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma. For patients presenting with early-stage disease, consensus recommendations endorse single-modality treatment utilizing either definitive intensity-modulated radiotherapy or transoral surgery with neck dissection. In locoregionally advanced settings, concurrent cisplatin-based chemoradiotherapy delivering 70 to 72 Gray of intensity-modulated radiation therapy remains the standard of care to achieve optimal locoregional control and overall survival. Following surgical resection, adjuvant radiotherapy or chemoradiotherapy is indicated upon identification of high-risk adverse features, including positive surgical margins or extranodal tumor extension. Despite superior overall survival and radiosensitivity compared to viral-negative malignancies, international guidelines explicitly caution against substituting cetuximab for cisplatin outside clinical trials. Furthermore, routine treatment de-escalation remains strictly investigational, as unvalidated modifications to established curative regimens risk compromising disease control in patients who otherwise carry favorable oncological prognoses. Multiple prospective randomized clinical trials have evaluated treatment de-escalation strategies intended to diminish long-term therapeutic toxicities, yet several pivotal investigations failed to demonstrate oncological safety. In the randomized phase III RTOG 1016 and De-ESCALaTE HPV trials, substituting cetuximab for cisplatin during radiation therapy produced significantly worse cancer control without reducing overall treatment toxicities. RTOG 1016 recorded a 5-year locoregional failure rate of 17.3 percent with cetuximab compared with 9.9 percent for cisplatin, while De-ESCALaTE documented a 2-year recurrence rate of 16.1 percent versus 6.0 percent. Similarly, the randomized phase II/III NRG-HN005 trial examined reduced-dose radiotherapy of 60 Gray combined with either cisplatin or nivolumab against standard 70 Gray chemoradiotherapy in non-smoking patients with p16-positive oropharyngeal tumors. At 2.2 years of median follow-up, estimated 2-year progression-free survival was 98.1 percent with standard therapy, compared to 88.6 percent with reduced radiation plus cisplatin and 90.3 percent with reduced radiation plus nivolumab, failing non-inferiority criteria. Surgical de-escalation approaches have also confronted substantial safety and functional hurdles in prospective clinical evaluations. The randomized ORATOR2 trial, which compared primary radiotherapy against transoral surgery with neck dissection and pathology-directed adjuvant therapy for early-stage disease, was terminated prematurely following two treatment-related deaths in the surgical arm. Among 61 randomized participants, two-year overall survival reached 100 percent in the radiotherapy cohort compared to 90 percent following surgery, while progression-free survival was 100 percent versus 86 percent, respectively. Concurrently, a cohort analysis associated with the prospective phase III PATHOS trial evaluated early functional recovery in 508 patients undergoing transoral robotic surgery or transoral laser microsurgery. Patients treated with robotic approaches experienced significantly higher nasogastric tube dependency rates at 45.0 percent compared to 7.9 percent for laser microsurgery, alongside modestly inferior swallowing scores. Although transoral robotic surgery combined with selective neck dissection provides effective tumor clearance, its functional advantages diminish substantially whenever adjuvant therapy is required. In recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, systemic therapy represents the primary therapeutic option, traditionally relying on platinum-based chemotherapy incorporating gemcitabine and cisplatin. Immunotherapy targeting the PD-1/PD-L1 axis has established a crucial role following disease progression on platinum agents. The CheckMate 141 clinical trial validated nivolumab following platinum failure, while KEYNOTE-048 established pembrolizumab as preferred first-line therapy, either as monotherapy for tumors expressing PD-L1 with a combined positive score of at least one or combined with platinum and 5-fluorouracil. Recently, KEYNOTE-689 expanded pembrolizumab approval into the perioperative setting for resectable locally advanced disease. Although the tumor microenvironment of viral-positive malignancies displays heightened immune infiltration, viral status itself did not independently predict therapeutic benefit in pivotal trials, and overall response rates to monotherapy remain between 13 and 19 percent. Survival gains were driven primarily by PD-L1 expression rather than viral etiology, confirming durable benefits across both viral-positive and viral-negative patient cohorts. To overcome limited response rates and treatment resistance in recurrent or metastatic settings, investigators are developing innovative targeted therapeutics and combination immunotherapies. Complete virion assembly occurs in the upper epithelial strata through expression of late capsid proteins L1 and L2. Chronic infection promotes host genome integration requiring double-strand DNA breaks, inducing severe genomic instability. High-risk E6 activates telomerase reverse transcriptase transcription through complex interactions with E6-associated protein, c-Myc, and NFX1, thereby counteracting telomere shortening and conferring cellular immortality.
