news.content:
Explainer Mint explainer: why HPV vaccination is critical for girls as India crosses 10 million doses Priyanka Sharma 4 min read 27 Nov 2026, 01:31 PM IST India has delivered more than 10 million HPV vaccine doses to 14-year-old girls in under nine months, reaching nearly 87% of its target group. ( Pexel ) Summary India has vaccinated over 10 million 14-year-old girls against HPV in less than nine months. Mint explains the campaign’s progress, the science behind it and the challenges ahead. This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you. Subscribe to enjoy similar stories. India has administered more than 10 million doses of the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine to 14-year-old girls in less than nine months under a campaign by the Union health ministry. The drive has covered nearly 87% of the annual target cohort of about 12 million girls, drawing praise from the World Health Organization’s (WHO) South-East Asia Region. The milestone comes against a stark public-health backdrop. According to estimates by the WHO’s cancer agency, India records 1,27,526 new cervical cancer cases and 79,906 deaths every year, making it the second most common cancer among Indian women after breast cancer. The rapid vaccination marks a shift from treating cervical cancer at later stages to preventing it at the source. But the campaign’s long-term impact will depend on sustained coverage, awareness and access to screening and treatment. Mint explains why the vaccination drive matters, how it works and how states are faring. Also Read | Why India’s HPV vaccination drive is a shot in the arm to end cervical cancer Why is HPV vaccination critical for girls in India? India reports more new cervical cancer cases and deaths than any other country, accounting for one-fifth of global cases and nearly a quarter of all cervical cancer deaths worldwide. According to GLOBOCAN 2022 estimates, India records 1,27,526 new cases and 79,906 deaths annually, making cervical cancer the second most common cancer among Indian women after breast cancer. Because persistent infection with high-risk HPV strains—which are linked to over 80% of cervical cancer cases in India—drives the vast majority of the disease, immunising girls offers direct, long-term protection against a largely preventable cancer. Which vaccine is being used, and why is it given at age 14? The national campaign uses Gardasil-4, a quadrivalent recombinant vaccine manufactured by MSD (Merck), which protects against high-risk, cancer-causing HPV strains. The vaccine is procured with support from Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance. The shot is administered at age 14 because the vaccine works best when given well before any potential exposure to the virus. Nearly two decades of scientific research and real-world experience, backed by more than 800 million doses administered globally, show strong, lasting protection against vaccine-targeted HPV strains and precancerous lesions. Meanwhile, Serum Institute of India’s indigenous quadrivalent vaccine, CERVAVAC , received WHO prequalification in September 2026, expanding future domestic supply options for public programmes and UN agencies. What is the policy framework behind the rollout? India’s campaign aligns with the WHO’s global 90–70–90 strategy to eliminate cervical cancer by 2030. The strategy calls for vaccinating 90% of girls by age 15, screening 70% of women by ages 35 and 45, and treating 90% of women diagnosed with cervical disease. Following recommendations from the National Technical Advisory Group on Immunisation (NTAGI) and the Union government’s push in the Interim Budget 2024–25, Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched the nationwide campaign in February 2026. Also Read | India to launch nationwide HPV vaccination drive to eradicate cervical cancer India adopted a single-dose regimen, endorsed by the WHO as offering comparable protection to multi-dose schedules in young adolescents. The approach lowers procurement costs, simplifies cold-chain logistics and removes the risk of dropouts between doses. After an intensive 90-day campaign phase, the shot is being integrated into Routine Immunisation days at Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, primary health centres (PHCs), community health centres (CHCs) and district hospitals. Why can’t India rely on cancer screening alone? Screening through Visual Inspection with Acetic Acid (VIA), Pap smears or HPV-DNA tests can detect precancerous changes early. But national screening uptake among Indian women aged 30–49 remains around 1.9%, far below global benchmarks. Low awareness, social stigma and weak follow-up for confirmation and treatment mean that roughly 60% to 70% of cervical cancer cases in India are detected only at advanced stages. Vaccinating adolescents interrupts the chain of infection upfront, reducing the future burden of disease and the need for expensive, late-stage cancer care. However, vaccination does not replace screening, which remains important for women who are already eligible. India crossing the milestone of 10 million HPV vaccine doses is a significant step towards strengthening preventive healthcare for women. It reflects the government’s commendable commitment to protecting women’s health from an early age. HPV vaccination is one of the most effective interventions for preventing cervical cancer, said said Dr Archana Dhawan Bajaj, gynaecologist and fertility expert at Nurture Clinic. Ideally, girls should receive the vaccine between 9 and 14 years of age, preferably before exposure to HPV. Catch-up vaccination is recommended up to 26 years, while women aged 27–45 may consider it after medical consultation. Vaccination, complemented by regular cervical cancer screening, can significantly reduce India’s cervical cancer burden and save lives, she added. How are states managing the rollout, safety and digital tracking? Under Centre-State coordination, six states—Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Mizoram, Madhya Pradesh and Bihar—have achieved 100% coverage of their identified target populations, while 12 states have crossed 80%. Uttar Pradesh leads in volume, with more than 29.33 lakh girls vaccinated, followed by Bihar with over 13.70 lakh and Gujarat with over 7.75 lakh. Uptake has also been strong in Assam (95.63%), Telangana (95.28%), Karnataka (93.16%) and Uttarakhand (90.17%). State-led drives in Bihar, Tamil Nadu and Sikkim have been folded into the national mission. Also Read | HPV vaccine: Is one dose enough for girls? Should males get this vaccine? All sessions are free and voluntary, require parental consent and are conducted under trained medical officers, with links to 24×7 facilities to manage any rare adverse events following immunisation (AEFI). Specialists from AIIMS, alongside teachers, ASHAs and ANMs, lead grassroots awareness efforts. The U-WIN digital platform enables slot booking, digital certificates and real-time district-level tracking of coverage gaps. About the Author Priyanka Sharma Priyanka Sharma is a journalist at Mint, where she covers the Union Ministry of Health and the pharmaceutical industry. Her work focuses on explaining government policies and how they impact healthcare and the medicine market in India. With 12 years of experience in journalism, she has built a reputation for providing clear and honest news on important health topics that affect the entire country.

Her educational background includes a journalism degree from the prestigious Indian Institute of Mass Communication (IIMC) and specialized training in public health from the Public Health Foundation of India. Before her current role at Mint, Priyanka worked with India Today, The Pioneer, and ANI. She also served as a lead consultant for the National Health Authority, which gave her firsthand knowledge of how the government manages large-scale health programmes.

Priyanka is based in New Delhi and is an avid traveller who loves visiting the mountains. She has a great interest in regional flavours, particularly South Indian food. Cervical cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality across Guatemala, resulting in 1,555 new diagnosed cases and 872 deaths each year. On a global level, cervical cancer represents a substantial preventable malignancy burden that disproportionately affects low- and middle-income nations. Although Guatemala has provided human papillomavirus vaccination to ten-year-old girls since 2018, public health decision-makers have faced the critical policy question of whether extending routine immunization coverage to boys represents an efficient allocation of limited resources. To address this question, researchers led by Beatriz Hernández evaluated the long-term economic outcomes of extending vaccination programs using locally derived epidemiological and cost data. The investigation adopted the perspective of the national public health system and implemented the PLANTEVEC static model. Methodological design and reporting strictly adhered to the CHEERS 2022 guidelines. To capture long-term health and financial impacts, the investigators applied an extensive 100-year analytic horizon. Future health outcomes and economic costs were both discounted at a standard annual rate of 3 percent, ensuring consistency across long-range projections. Model estimates established incremental cost-effectiveness ratios, or ICERs, measured in United States dollars per disability-adjusted life year avoided. The evaluated interventions were compared directly against Guatemala’s gross domestic product per capita, which was established at USD 4,354.89 as the decision benchmark. Maintaining vaccination exclusively for girls yielded an estimated ICER of USD 1,089 per DALY avoided. In comparison, transitioning to a gender-neutral vaccination strategy covering both girls and boys yielded an estimated ICER of USD 1,959 per DALY avoided. Crucially, the modeled costs of both immunization strategies remained well below the benchmark threshold of one GDP per capita. Based on these findings, the study concluded that human papillomavirus vaccination strategies in Guatemala are economically efficient under established decision criteria. While expanding routine immunization to include boys carries a higher cost per disability-adjusted life year avoided than vaccinating girls alone, the gender-neutral intervention remains fully within accepted cost-effectiveness thresholds. Consequently, extending coverage beyond ten-year-old girls to include male cohorts provides an economically justifiable approach for the public health sector that directly supports equity-oriented prevention across the country. elements_zh.time: 该研究于 2026 年 11 月 26 日发布。该分析评估了 100 年范围内的长期经济成果,发布日期为最新参考日期。
elements_zh.location_and_population: 该研究以危地马拉为重点,专门检查了公共卫生系统及其人口,重点关注 10 岁女孩以及可能将男孩纳入 HPV 疫苗接种 计划的情况。
elements_zh.event: Beatriz Hernández 领导的研究人员进行的一项研究发现,根据使用当地​​流行病学和成本数据进行的成本效益分析,将 HPV 疫苗接种 扩大到危地马拉的男孩具有经济效率。Bioengineer.org 于 2026 年 11 月 26 日报道了该研究。
elements_zh.scale_impact_and_risk: 该研究比较了两种 疫苗接种 策略:一种仅针对女孩,预计可避免每个 DALY 的 ICER 1,089 美元;另一种针对女孩和男孩,预计可避免每个 DALY 的 ICER 1,959 美元。这两种策略均在可接受的成本效益阈值之内,因为其成本仍低于人均 GDP 基准 4,354.89 美元。
elements_zh.response_status_and_uncertainty: 该研究得出的结论是,将 HPV 疫苗接种 覆盖范围扩大到男孩对于危地马拉的公共卫生部门来说在经济上是合理的。该分析基于 PLANTEVEC 静态模型并遵循 CHEERS 2022 指南。研究结果基于建模数据,并不代表已确认的 暴发 或实时公共卫生反应。

news.content_zh: Bioengineer.org 于 2026 年 11 月 26 日发表的一项研究发现,将 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 疫苗接种 扩大到危地马拉的男孩具有经济效率。这项研究由 Beatriz Hernández 领导,利用本地数据评估了将男性 队列研究 纳入 HPV 免疫计划的长期成本效益。该研究比较了两种策略:只为女孩接种疫苗,每避免一个残疾调整生命年 (DALY) 的增量成本效益比 (ICER) 估计为 1,089 美元;对女孩和男孩都接种疫苗,每避免一个 DALY 的 ICER 为 1,959 美元。这两种策略均在可接受的成本效益阈值之内,因为其成本仍低于危地马拉人均 GDP 基准 4,354.89 美元。该分析使用 PLANTEVEC 静态模型并遵循 CHEERS 2022 指南。研究结果表明,将 疫苗接种 扩大到男孩对于公共卫生部门来说是一种经济上合理的方法,支持以公平为导向的预防工作。

analysis_zh.location_and_population: 该研究以危地马拉为重点,专门检查了公共卫生系统及其人口,重点关注 10 岁女孩以及可能将男孩纳入 HPV 疫苗接种 计划的情况。
analysis_zh.event: Beatriz Hernández 领导的研究人员进行的一项研究发现,根据使用当地​​流行病学和成本数据进行的成本效益分析,将 HPV 疫苗接种 扩大到危地马拉的男孩具有经济效率。Bioengineer.org 于 2026 年 11 月 26 日报道了该研究。
analysis_zh.scale_impact_and_risk: 该研究比较了两种 疫苗接种 策略:一种仅针对女孩,预计可避免每个 DALY 的 ICER 1,089 美元;另一种针对女孩和男孩,预计可避免每个 DALY 的 ICER 1,959 美元。这两种策略均在可接受的成本效益阈值之内,因为其成本仍低于人均 GDP 基准 4,354.89 美元。
analysis_zh.response_status_and_uncertainty: 该研究得出的结论是,将 HPV 疫苗接种 覆盖范围扩大到男孩对于危地马拉的公共卫生部门来说在经济上是合理的。该分析基于 PLANTEVEC 静态模型并遵循 CHEERS 2022 指南。研究结果基于建模数据,并不代表已确认的 暴发 或实时公共卫生反应。

news.content: Skip to main content Montreal Calgary Edmonton Halifax Kitchener Montreal Ottawa Toronto Vancouver Winnipeg About About Us Our Team Contact Contact Us Advertise With Us Submit a News Tip News All Local Canada World Watch All Latest Videos Weather Montreal All Montreal Calgary Edmonton Halifax Kitchener Montreal Ottawa Toronto Vancouver Winnipeg About All About Us Our Team Contact All Contact Us Advertise With Us Submit a News Tip Quebec gradually rolls out HPV self-testing for cervical cancer screening A swab and collection tube used by patients to collect their own samples for human papillomavirus (HPV) testing as part of cervical cancer screening. (Courtesy: Santé Québec Chaudière-Appalaches) By News Staff Posted November 27, 2026 7:31 pm. Quebec is gradually introducing self-collection for cervical cancer screening, offering an alternative to traditional pelvic exams for people who may have delayed testing or face barriers to accessing health care. The initiative is currently being rolled out in Chaudière-Appalaches. Dr. Jeannot Dumaresq, a medical microbiologist and infectious diseases specialist with Santé Québec in the region, says the Health Ministry and Santé Québec have asked hospitals and regions across the province to make self-sampling available next year. The tests detect human papillomavirus (HPV), a virus that can cause cervical cancer, and allow eligible individuals to collect their own samples without requiring a health-care professional to perform the initial pelvic exam. A swab and collection tube used by patients to collect their own samples for human papillomavirus (HPV) testing as part of cervical cancer screening. (Courtesy: Santé Québec Chaudière-Appalaches) Dr. Shannon Salvador, a gynecologic oncologist at the Jewish General Hospital and an associate professor at McGill University, says the initiative could help reach people who have difficulty accessing screening. “This is an incredible progression for Quebec and being able to treat and screen people who could potentially have cervix cancer or pre cancer of the cervix,” Salvador said. Removing barriers to screening Dumaresq says the self-collection option is intended to reach people who may be uncomfortable with traditional screening or have put it off for years. “A lot of people are reluctant to have a pelvic exam for the cervical cancer screening either because of anxiety, because of discomfort, past trauma or sometimes cultural norms,” he said. He estimates that roughly one in four women is not up to date with cervical cancer screening. Dumaresq says cervical cancer is one of the most preventable cancers, thanks to vaccination and screening. He says early detection is associated with very high survival rates, while the chances of survival drop sharply when the disease is diagnosed at a later stage. Salvador says the test could make screening more accessible to people who struggle to reach health-care providers. “The individuals who can benefit the most from this test are those who do not have easy access to the healthcare system, whether they don’t have a family doctor or they’re too far remote and they can’t come into an area where there is healthcare professionals who do this test,” she said. How self-collection works The process involves a swab and a transport tube. Eligible individuals can collect their own sample at a clinic or take the kit home before returning it to a health-care provider. Dumaresq explains how the sample is collected. “We give the person a kit. There’s a swab, there’s a transport tube and then the person has to insert the swab just a few centimeters inside the vagina, just turns it there for a couple of seconds, then we put it back in the transport tube and that’s it. And then we bring it back to the medical clinic, the local service point or the test center,” he said. The service is covered by the Régie de l’assurance maladie du Québec (RAMQ). For now, there are no plans to distribute the kits by mail. Dumaresq says they are available through medical clinics known as local service points. People with a prescription can also obtain a kit at traditional testing centres, complete the sample at home or on-site and return it to their health-care provider. Positive results require further testing A positive HPV result does not mean someone has cervical cancer, but further investigation is necessary. Dumaresq says anyone who tests positive will need further screening to determine whether cancerous or precancerous changes are present. “We have to make sure that the person knows that if the result is negative, that we will just do another screening in a couple of years. But if the test is positive, the person has to know that then a pelvic exam will be needed to collect some cells directly in the cervix to look at the cells and see if there is cancerous or pre-cancerous cells,” he said. Salvador says people with positive results should be followed in a specialized clinic, such as a colposcopy clinic, where they can be assessed by a gynecologist or gynecologic oncologist. She says laboratory validation has also helped address concerns about the reliability of samples collected by patients themselves. “They have now shown that with the new validations that they do in the lab, they’re able to identify that the sample is just as good as a sample collected within a clinic by a healthcare professional,” Salvador said. If a sample does not meet laboratory validation requirements, Salvador says the person will be notified and may be asked to repeat the test or have a health-care professional collect the sample. Provincewide rollout expected next year Although Santé Québec and the Health Ministry have asked regions to offer self-sampling next year, implementation will be gradual because laboratories use different HPV tests, and each must be validated to ensure it works with self-collected samples. Dumaresq says the validation process is necessary because the tests used in Quebec laboratories vary. “In Canada there is no HPV or human papuomavirus test that is approved by Health Canada for self-sampling. So every lab had to do what we call a validation to make sure that the kits, the sampling kits we use, the tests we use in the lab are compatible and it works well with self-sampling,” he said. Dumaresq says regions using the same laboratory test as Chaudière-Appalaches can use the results of its validation work, while regions using different tests must complete their own validation. In a statement to CityNews, Santé Québec said it began working with health and social services institutions following a September 2026 update to HPV self-sampling guidelines and standards by the Institut national d’excellence en santé et en services sociaux (INESSS). “The next steps will be determined once this work with the network is completed,” the statement said. “Each region will be able to organize implementation based on its local context and available resources.” Santé Québec also confirmed that its Chaudière-Appalaches institution is currently the only one gradually rolling out self-sampling for cervical cancer screening. Salvador hopes the program will be available across Quebec by early to mid-2027, although a provincewide implementation date has not been confirmed. She stresses that timely follow-up is essential for anyone who receives a positive result. “If you know that you are positive, is it extremely important that you get in for the next steps, which is a colposcopy. To miss that is the shame of why did we even do the test in the first place,” she said. In the longer term, Dumaresq hopes self-collection will help detect more precancerous changes before they develop into cancer, potentially preventing cases and deaths. news.content_title: Review Maps How Papillomavirus and Tumor Barriers Disrupt Natural Killer
news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Saturday, November 28, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Review Maps How Papillomavirus and Tumor Barriers Disrupt Natural Killer Immunity by November 24, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Review Maps How Papillomavirus and Tumor Barriers Disrupt Natural Killer Immunity Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram In a comprehensive narrative review published in Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology, researchers led by Bowen Xu and colleagues synthesized translational and preclinical evidence detailing how high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) infection coordinates multilayered tumor immune microenvironment barriers to drive natural killer (NK) cell dysfunction in cervical cancer. Cervical cancer remains a significant global health burden as the fourth most common cancer in women, accounting for approximately 570,000 new cases and 311,000 deaths annually worldwide, with high-risk HPV types 16 and 18 responsible for roughly 70 percent of all diagnoses. The authors emphasize that although NK cells act as critical innate effectors capable of recognizing and destroying transformed cells in an antigen-independent manner, their antitumor efficacy within cervical tumors is progressively blunted. Rather than stemming purely from isolated intrinsic cellular defects, this functional decline reflects an integrated, actively maintained suppressive ecosystem that impedes NK cell recruitment, spatial penetration, receptor activation, and cytotoxicity. The investigators conducted a structured literature search across PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, and Scopus, focusing predominantly on studies published over the past five years alongside foundational landmark mechanistic research. To establish rigorous interpretation across diverse experimental systems, the review explicitly categorized evidence into three distinct tiers: cervical cancer-specific evidence obtained directly from patient tissues or cell models, HPV-associated mechanistic findings detailing viral oncoprotein effects, and cross-tumor mechanistic evidence derived from other solid tumors or general preclinical systems. The authors noted that cross-tumor findings serve only to provide biological plausibility and mechanistic context rather than proof of dominant drivers in cervical malignancy. Furthermore, because the evaluation was structured as a narrative synthesis rather than a quantitative systematic review or meta-analysis, formal risk-of-bias scoring was omitted, though potential publication biases, model heterogeneity, and the translational limits of extrapolating preclinical findings to human disease were critically integrated into their evaluations. At the molecular initiator level, persistent high-risk HPV infection actively sabotages innate immune perception through the coordinated action of its viral oncoproteins. Experimental studies highlighted in the review demonstrate that HPV18 E7 functions as a branch-selective modulator of the cGAS–STING cytosolic DNA-sensing pathway; rather than causing broad pathway inhibition, E7 selectively suppresses STING-induced NF-κB signaling by restricting the nuclear accumulation of p65, while leaving the parallel STING–TBK1–IRF3 signaling cascade relatively preserved. Concurrently, HPV E7 impairs inflammatory signaling by binding IFI16 and recruiting the E3 ubiquitin ligase TRIM21, driving the ubiquitination and degradation of IFI16-associated inflammasome complexes and drastically reducing the production of interleukin-18, an essential cytokine required for NK cell activation and proliferation. Additionally, HPV16 E5 alters Golgi trafficking and chaperone interactions to selectively downregulate surface expression of classical human leukocyte antigen molecules HLA-A and HLA-B, blunting CD8+ T-cell recognition while deliberately preserving inhibitory ligands that suppress NK cells. Discover more Study Biology cancers cancer Find Cancer Care Cancer Beyond viral oncoprotein signaling, physical and structural remodeling of the extracellular matrix establishes a rigid mechanical barrier that physically excludes NK cells from the tumor core. The synthesis details how cancer-associated fibroblasts drive excessive deposition of collagen fibers, fibronectin, and hyaluronic acid, altering tissue mechanical properties. Studies indicate that when the pore size of dense collagen networks contracts below 2 square micrometers, cytotoxic lymphocyte migration is completely blocked, forcing lymphocytes to switch from efficient ameboid movement to slow, inefficient interstitial crawling that reduces tissue patrolling speed. In vitro and engineered-matrix models show that while fibronectin stabilizes immune synapses between T cells and tumor cells, it disrupts synaptic stability in NK cells, prompting continuous migration and diminished killing capacity. Although multiplex immunohistochemistry of human cervical cancer samples confirms that NK cells and CD8+ T cells are restricted largely to the surrounding stroma rather than tumor epithelial nests, specific matrix features driving this spatial exclusion in patients require further characterization. Cellular components of the tumor immune microenvironment further amplify this immune-restricted state through interlocking suppressive networks. Regulatory T cells directly curb NK cell activation, cytokine production, and degranulation through competitive consumption of interleukin-2 and secretion of transforming growth factor-beta and interleukin-10. Tumor-associated neutrophils release reactive oxygen species, arginase, and proteases that damage surface activating receptors, while tumor-associated macrophages secrete vascular endothelial growth factor and prostaglandins to enforce immunosuppression, though much of this detailed myeloid-suppression data originates from non-cervical tumor models. Notably, the review highlights that cervical cancer tissue analyses have identified a spatially associated subpopulation of LAMP3-positive dendritic cells that express indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1. This enzyme accelerates tryptophan depletion and kynurenine accumulation, activating aryl hydrocarbon receptor pathways to foster regulatory T-cell tolerance. However, the authors caution that existing cervical evidence for LAMP3-positive dendritic-cell interactions through IL-15 receptor or NECTIN2–TIGIT signaling remains correlative and lacks direct causal confirmation. Impaired NK cell trafficking and effector fitness are also driven by dysregulated chemokine signaling and severe metabolic constraints within the cervical tumor milieu. Chemotactic axes critical for NK cell recruitment, including CCL5-CCR5, CCL27-CCR10, and CX3CL1-CX3CR1, are frequently restricted by microenvironmental signals, while hypoxic conditions downregulate CCR1, CCR5, and CXCR3 expression on NK cells. Furthermore, disruptions to the interferon-gamma–CXCL9/CXCL10–CXCR3 recruitment circuit hamper lymphocyte infiltration into tumors. Concurrently, metabolic stressors including lactate accumulation, extracellular acidification, adenosine–A2A receptor signaling, and nutrient deprivation compromise NK cell cytotoxicity, although their specific contributions in human cervical cancer await direct characterization. Clinical investigations in HPV-associated cervical lesions document marked downregulation of key activating receptors—including NKG2D, NKp30, and NKp46—alongside reduced perforin levels and increased inhibitory signaling via non-classical HLA-E binding to CD94/NKG2A and elevated TIGIT expression on CD56-bright NK subsets, tilting the receptor balance toward profound functional inactivation. The review examines how current clinical immunotherapies intersect with these microenvironmental hurdles, pointing out that established treatments do not automatically reverse NK cell impairment. While the KEYNOTE-A18 trial validated the clinical benefit of adding the PD-1 inhibitor pembrolizumab to chemoradiotherapy in patients with newly diagnosed, high-risk locally advanced cervical cancer, and cemiplimab demonstrated survival improvements in recurrent or metastatic disease, these achievements do not demonstrate restored NK cell cytotoxicity, as neither trial verified NK-specific functional recovery. Conversely, direct clinical evaluation of the anti-NKG2A antibody monalizumab in advanced gynecologic cancers, including cervical carcinoma under trial NCT02459301, yielded no objective tumor responses despite good tolerability. Furthermore, an expansion cohort combining monalizumab with durvalumab in trial NCT02671435 reported an objective response rate of zero percent in cervical cancer patients. These clinical outcomes demonstrate that simply blocking inhibitory checkpoints on NK cells is insufficient without overcoming concurrent microenvironmental constraints. To address these limitations, emerging NK cell-directed therapies are being explored, though they remain largely confined to preclinical testing in cervical oncology. Adoptive transfer using allogeneic umbilical cord blood-derived or stem-cell-derived NK cells provides HLA-independent tumor killing, yet clinical translation is hampered by limited in vivo persistence, host-mediated clearance, cytokine dependence, and rapid suppression upon entering the tumor microenvironment. Chimeric antigen receptor engineering offers enhanced selectivity; specifically, anti-FAP CAR-NK cells have demonstrated preclinical efficacy against FAP-expressing cervical cancer cells and cancer-associated fibroblasts in three-dimensional spheroid models, while anti-mesothelin CAR-NK cells show activity against mesothelin-expressing targets. However, the authors stress that target heterogeneity and the risk of off-tumor stromal toxicity remain major concerns, particularly given the functional diversity of fibroblasts. Cytokine therapies utilizing IL-15 superagonists or memory-like NK cells pre-activated with IL-12 and IL-15 show promise in enhancing cytotoxicity, but their clinical utility must balance antitumor potency against systemic toxicities and lack of durability. The review synthesizes clinicopathological and prognostic studies evaluating NK cell parameters, concluding that NK cell functional phenotype provides far greater predictive insight than raw cell abundance. In a retrospective clinical cohort of 101 postoperative cervical cancer patients receiving adjuvant radiotherapy by Wang and colleagues, circulating NK cell proportions below 16 percent or absolute counts below 200 cells per microliter correlated with poorer overall survival in univariable analyses, though statistical significance was lost after multivariable adjustment. In a tissue-microarray cohort of 406 patients evaluated by Zou and colleagues, intratumoral CD57-positive cell density declined with advancing clinical stage, contributing to a composite immune score distinguishing 3-year survival rates of 96.6 percent versus 83.0 percent, though CD57 is not entirely NK-specific. Additionally, single-cell transcriptomic analyses by Liu and colleagues linked mature cytotoxic CD16-positive NK cell signatures to longer survival, whereas Gutierrez-Silerio and Cao reported progressive receptor loss and exhaustion profiles across advanced disease stages. Looking toward future therapeutic design, the authors propose rational, barrier-oriented combination strategies that integrate extracellular matrix remodeling, cytokine metabolic support, and targeted checkpoint inhibition. For example, combining matrix-degrading enzymes or anti-FAP CAR-NK cells with adoptive cell transfer could mitigate physical exclusion, while pairing TGF-beta pathway inhibitors with PD-1/PD-L1 blockade could relieve dual immunosuppressive mechanisms. Similarly, cytokine priming might compensate for HPV-driven IL-18 deficiency. Nonetheless, the authors caution that these combinatorial concepts remain hypothesis-generating and carry significant safety risks, including excessive immune activation, severe inflammatory toxicities, and impaired normal tissue repair. The synthesis concludes that clinical progress demands prospective validation of standardized spatial and cellular biomarkers, rigorous stratification by HPV infection status, and carefully designed trials evaluating whether multi-target regimens can safely dismantle the tumor microenvironment barrier and restore durable natural killer cell immunity in cervical cancer. Cervical cancer remains a significant global health burden as the fourth most common cancer in women, accounting for approximately 570,000 new cases and 311,000 deaths annually worldwide, with high-risk HPV types 16 and 18 responsible for roughly 70 percent of all diagnoses. The authors emphasize that although NK cells act as critical innate effectors capable of recognizing and destroying transformed cells in an antigen-independent manner, their antitumor efficacy within cervical tumors is progressively blunted. Rather than stemming purely from isolated intrinsic cellular defects, this functional decline reflects an integrated, actively maintained suppressive ecosystem that impedes NK cell recruitment, spatial penetration, receptor activation, and cytotoxicity. The investigators conducted a structured literature search across PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, and Scopus, focusing predominantly on studies published over the past five years alongside foundational landmark mechanistic research. To establish rigorous interpretation across diverse experimental systems, the review explicitly categorized evidence into three distinct tiers: cervical cancer-specific evidence obtained directly from patient tissues or cell models, HPV-associated mechanistic findings detailing viral oncoprotein effects, and cross-tumor mechanistic evidence derived from other solid tumors or general preclinical systems. The authors noted that cross-tumor findings serve only to provide biological plausibility and mechanistic context rather than proof of dominant drivers in cervical malignancy. Furthermore, because the evaluation was structured as a narrative synthesis rather than a quantitative systematic review or meta-analysis, formal risk-of-bias scoring was omitted, though potential publication biases, model heterogeneity, and the translational limits of extrapolating preclinical findings to human disease were critically integrated into their evaluations. At the molecular initiator level, persistent high-risk HPV infection actively sabotages innate immune perception through the coordinated action of its viral oncoproteins. Experimental studies highlighted in the review demonstrate that HPV18 E7 functions as a branch-selective modulator of the cGAS–STING cytosolic DNA-sensing pathway; rather than causing broad pathway inhibition, E7 selectively suppresses STING-induced NF-κB signaling by restricting the nuclear accumulation of p65, while leaving the parallel STING–TBK1–IRF3 signaling cascade relatively preserved. Concurrently, HPV E7 impairs inflammatory signaling by binding IFI16 and recruiting the E3 ubiquitin ligase TRIM21, driving the ubiquitination and degradation of IFI16-associated inflammasome complexes and drastically reducing the production of interleukin-18, an essential cytokine required for NK cell activation and proliferation. Additionally, HPV16 E5 alters Golgi trafficking and chaperone interactions to selectively downregulate surface expression of classical human leukocyte antigen molecules HLA-A and HLA-B, blunting CD8+ T-cell recognition while deliberately preserving inhibitory ligands that suppress NK cells. Discover more Study Biology cancers cancer Find Cancer Care Cancer Beyond viral oncoprotein signaling, physical and structural remodeling of the extracellular matrix establishes a rigid mechanical barrier that physically excludes NK cells from the tumor core. The synthesis details how cancer-associated fibroblasts drive excessive deposition of collagen fibers, fibronectin, and hyaluronic acid, altering tissue mechanical properties. Studies indicate that when the pore size of dense collagen networks contracts below 2 square micrometers, cytotoxic lymphocyte migration is completely blocked, forcing lymphocytes to switch from efficient ameboid movement to slow, inefficient interstitial crawling that reduces tissue patrolling speed. In vitro and engineered-matrix models show that while fibronectin stabilizes immune synapses between T cells and tumor cells, it disrupts synaptic stability in NK cells, prompting continuous migration and diminished killing capacity. Although multiplex immunohistochemistry of human cervical cancer samples confirms that NK cells and CD8+ T cells are restricted largely to the surrounding stroma rather than tumor epithelial nests, specific matrix features driving this spatial exclusion in patients require further characterization. Cellular components of the tumor immune microenvironment further amplify this immune-restricted state through interlocking suppressive networks. Regulatory T cells directly curb NK cell activation, cytokine production, and degranulation through competitive consumption of interleukin-2 and secretion of transforming growth factor-beta and interleukin-10. Tumor-associated neutrophils release reactive oxygen species, arginase, and proteases that damage surface activating receptors, while tumor-associated macrophages secrete vascular endothelial growth factor and prostaglandins to enforce immunosuppression, though much of this detailed myeloid-suppression data originates from non-cervical tumor models. Notably, the review highlights that cervical cancer tissue analyses have identified a spatially associated subpopulation of LAMP3-positive dendritic cells that express indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1. This enzyme accelerates tryptophan depletion and kynurenine accumulation, activating aryl hydrocarbon receptor pathways to foster regulatory T-cell tolerance. However, the authors caution that existing cervical evidence for LAMP3-positive dendritic-cell interactions through IL-15 receptor or NECTIN2–TIGIT signaling remains correlative and lacks direct causal confirmation. Impaired NK cell trafficking and effector fitness are also driven by dysregulated chemokine signaling and severe metabolic constraints within the cervical tumor milieu. Chemotactic axes critical for NK cell recruitment, including CCL5-CCR5, CCL27-CCR10, and CX3CL1-CX3CR1, are frequently restricted by microenvironmental signals, while hypoxic conditions downregulate CCR1, CCR5, and CXCR3 expression on NK cells. Furthermore, disruptions to the interferon-gamma–CXCL9/CXCL10–CXCR3 recruitment circuit hamper lymphocyte infiltration into tumors. Concurrently, metabolic stressors including lactate accumulation, extracellular acidification, adenosine–A2A receptor signaling, and nutrient deprivation compromise NK cell cytotoxicity, although their specific contributions in human cervical cancer await direct characterization. Clinical investigations in HPV-associated cervical lesions document marked downregulation of key activating receptors—including NKG2D, NKp30, and NKp46—alongside reduced perforin levels and increased inhibitory signaling via non-classical HLA-E binding to CD94/NKG2A and elevated TIGIT expression on CD56-bright NK subsets, tilting the receptor balance toward profound functional inactivation. The review examines how current clinical immunotherapies intersect with these microenvironmental hurdles, pointing out that established treatments do not automatically reverse NK cell impairment. While the KEYNOTE-A18 trial validated the clinical benefit of adding the PD-1 inhibitor pembrolizumab to chemoradiotherapy in patients with newly diagnosed, high-risk locally advanced cervical cancer, and cemiplimab demonstrated survival improvements in recurrent or metastatic disease, these achievements do not demonstrate restored NK cell cytotoxicity, as neither trial verified NK-specific functional recovery. Conversely, direct clinical evaluation of the anti-NKG2A antibody monalizumab in advanced gynecologic cancers, including cervical carcinoma under trial NCT02459301, yielded no objective tumor responses despite good tolerability. Furthermore, an expansion cohort combining monalizumab with durvalumab in trial NCT02671435 reported an objective response rate of zero percent in cervical cancer patients. These clinical outcomes demonstrate that simply blocking inhibitory checkpoints on NK cells is insufficient without overcoming concurrent microenvironmental constraints. To address these limitations, emerging NK cell-directed therapies are being explored, though they remain largely confined to preclinical testing in cervical oncology. Adoptive transfer using allogeneic umbilical cord blood-derived or stem-cell-derived NK cells provides HLA-independent tumor killing, yet clinical translation is hampered by limited in vivo persistence, host-mediated clearance, cytokine dependence, and rapid suppression upon entering the tumor microenvironment. Chimeric antigen receptor engineering offers enhanced selectivity; specifically, anti-FAP CAR-NK cells have demonstrated preclinical efficacy against FAP-expressing cervical cancer cells and cancer-associated fibroblasts in three-dimensional spheroid models, while anti-mesothelin CAR-NK cells show activity against mesothelin-expressing targets. However, the authors stress that target heterogeneity and the risk of off-tumor stromal toxicity remain major concerns, particularly given the functional diversity of fibroblasts. Cytokine therapies utilizing IL-15 superagonists or memory-like NK cells pre-activated with IL-12 and IL-15 show promise in enhancing cytotoxicity, but their clinical utility must balance antitumor potency against systemic toxicities and lack of durability. The review synthesizes clinicopathological and prognostic studies evaluating NK cell parameters, concluding that NK cell functional phenotype provides far greater predictive insight than raw cell abundance. In a retrospective clinical cohort of 101 postoperative cervical cancer patients receiving adjuvant radiotherapy by Wang and colleagues, circulating NK cell proportions below 16 percent or absolute counts below 200 cells per microliter correlated with poorer overall survival in univariable analyses, though statistical significance was lost after multivariable adjustment. In a tissue-microarray cohort of 406 patients evaluated by Zou and colleagues, intratumoral CD57-positive cell density declined with advancing clinical stage, contributing to a composite immune score distinguishing 3-year survival rates of 96.6 percent versus 83.0 percent, though CD57 is not entirely NK-specific. Additionally, single-cell transcriptomic analyses by Liu and colleagues linked mature cytotoxic CD16-positive NK cell signatures to longer survival, whereas Gutierrez-Silerio and Cao reported progressive receptor loss and exhaustion profiles across advanced disease stages. Looking toward future therapeutic design, the authors propose rational, barrier-oriented combination strategies that integrate extracellular matrix remodeling, cytokine metabolic support, and targeted checkpoint inhibition. For example, combining matrix-degrading enzymes or anti-FAP CAR-NK cells with adoptive cell transfer could mitigate physical exclusion, while pairing TGF-beta pathway inhibitors with PD-1/PD-L1 blockade could relieve dual immunosuppressive mechanisms. Similarly, cytokine priming might compensate for HPV-driven IL-18 deficiency. Nonetheless, the authors caution that these combinatorial concepts remain hypothesis-generating and carry significant safety risks, including excessive immune activation, severe inflammatory toxicities, and impaired normal tissue repair. The synthesis concludes that clinical progress demands prospective validation of standardized spatial and cellular biomarkers, rigorous stratification by HPV infection status, and carefully designed trials evaluating whether multi-target regimens can safely dismantle the tumor microenvironment barrier and restore durable natural killer cell immunity in cervical cancer. news.content_title: 🇿🇦 83 percent fewer girls in South Africa carry the most dangerous HPV types
news.content: Photo: ©epicurean via Canva.com The share of 17- and 18-year-old girls with HPV types 16 and 18 fell from 21.6 percent in 2019 to 3.2 percent in 2023. Among girls with HIV, the share fell from 29.4 to 4.4 percent. Even girls who had not been vaccinated had 74 percent lower prevalence of these types, because the virus spreads less when most people are vaccinated. HPV, human papillomavirus, is a virus that spreads through sex. Some types of the virus can lead to cervical cancer. Types 16 and 18 cause about 70 percent of all cases worldwide. South Africa began vaccinating against HPV in 2014. The vaccine is given free of charge in public schools to girls in Grade 4 who are at least nine years old. It protects against types 16 and 18. In the first year, 87 percent of the girls received at least one dose. From one in five to three in a hundred Researchers from Wits RHI at the University of the Witwatersrand and the Kirby Institute at the University of New South Wales have studied how the program works. The results are published in a study in The Lancet Global Health. Cervical cancer often takes decades to develop. So the researchers measured how common the virus is, since it is the virus that causes the cancer. The study is based on 2,357 girls aged 17 and 18. They came from 15 health clinics in four provinces: Free State, Gauteng, Mpumalanga and North West. The girls took a sample themselves, which was tested for 28 HPV types. The first group was examined in 2019. Those girls were too old to have been offered the vaccine. Among them, 21.6 percent carried type 16 or 18. The second group was examined in 2023 and had been offered the vaccine. In that group, the share was 3.2 percent. That is a reduction of 83 percent. Among the girls whose vaccination was on record, the share was 1.5 percent. That is 92 percent lower than before the program. The same effect for girls with HIV About a quarter of the girls were living with HIV. In South Africa, about 7.9 million people were living with HIV in 2025, or 12.3 percent of the population. HIV makes it more likely that HPV stays in the body and leads to cancer. Among girls with HIV, the share with type 16 or 18 fell from 29.4 to 4.4 percent. That is a reduction of 82 percent. For girls without HIV, the result was about the same. According to Wits, this is the first time in the world that this has been shown at the population level. The protection also reaches the unvaccinated Girls who had not been vaccinated also had less HPV in 2023. Among them, 5.5 percent carried type 16 or 18, which is 74 percent lower than in 2019. The researchers attribute this to herd immunity. When most people are vaccinated, the virus spreads less, and that also protects those who have not received the vaccine. Types 31 and 45, which are related to 16 and 18, also declined. The share fell from 16.6 to 5.7 percent. Other HPV types did not decline. According to the researchers, this strongly suggests that the vaccine, and not changes in sexual behavior, is behind the decline. Two doses were enough South Africa gave two doses. Even so, the decline was as large as in wealthy countries that gave three doses. The researchers say that part of the explanation is that more than 80 percent of the girls were vaccinated in the first years. In 2022, the World Health Organization, WHO, recommended that one dose is enough for most people. For people with HIV, WHO still recommends three doses. South Africa switched to one dose in 2024. We have previously written that cervical cancer could become the first type of cancer to be completely eliminated. Every year, more than 660,000 women worldwide get cervical cancer. More than 90 percent of the cases and deaths occur in low- and middle-income countries. According to Gavi, South Africa has one of the world's highest burdens of the disease. analysis.location_and_population: South Africa, 17- and 18-year-old girls, including those with HIV.
analysis.event: A significant reduction in the prevalence of high-risk HPV types 16 and 18 among vaccinated and unvaccinated girls, with a 83% decrease overall.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The prevalence of HPV types 16 and 18 fell from 21.6% in 2019 to 3.2% in 2023 among vaccinated girls, and from 29.4% to 4.4% among girls with HIV. The study involved 2,357 girls from four provinces in South Africa.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study was conducted by researchers from Wits RHI and the Kirby Institute, and the results are published in The Lancet Global Health. The program has shown success in reducing HPV prevalence, but further investigation is ongoing.

analysis.brief_en: A study in The Lancet Global Health shows that the prevalence of high-risk HPV types 16 and 18 among 17- and 18-year-old girls in South Africa has significantly decreased from 21.6% in 2019 to 3.2% in 2023. Among girls with HIV, the decrease was from 29.4% to 4.4%. The vaccination program, which began in 2014 and provides free HPV vaccines in public schools, has been highly effective, even reducing HPV prevalence among unvaccinated girls by 74%. This is the first time such a reduction has been shown at the population level.

“畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Review Open access ## 摘要### 研究背景高危型人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)的持续性感染是宫颈癌及多种其他上皮恶性肿瘤的重要病因学基础。因此,深入剖析HPV早期的进入过程和细胞内转运,对于寻找阻断HPV感染的新靶点至关重要。### 主要内容HPV的进入并非由单一受体介导的线性过程,而是一个跨越基底膜(BM)/细胞外基质(ECM)、质膜、内体、高尔基体相关区室以及细胞核的多步骤转运网络。在研究相对充分的HPV16及假病毒(PsV)模型中,HPV病毒粒子可被与BM/ECM相关及位于细胞表面的附着因子捕获并发生初始附着,其中包括层粘连蛋白-332(LN332)和硫酸乙酰肝素蛋白聚糖(HSPGs)。随后,宿主因子如亲环蛋白B(CyPB)和弗林蛋白酶参与衣壳构象预激活、L2氨基端暴露以及弗林蛋白酶介导的L2切割,从而为病毒粒子从初始附着过渡至进入平台的组装创造条件。整合素/黏着斑激酶(FAK)信号传导、富四跨膜蛋白微区(TEMs)、膜联蛋白A2/S100A10异四聚体(A2t)以及细胞骨架相关调控因子,均被认为参与进入平台的组织、非典型内吞和早期细胞内转运;但其作用环节及依赖程度可能因HPV型别、细胞模型和实验体系而异。病毒粒子进入内体系统后,γ-分泌酶介导的L2膜插入、Retromer/Retriever介导的逆行转运,以及由囊泡包裹且依赖有丝分裂的核内进入过程,被认为有助于将L2/病毒DNA(vDNA)复合物递送至细胞核。### 简短结论本综述总结了HPV进入过程中涉及的关键宿主因子、膜平台、非典型内吞途径、内体分选事件、逆行转运通路及核内进入过程,并讨论了它们作为HPV感染早期干预靶点的潜在价值。## 摘要### 研究背景高危型人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)的持续性感染是宫颈癌及多种其他上皮恶性肿瘤的重要病因学基础。因此,深入剖析HPV早期的进入过程和细胞内转运,对于寻找阻断HPV感染的新靶点至关重要。### 主要内容HPV的进入并非由单一受体介导的线性过程,而是一个跨越基底膜(BM)/细胞外基质(ECM)、质膜、内体、高尔基体相关区室以及细胞核的多步骤转运网络。在研究相对充分的HPV16及假病毒(PsV)模型中,HPV病毒粒子可被与BM/ECM相关及位于细胞表面的附着因子捕获并发生初始附着,其中包括层粘连蛋白-332(LN332)和硫酸乙酰肝素蛋白聚糖(HSPGs)。随后,宿主因子如亲环蛋白B(CyPB)和弗林蛋白酶参与衣壳构象预激活、L2氨基端暴露以及弗林蛋白酶介导的L2切割,从而为病毒粒子从初始附着过渡至进入平台的组装创造条件。整合素/黏着斑激酶(FAK)信号传导、富四跨膜蛋白微区(TEMs)、膜联蛋白A2/S100A10异四聚体(A2t)以及细胞骨架相关调控因子,均被认为参与进入平台的组织、非典型内吞和早期细胞内转运;但其作用环节及依赖程度可能因HPV型别、细胞模型和实验体系而异。病毒粒子进入内体系统后,γ-分泌酶介导的L2膜插入、Retromer/Retriever介导的逆行转运,以及由囊泡包裹且依赖有丝分裂的核内进入过程,被认为有助于将L2/病毒DNA(vDNA)复合物递送至细胞核。### 简短结论本综述总结了HPV进入过程中涉及的关键宿主因子、膜平台、非典型内吞途径、内体分选事件、逆行转运通路及核内进入过程,并讨论了它们作为HPV感染早期干预靶点的潜在价值。 打赏 展开全文 开通VIP 享海量文章 全站开放获取+解锁超过 200万篇新闻全文+每日更新 2000+篇,学术前沿动态全时追踪! news.content: 推荐 观点 时政 湖北 武汉 世相 环球 专题 极客圈 经济 城建 科教 健康 悠游 相亲 汽车 房产 消费 创意 文化 体育 娱乐 影像 帅作文 International 职教院 酒道 登录 | 极目新闻客户端 推荐 观点 时政 湖北 武汉 世相 环球 专题 极客圈 经济 城建 科教 健康 悠游 相亲 汽车 房产 消费 创意 文化 体育 娱乐 影像 帅作文 International 职教院 酒道 湖北过半适龄女性接种HPV疫苗 湖北日报 2026-11-26 21:26:07 阅读量: 湖北日报全媒记者余瑾毅 11月25日,大学生小王(化姓)在湖北省妇幼保健院完成了首剂进口九价HPV疫苗接种。HPV疫苗纳入国家免疫规划一年来,我省逐步形成免费接种保障基础、惠民减免回应多元需求的接种模式,覆盖适龄女孩并向更广泛人群延伸。截至11月24日,全省HPV疫苗首剂累计接种217483剂次,全省HPV疫苗首剂接种覆盖率67.39%。 接种疫苗的女孩 我国宫颈癌发病率呈上升趋势,防控关口在于“早” 近年来,我国宫颈癌发病率呈上升趋势,宫颈癌发病年龄呈现年轻化趋势。湖北省妇幼保健院妇科首席专家、湖北省宫颈癌防治中心主任吴绪峰介绍,HPV即人乳头瘤病毒,超过99%的宫颈癌都和高危型HPV的持续感染相关。在中国,常见的感染型别为HPV16、52、58三种。 HPV的主要传播途径是通过皮肤、黏膜或体液直接接触传播,其中性接触是最常见的传播方式。“需要说明的是,并非只有发生性行为才会感染,只要存在皮肤黏膜的直接接触,理论上就存在感染风险。” 幸运的是,宫颈癌也是一种可以预防的癌症,有成熟的三级预防体系。吴绪峰说,一级预防包括健康教育+HPV疫苗接种,接种疫苗是核心手段。二级预防指适龄女性定期筛查+癌前病变规范管理。三级预防是宫颈癌确诊后的规范治疗与康复,属于筛查失守后的补救手段。 “需要提醒的是,很多人认为身体没有不适,就不需要做筛查。现实中,从未参加筛查的女性,一旦出现出血症状再来就诊,往往已是局部晚期宫颈癌。”吴绪峰说。 2025年11月10日起,我国将HPV疫苗正式纳入国家免疫规划,为2011年11月10日以后出生、年满13周岁的女孩免费接种二价HPV疫苗,全程2剂次。 武汉市疾病预防控制中心免疫规划所副主任医师许慧琼表示,这能显著降低未来宫颈癌及其癌前病变的发病率,也能有效缩小城乡、区域和群体间的健康差距。同时大家也可以根据自身需求,自费选择九价HPV疫苗。 惠民减免覆盖更广人群,“男女共防”很重要 目前,除免疫规划疫苗免费为适龄女孩提供外,还有多种非免疫规划HPV疫苗供受种者自愿、自费接种。我省多地在落实国家免疫规划基础上,还通过地方惠民活动丰富了接种选择。 许慧琼详细介绍,武汉推出了进口九价HPV疫苗的限时优惠接种活动,覆盖了9-14岁的女孩,还有18—26岁的女性和男性,给家长和孩子多一个选择。 由中华医学会妇科肿瘤学分会等七个学会共同制定发布的《预防性人乳头瘤病毒疫苗中国临床应用指南(2025版)》,优先推荐9—26岁女性接种HPV疫苗,其中9—14岁女孩是重点人群;同时推荐27—45岁女性和9—26岁男性接种。 据悉,HPV感染并非女性“专属”,HPV感染对男女均有明确健康危害。高危型HPV感染引发阴茎癌、肛门癌、口咽癌。 “值得注意的是,很多男性感染后没有明显症状,属于无症状携带者,容易在不知情的情况下传染给伴侣。”吴绪峰说,HPV防控是全人群的公共卫生问题。 HPV感染可防可控,关键在于早接种早预防 在武汉市汉兴街第二社区卫生服务中心,负责人王星翘频繁遇到家长关于HPV疫苗的疑问。他说,很多人把HPV等同于性病,忽略了提前接种、尽早保护才是更有效的预防方式。其次,部分家长忽视了为男孩接种的重要性。 针对家长普遍关心的疫苗安全性问题,王星翘明确表示,HPV疫苗属于重组蛋白疫苗,只含有病毒外壳的蛋白质颗粒,不含病毒DNA,不含激素,不含任何影响生殖功能或生长发育的成分。全球数亿剂次的接种实践表明,没有证据显示接种HPV疫苗会影响生长发育或干扰内分泌系统。 世界卫生组织明确推荐,9-14岁未发生性行为的女孩是首要接种人群。9-14岁女孩接种后产生的抗体水平是15岁以上人群的2倍以上,保护效果可持续至少10年,仅需接种两剂即可获得长期保护。 王星翘表示,2011年11月10日以后出生、年满13周岁的女孩可免费接种二价HPV疫苗,能预防约70%的宫颈癌。对于希望获得更广泛保护的家庭,9-14岁女性及18-26岁男性和女性,知情自愿自费接种进口九价HPV疫苗,可享受6.7折优惠价格。他总结,HPV感染可防可控,关键在于“早接种、早预防、不恐慌、不拖延”。 责任编辑:张扬 相关新闻 极目新闻

source_language_evidence.brief_en: 推荐 观点 时政 湖北 武汉 世相 环球 专题 极客圈 经济 城建 科教 健康 悠游 相亲 汽车 房产 消费 创意 文化 体育 娱乐 影像 帅作文 International 职教院 酒道 登录 | 极目新闻客户端 推荐 观点 时政 湖北 武汉 世相 环球 专题 极客圈 经济 城建 科教 健康 悠游 相亲 汽车 房产 消费 创意 文化 体育 娱乐 影像 帅作文 International 职教院 酒道 湖北过半适龄女性接种HPV疫苗 湖北日报 2026-11-26 21:26:07 阅读量: 湖北日报全媒记者余瑾毅 11月25日,大学生小王(化姓)在湖北省妇幼保健院完成了首剂进口九价HPV疫苗接种。HPV疫苗纳入国家免疫规划一年来,我省逐步形成免费接种保障基础、惠民减免回应多元需求的接种模式,覆盖适龄女孩并向更广泛人群延伸。截至11月24日,全省HPV疫苗首剂累计接种217483剂次,全省HPV疫苗首剂接种覆盖率67.39%。 接种疫苗的女孩 我国宫颈癌发病率呈上升趋势,防控关口在于“早” 近年来,我国宫颈癌发病率呈上升趋势,宫颈癌发病年龄呈现年轻化趋势。湖北省妇幼保健院妇科首席专家、湖北省宫颈癌防治中心主任吴绪峰介绍,HPV即人乳头瘤病毒,超过99%的宫颈癌都和高危型HPV的持续感染相关。在中国,常见的感染型别为HPV16、52、58三种。 HPV的主要传播途径是通过皮肤、黏膜或体液直接接触传播,其中性接触是最常见的传播方式。“需要说明的是,并非只有发生性行为才会感染,只要存在皮肤黏膜的直接接触,理论上就存在感染风险。” 幸运的是,宫颈癌也是一种可以预防的癌症,有成熟的三级预防体系。吴绪峰说,一级预防包括健康教育+HPV疫苗接种,接种疫苗是核心手段。二级预防指适龄女性定期筛查+癌前病变规范管理。三级预防是宫颈癌确诊后的规范治疗与康复,属于筛查失守后的补救手段。 “需要提醒的是,很多人认为身体没有不适,就不需要做筛查。现实中,从未参加筛查的女性,一旦出现出血症状再来就诊,往往已是局部晚期宫颈癌。”吴绪峰说。 2025年11月10日起,我国将HPV疫苗正式纳入国家免疫规划,为2011年11月10日以后出生、年满13周岁的女孩免费接种二价HPV疫苗,全程2剂次。 武汉市疾病预防控制中心免疫规划所副主任医师许慧琼表示,这能显著降低未来宫颈癌及其癌前病变的发病率,也能有效缩小城乡、区域和群体间的健康差距。同时大家也可以根据自身需求,自费选择九价HPV疫苗。 惠民减免覆盖更广人群,“男女共防”很重要 目前,除免疫规划疫苗免费为适龄女孩提供外,还有多种非免疫规划HPV疫苗供受种者自愿、自费接种。我省多地在落实国家免疫规划基础上,还通过地方惠民活动丰富了接种选择。

news.content: DutchNews.nl - DutchNews.nl brings daily news from The Netherlands in English 28 November 2026 Newsletter Donate Advertise News Life in the Netherlands Jobs Partner content Podcast Advertise About us Search Home Economy Politics Art and culture Sport Europe Society Environment Health Housing Education News Home Economy Politics Art and culture Sport Europe Society Environment Health Housing Education Life in the Netherlands Latest Opinion Books Travel 10 Questions Learning Dutch Inburgering with DN Food & Drink Ask us anything Jobs Partner content Podcast Advertise About us Donate Team Advertise Contact us Writing for Dutch News Privacy Newsletter Search New HPV vaccine could save nearly 13,000 cancer diagnoses a year November 24, 2026 Photo: Depositphotos.com See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google Listen to this article 2 min Nearly 13,000 people could avoid a cancer diagnosis later in life if the Netherlands raises its HPV vaccination rate, new medical research has found. Children aged 10 are given two doses of the vaccine, which protects against a virus that causes cervical cancer in women. A new version introduced in September covers a wider range of cancers that affect both sexes, such as vaginal and penile cancers. Around 80% of people in the Netherlands contract the human papillomavirus, mainly though sexual activity. Most people who are infected have no symptoms, but persistent infection is responsible for around 99.7% of all cases of cervical cancer, one of the most common types in women. Every year 1,100 women and 400 men are diagnosed with a form cancer linked to HPV, most of whom are under the age of 45. Researchers at Erasmus Medical Centre in Rotterdam and the Dutch cancer centre IKNL said 12,800 diagnoses could be saved if the new vaccine is given to all children who reach the age of 10 in future. The Netherlands currently has a vaccination rate of 61% for the HPV vaccine, well below the World Health Organisation’s advisory rate of 90% for girls. Around 60% of boys have had the jab as well since the public health agency RIVM added it to their vaccine schedule in 2022. Gynaecologist and oncologist Luc van Lonkhuijsen, of Amsterdam’s university medical centre, said many parents were anxious about side effects or dismissed it as unimportant. “We have been vaccinating for 15 years and the number of side-effects we see is really very limited,” he told NOS. Our missions Governance Our academic partners Our work program Our publications News Thematic Files COVID-19 Pregnancy and Children EN FR AccueilRisk of Guillain-Barré syndrome following each dose of HPV vaccination ‌November 23rd, 2026 Risk of Guillain-Barré syndrome following each dose of HPV vaccination EPI-PHARE publishes an article in Vaccine Risk of Guillain-Barré syndrome following each dose of HPV vaccination: an 18-year nationwide self-controlled case series study Background Although the safety of human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccines has been largely established, the risk of Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) remains uncertain. This study aimed to assess the dose-specific risk of GBS following HPV vaccination, considering the whole population targeted by the national vaccination program in France. Methods Using data from the French National Health Data System (SNDS), a self-controlled case series (SCCS) study was conducted, including all individuals aged 10–29 years hospitalized with a diagnosis of GBS from 2007 to 2024. The relative incidence (RI) of GBS during the 42-day risk periods following each HPV vaccine dose compared to control periods was estimated, adjusting for other vaccinations, concomitant respiratory and gastrointestinal infections, age, and seasonality. The number of excess cases attributable to HPV vaccination was derived. Findings During the study period, 14.4 million (M) HPV vaccine doses (6.7 M first, 5.1 M second, 2.5 M third doses) were administered in a target population of 32.3 M individuals. Among 2604 GBS cases, 656 had received at least one dose of HPV vaccine, and 25 cases occurred within 42 days following HPV vaccination (9 after the first dose, 9 after the second, 7 after the third). No increase in GBS incidence was observed after the first vaccine dose (RI 1.29 [0.68–2.45]). In contrast, the incidence of GBS was increased after the second (RI 1.91 [1.01–3.60]) and third (RI 2.25 [1.06–4.79]) doses, a result consistent across sex, age subgroups and vaccine products. Accounting for the rarity of GBS, these relative increases resulted in 0.9 and 2.5 excess cases of GBS per million vaccinated individuals under a two-dose and three-dose schedule, respectively. Conclusion Although revealing a potentially heterogeneous risk profile across vaccine doses, this large study found no evidence of a substantial increase in the absolute risk of GBS following HPV vaccination, further confirming the safety of HPV vaccination. Article Dufour, L. et al. news.content_title: JAM3 and PAX1 Gene Methylation Tracks Cervical Lesion Severity in Hospital
news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Saturday, November 28, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Cancer JAM3 and PAX1 Gene Methylation Tracks Cervical Lesion Severity in Hospital Study by November 26, 2026 in Cancer, Health Reading Time: 5 mins read 0 JAM3 and PAX1 Gene Methylation Tracks Cervical Lesion Severity in Hospital Study Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A hospital-based investigation conducted at the Gynecologic Oncology Center of the Affiliated Cancer Hospital of Xinjiang Medical University has found that DNA methylation of host genes JAM3 and PAX1 is significantly associated with increasing histological severity of cervical lesions among women testing positive for high-risk human papillomavirus. Published in Frontiers in Oncology, the research examined cervical exfoliated cell samples to evaluate how epigenetic alterations correlate with disease stages ranging from normal tissue to invasive cervical cancer, while also assessing whether combining methylation testing with HPV16 and HPV18 genotyping could refine the detection of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or higher. Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus, or hrHPV, is established as the causative factor behind more than ninety percent of cervical cancer cases worldwide. Although primary screening programs relying on hrHPV testing provide substantial sensitivity for identifying viral presence, hrHPV positivity by itself fails to differentiate benign or transient infections from high-grade precancerous lesions, frequently precipitating unnecessary colposcopy referrals and repeat clinical follow-up visits. Liquid-based cytology is widely employed as a secondary triage method, but its reliance on morphological evaluation introduces challenges related to subjective interpretation and interobserver variability, driving the search for objective, reproducible molecular markers capable of improving risk stratification under international cervical cancer elimination initiatives. Discover more Hospital Check Symptoms Book a Checkup Host-cell DNA methylation has surfaced as a prominent molecular mechanism reflecting cellular transformation and progression toward malignancy. To rigorously investigate their clinical relevance, the research team designed a hospital-based observational study assessing treatment-negative women aged 25 years or older with confirmed baseline hrHPV positivity who presented with available JAM3 and PAX1 methylation measurements alongside definitive histopathological diagnoses. Discover more Order DNA Kits Study Biology Find Skin Care Find Cancer Care From an initial hospital cohort of 325 women evaluated between September 2024 and December 2025, investigators applied rigorous inclusion and exclusion criteria to isolate an untreated target population. Patients were excluded if they lacked definitive histopathological verification, had undergone a prior hysterectomy, or had received surgical or chemoradiotherapy interventions for cervical cancer before methylation testing. After removing 19 individuals without definitive histology, 4 with prior hysterectomies, and 97 who underwent testing only following cancer therapy, the primary analytical cohort comprised 205 treatment-negative women. Based on reference histopathology, the 205 participants were classified into five distinct groups: 5 normal cases, 51 cases of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 1, 36 cases of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2, 70 cases of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3, and 43 cases of invasive cervical cancer. Laboratory procedures combined commercial multiplex molecular diagnostics and standardized cytology systems. HPV testing identified 14 high-risk HPV types using PCR amplification and capillary electrophoresis fragment analysis, while liquid-based cytology was executed using the BD SurePath platform and evaluated according to the 2014 Bethesda System criteria by experienced cytologists working in a blinded manner. DNA methylation of PAX1 and JAM3 was quantified from exfoliated cervical cells using a commercial multiplex real-time PCR assay with fluorescent probes, utilizing GAPDH as an internal reference gene. Methylation positivity was defined by predefined cycle threshold differences, specifically a delta Ct of 6.6 or less for PAX1, a delta Ct of 10.0 or less for JAM3, or positivity in either gene to constitute an overall positive JAM3/PAX1 result. Across the entire cohort of 205 women, the overall positivity rate for combined JAM3/PAX1 methylation was 46.83 percent, representing 96 positive cases. Stratification across histological categories revealed a pronounced, statistically significant upward gradient: methylation positivity was recorded at 20.00 percent in the normal histopathology group, rising to 23.53 percent in CIN1, 33.33 percent in CIN2, 61.43 percent in CIN3, and reaching 65.12 percent among women diagnosed with cervical cancer. The Cochran-Armitage trend test confirmed this progressive escalation across advancing lesion severity with a chi-square value of 24.51 and a significance value of P less than 0.001. Age-stratified analyses among the 205 participants evaluated lesion severity and biomarker positivity across four distinct age bands: younger than 40 years, 40 to 49 years, 50 to 59 years, and 60 years or older. While overall methylation positivity rates showed statistically significant differences across these age brackets—registering at 32.73 percent, 50.85 percent, 58.06 percent, and 41.38 percent, respectively—the Cochran-Armitage test indicated no significant linear trend with advancing age. Histopathological grade distributions also varied significantly by age, reflecting distinct disease burdens within the hospital-based clinical sample. Discover more cancer Cancer See an OB-GYN Find Hospitals hospital To evaluate independent risk associations and diagnostic accuracy, the researchers conducted detailed multivariable modeling within a complete-data subset of 105 participants who possessed full records for HPV genotyping, cytology, methylation, and histopathology. Within this subset, 14 women had lesions classified as CIN1 or normal, 20 had CIN2, 53 had CIN3, and 18 had cervical cancer. Genotype analysis demonstrated that HPV16 was the most prevalent strain at 59.05 percent, followed by HPV52 at 14.29 percent, HPV58 at 13.33 percent, and HPV18 at 6.67 percent. HPV16/18 positivity rose across severity stages from 28.57 percent in the sub-CIN2 group to 77.78 percent in cervical cancer, displaying a significant linear trend. In the ordinal logistic regression model adjusted for concurrent diagnostic tests, JAM3/PAX1 methylation positivity was independently associated with higher cervical lesion grades, yielding an adjusted odds ratio of 5.02 with a 95 percent confidence interval of 2.15 to 11.77. HPV16/18 positivity was likewise independently associated with increased lesion severity, demonstrating an adjusted odds ratio of 3.88 and a 95 percent confidence interval of 1.75 to 8.60. Conversely, positive liquid-based cytology findings of atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance or higher showed no statistically significant independent association with histological severity in this adjusted model, displaying an odds ratio of 0.95 with a 95 percent confidence interval spanning 0.42 to 2.15. Diagnostic accuracy evaluations for detecting CIN2 or worse highlighted marked operational differences between standalone and combined testing modalities. Standalone HPV16/18 genotyping achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.692, with a sensitivity of 67.03 percent and a specificity of 71.43 percent. Standalone JAM3/PAX1 methylation produced an area under the curve of 0.676, with 63.74 percent sensitivity and 71.43 percent specificity. Combining both tests through a parallel testing strategy—where positivity for either marker defined a positive screen—boosted sensitivity to 86.81 percent, but reduced specificity to 50.00 percent, generating a test-positive rate of 81.90 percent. In contrast, sequential testing requiring positivity on both assays maximized specificity at 92.86 percent and achieved a positive predictive value of 97.56 percent, though sensitivity dropped to 43.96 percent. The authors emphasized several methodological constraints inherent to the study design. Because the investigation was performed within a single tertiary cancer hospital, the enrolled cohort was clinically enriched with high-grade lesions and cancer cases, limiting direct extrapolation to unselected primary screening populations. Furthermore, the complete diagnostic subset contained 91 cases of CIN2+ and only 14 cases below CIN2, an imbalance that heavily influences specificity and predictive value metrics, particularly the elevated positive predictive value seen in sequential testing. Finally, because the investigation utilized a cross-sectional assessment of existing lesions rather than longitudinal follow-up, the observed associations do not demonstrate an ability to predict prospective disease progression, underscoring the need for large multicenter prospective trials to clarify the clinical triage utility of JAM3 and PAX1 methylation. Discover more Order DNA Kits Study Biology Find Skin Care Find Cancer Care From an initial hospital cohort of 325 women evaluated between September 2024 and December 2025, investigators applied rigorous inclusion and exclusion criteria to isolate an untreated target population. Patients were excluded if they lacked definitive histopathological verification, had undergone a prior hysterectomy, or had received surgical or chemoradiotherapy interventions for cervical cancer before methylation testing. After removing 19 individuals without definitive histology, 4 with prior hysterectomies, and 97 who underwent testing only following cancer therapy, the primary analytical cohort comprised 205 treatment-negative women. Based on reference histopathology, the 205 participants were classified into five distinct groups: 5 normal cases, 51 cases of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 1, 36 cases of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2, 70 cases of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3, and 43 cases of invasive cervical cancer. Laboratory procedures combined commercial multiplex molecular diagnostics and standardized cytology systems. HPV testing identified 14 high-risk HPV types using PCR amplification and capillary electrophoresis fragment analysis, while liquid-based cytology was executed using the BD SurePath platform and evaluated according to the 2014 Bethesda System criteria by experienced cytologists working in a blinded manner. DNA methylation of PAX1 and JAM3 was quantified from exfoliated cervical cells using a commercial multiplex real-time PCR assay with fluorescent probes, utilizing GAPDH as an internal reference gene. Methylation positivity was defined by predefined cycle threshold differences, specifically a delta Ct of 6.6 or less for PAX1, a delta Ct of 10.0 or less for JAM3, or positivity in either gene to constitute an overall positive JAM3/PAX1 result. Across the entire cohort of 205 women, the overall positivity rate for combined JAM3/PAX1 methylation was 46.83 percent, representing 96 positive cases. Stratification across histological categories revealed a pronounced, statistically significant upward gradient: methylation positivity was recorded at 20.00 percent in the normal histopathology group, rising to 23.53 percent in CIN1, 33.33 percent in CIN2, 61.43 percent in CIN3, and reaching 65.12 percent among women diagnosed with cervical cancer. The Cochran-Armitage trend test confirmed this progressive escalation across advancing lesion severity with a chi-square value of 24.51 and a significance value of P less than 0.001. Age-stratified analyses among the 205 participants evaluated lesion severity and biomarker positivity across four distinct age bands: younger than 40 years, 40 to 49 years, 50 to 59 years, and 60 years or older. While overall methylation positivity rates showed statistically significant differences across these age brackets—registering at 32.73 percent, 50.85 percent, 58.06 percent, and 41.38 percent, respectively—the Cochran-Armitage test indicated no significant linear trend with advancing age. Histopathological grade distributions also varied significantly by age, reflecting distinct disease burdens within the hospital-based clinical sample. Discover more cancer Cancer See an OB-GYN Find Hospitals hospital To evaluate independent risk associations and diagnostic accuracy, the researchers conducted detailed multivariable modeling within a complete-data subset of 105 participants who possessed full records for HPV genotyping, cytology, methylation, and histopathology. Within this subset, 14 women had lesions classified as CIN1 or normal, 20 had CIN2, 53 had CIN3, and 18 had cervical cancer. Genotype analysis demonstrated that HPV16 was the most prevalent strain at 59.05 percent, followed by HPV52 at 14.29 percent, HPV58 at 13.33 percent, and HPV18 at 6.67 percent. HPV16/18 positivity rose across severity stages from 28.57 percent in the sub-CIN2 group to 77.78 percent in cervical cancer, displaying a significant linear trend. In the ordinal logistic regression model adjusted for concurrent diagnostic tests, JAM3/PAX1 methylation positivity was independently associated with higher cervical lesion grades, yielding an adjusted odds ratio of 5.02 with a 95 percent confidence interval of 2.15 to 11.77. HPV16/18 positivity was likewise independently associated with increased lesion severity, demonstrating an adjusted odds ratio of 3.88 and a 95 percent confidence interval of 1.75 to 8.60. Conversely, positive liquid-based cytology findings of atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance or higher showed no statistically significant independent association with histological severity in this adjusted model, displaying an odds ratio of 0.95 with a 95 percent confidence interval spanning 0.42 to 2.15. Diagnostic accuracy evaluations for detecting CIN2 or worse highlighted marked operational differences between standalone and combined testing modalities. Standalone HPV16/18 genotyping achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.692, with a sensitivity of 67.03 percent and a specificity of 71.43 percent. Standalone JAM3/PAX1 methylation produced an area under the curve of 0.676, with 63.74 percent sensitivity and 71.43 percent specificity. Combining both tests through a parallel testing strategy—where positivity for either marker defined a positive screen—boosted sensitivity to 86.81 percent, but reduced specificity to 50.00 percent, generating a test-positive rate of 81.90 percent. In contrast, sequential testing requiring positivity on both assays maximized specificity at 92.86 percent and achieved a positive predictive value of 97.56 percent, though sensitivity dropped to 43.96 percent. The authors emphasized several methodological constraints inherent to the study design. Because the investigation was performed within a single tertiary cancer hospital, the enrolled cohort was clinically enriched with high-grade lesions and cancer cases, limiting direct extrapolation to unselected primary screening populations. Furthermore, the complete diagnostic subset contained 91 cases of CIN2+ and only 14 cases below CIN2, an imbalance that heavily influences specificity and predictive value metrics, particularly the elevated positive predictive value seen in sequential testing. Finally, because the investigation utilized a cross-sectional assessment of existing lesions rather than longitudinal follow-up, the observed associations do not demonstrate an ability to predict prospective disease progression, underscoring the need for large multicenter prospective trials to clarify the clinical triage utility of JAM3 and PAX1 methylation. analysis.brief_en: A hospital-based study conducted at the Gynecologic Oncology Center of the Affiliated Cancer Hospital of Xinjiang Medical University found that DNA methylation of host genes JAM3 and PAX1 is significantly associated with increasing histological severity of cervical lesions among women with high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) infections. The research, published on November 26, 2026, evaluated 205 treatment-negative women aged 25 or older, classified into five histological groups: normal tissue, cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) grades 1-3, and invasive cervical cancer. Methylation positivity rates rose from 20% in normal cases to 65.12% in cervical cancer, with HPV16 being the most prevalent strain. The study highlights the potential of JAM3/PAX1 methylation as an objective biomarker for improving risk stratification in cervical cancer detection, as standalone HPV16/18 genotyping showed limited diagnostic accuracy compared to combined methylation testing. The findings suggest a need for further research to integrate these molecular markers into clinical practice for better patient outcomes.

news.content: 新闻 体育 汽车 房产 旅游 教育 时尚 科技 财经 娱乐 HPV疫苗系列科普(十一)| HPV疫苗≠只防宫颈癌!这些疾病也能抵挡 2026-11-24 16:36 来源: 中部城市生活指南 发布于:北京市 提起HPV疫苗,很多人的第一印象就是“宫颈癌疫苗”。不少人认为,它的作用仅仅是保护宫颈。事实上,HPV病毒不只是会感染宫颈,还可以感染外阴、阴道、肛门、口腔、咽喉、阴茎等多处黏膜皮肤,持续感染后可能诱发多种病变和癌症。HPV疫苗的防护范围远比大家想象的更广,是一种面向男女都有健康收益的疫苗。 HPV是什么? 人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)是一类主要感染人体皮肤和黏膜上皮的球形DNA病毒,大约有200多种亚型。大多数HPV感染是无症状的,可自行消除,但持续感染HPV可能导致疾病发生。研究显示,在至少有一名异性伴侣的人群中,女性一生中感染HPV的概率为84.6%,男性为91.3%[1]。 HPV的致病性 HPV依据其致癌潜力可分为高危型和低危型两大类。 在高危型HPV中, 16型和18型是致癌能力最强的两个亚型,大约造成全球70%的宫颈癌,同时还可能诱发阴道癌、肛门癌、阴茎癌等多种恶性肿瘤。 低危型HPV通常引起良性病变,常见的型别有6型和11型,占生殖器疣病因的90%[2]。 HPV疫苗分为哪几种? 可以预防哪些疾病? 二价HPV疫苗(16、18型): 可预防约70%宫颈癌,也可预防由16、18型 HPV病毒导致的外阴癌、阴道癌、肛门癌、口咽癌、阴茎癌以及对应的癌前病变。 四价HPV疫苗(6、11、16、18型): 可预防约70%宫颈癌+90%生殖器疣。拥有二价全部防护能力,额外预防尖锐湿疣、复发性呼吸道乳头状瘤病。 九价HPV疫苗(6、11、16、18、31、33、45、52、58型): 可预防约90%宫颈癌+90%生殖器疣。覆盖范围最广,在四价HPV疫苗的基础上增加5种高危亚型,能预防更多HPV相关恶性肿瘤。 避开常见误区 错误 HPV只通过性接触传播。 正确 性接触传播是最常见的传播途径;也可通过密切接触,如皮肤直接接触被病毒污染的物品或共用毛巾、浴巾、浴缸等感染;还存在母婴传播,如分娩经产道时传染给婴儿。 展开全文 错误 接种HPV疫苗会影响怀孕。 正确 HPV疫苗是重组蛋白疫苗,不含活病毒,不会损伤卵巢和输卵管,不会降低怀孕概率。 错误 已经有性生活/已经查出HPV阳性就不能接种HPV疫苗。 正确 可以接种,对还没有感染的亚型依然有保护作用。 错误 接种完疫苗就不用再做宫颈癌筛查。 正确 疫苗不能覆盖全部致癌HPV亚型:无论接种几价疫苗,女性到适龄之后都要定期做宫颈癌TCT(液基薄层细胞学检测)/HPV筛查。 错误 只有女性需要接种HPV疫苗。 正确 肛门癌、口咽癌、阴茎癌、尖锐湿疣等疾病男性同样会中招,男性接种HPV疫苗既能保护自己,也能减少病毒传给伴侣的概率。 HPV疫苗不只是“宫颈癌专属疫苗”,它可以预防HPV病毒家族带来的多种疾病。比起盲目观望等待,尽早接种才是最重要的原则。结合自身需求选择合适的疫苗,再配合定期筛查,才能建立起完整可靠的健康保护屏障。 参考文献: [1] Chesson H W, Dunne E F, Hariri S, et al. The Estimated Lifetime Probability of Acquiring Human Papilonmavirus in the United Dtetes[J]. Sexually Transmitted Diseases, 2014, 41(11): 660-664. [2] 中华预防医学会,中华预防医学会疫苗与免疫分会. 子宫颈癌等人乳头瘤病毒相关疾病免疫预防专家共识(2025年版)[J]. 中国预防医学杂志, 2025, 26(7): 775-812.返回搜狐,查看更多 阅读 () 平台声明 该文观点仅代表作者本人,搜狐号系信息发布平台,搜狐仅提供信息存储空间服务。
