supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Saturday, November 28, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Cancer Natural HPV16 Capsid Variants Show Reduced Sensitivity to Standard Vaccines by November 24, 2026 in Cancer Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Natural HPV16 Capsid Variants Show Reduced Sensitivity to Standard Vaccines Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A comprehensive laboratory evaluation of naturally occurring variants of human papillomavirus type 16 has demonstrated that specific amino acid substitutions in the major capsid protein L1 can destabilize virion assembly and significantly diminish neutralization by vaccine-induced human antibodies. Published in the journal Tumour Virus Research, the experimental study systematically examined how the natural genetic diversification of the HPV16 L1 protein influences the physical formation of pseudovirus particles, the capacity of those particles to infect host cells, and their vulnerability to serum antibodies elicited by three standard prophylactic vaccines: the bivalent Cervarix, the quadrivalent Gardasil, and the nonavalent Gardasil-9 formulations. By combining computational structural modeling, in vitro pseudovirus assays, molecular dynamics simulations, and phylogenetic selection analyses, the research team established that while several naturally circulating variants assemble normally and infect human epithelial cell lines efficiently, specific variants exhibit substantial reductions in susceptibility to vaccine-mediated antibody neutralization, driven by weakened antibody-antigen binding avidity. Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus types represents the primary etiological contributor to multiple malignancies, posing a profound global threat to women’s health. Cervical cancer ranks as the fourth most common cancer among women worldwide, with the World Health Organization recording an estimated 660,000 incident cases and 348,000 fatalities in 2022. Among high-risk types, HPV16 is responsible for more than fifty percent of all cervical cancer cases globally. Current prophylactic HPV vaccines are constructed using recombinant virus-like particles composed of the major capsid protein L1, which naturally self-assembles into pentameric capsomeres that form the outer virion shell. Although the double-stranded DNA virus evolves at a relatively constant rate and the L1 protein is considered relatively conserved, natural sequence variations can alter capsomere architecture, viral infectivity, and surface loop conformations. Because the principal neutralizing epitopes recognized by host antibodies reside within five surface-exposed hypervariable loops designated as BC, DE, EF, FG, and HI, amino acid substitutions within these regions have the potential to compromise antibody recognition and permit immune evasion. To investigate the extent of natural variation across circulating viral lineages, the investigators retrieved 1,437 complete or near-complete HPV16 L1 protein sequences with completeness exceeding 85 percent from the National Center for Biotechnology Information database. Using CD-HIT clustering to remove redundant entries, they consolidated the repository into 228 unique L1 amino acid sequences, which were subsequently aligned using the Clustal Omega algorithm implemented within UGENE software. Maximum likelihood phylogenetic reconstruction executed with IQ-TREE categorized these 228 unique sequences into four major evolutionary clades comprising fourteen distinct clusters. The consensus amino acid sequence derived from each cluster was confirmed to exist naturally in circulating populations. The consensus sequence matching accession P03101 in the UniProt database was designated as the reference wild-type construct, P16_WT, representing the most prevalent lineage at 49.8 percent of analyzed sequences. The remaining thirteen clusters, designated P16_1 through P16_13, ranged in natural prevalence from 0.07 percent to substantial frequencies, displaying branched divergence around the reference wild type across the phylogenetic tree. Comparative sequence analysis between the wild-type reference and the thirteen variant consensus sequences revealed a total of thirty distinct amino acid substitution sites distributed throughout the length of the L1 polypeptide chain. Structural mapping onto the assembled pentameric capsomere demonstrated that ten of these mutated residues mapped directly onto surface-exposed neutralizing epitope loops, exhibiting particular concentration across the EF, FG, and HI loops, whereas the BC and DE loops remained comparatively invariant. The remaining twenty mutation sites localized within relatively conserved structural framework regions of the viral capsomere. To evaluate the biophysical consequences of these mutations prior to laboratory synthesis, the researchers performed FoldX energy calculations across crystallographic datasets of L1 monomers, pentamers, and antibody-bound complexes. The free energy calculations predicted that variants P16_2, P16_3, P16_4, and P16_8 possessed positive free energy changes relative to wild type, indicating thermodynamic destabilization of the monomer or pentameric assemblies, whereas most predictions for P16_5 and P16_6 also indicated elevated free energy, while the remaining variants exhibited negative free energy shifts suggestive of maintained or enhanced structural stability. To empirically test particle assembly and infectivity, the authors synthesized codon-optimized variant L1 genes and inserted them into modified mammalian expression vectors along with the wild-type L2 gene and a green fluorescent protein reporter plasmid, cotransfecting human embryonic kidney 293FT cells to generate pseudovirions. Consistent with the biophysical FoldX predictions, variants P16_2, P16_3, P16_4, and P16_8 completely failed to assemble into infectious pseudovirus particles, generating zero detectable viral titers and revealing no recognizable capsids under negative-stain transmission electron microscopy. Variant P16_1 successfully assembled but yielded an extremely suppressed pseudovirus titer. Western blot analysis of whole-cell lysates conducted before and after a twenty-four-hour maturation period in hypertonic sodium chloride revealed that although all variants produced L1 protein to varying degrees before maturation, L1 protein in the four non-forming variants and P16_1 was undetectable or sharply diminished following maturation. In contrast, the remaining eight variants and the reference wild type assembled high-titer pseudoviruses with intact morphology, showing equivalent packaging capacity and demonstrating indistinguishable infectivity when titrated onto human HeLa and 293FT epithelial cultures. The eight successfully assembled high-titer variants along with the wild-type reference were subsequently evaluated in pseudovirus-based neutralization assays using human sera collected from individuals under fifty years of age who had completed standard three-dose immunization regimens with Cervarix (27 participants), Gardasil (26 participants), or Gardasil-9 (29 participants). Blood samples were drawn primarily within one month following the final vaccine dose. Neutralization titers against the reference wild-type strain showed slight numerical variations across the three vaccine cohorts, but these differences did not reach statistical significance, verifying that all three vaccines established robust baseline neutralizing titers against the standard HPV16 L1 antigen. However, when tested against the natural variants, marked differences in neutralization susceptibility emerged across the vaccine cohorts, uncovering distinct patterns of antibody escape and resilience that depended on both the specific viral mutational profile and the valency of the vaccine administered. Neutralizing titers against the assembled variants demonstrated that Cervarix-induced antibodies experienced significant reductions in neutralization efficacy against four variants: P16_5, P16_11, P16_12, and P16_13. The loss of inhibitory potency was most pronounced against P16_12 and P16_13, where neutralizing capacity fell to approximately 70 percent and 50 percent of that observed against the wild-type reference, respectively. Sera from individuals vaccinated with Gardasil likewise exhibited significantly diminished neutralization against P16_5, P16_12, and P16_13, dropping to roughly 60 percent of wild-type levels against P16_13, although Gardasil sera maintained full neutralization potency against P16_11, effectively compensating for the deficiency observed with Cervarix. In contrast, sera from Gardasil-9 recipients demonstrated broader resilience, successfully restoring neutralizing activity against P16_12 and improving the neutralization of P16_13 to approximately 80 percent of wild-type levels. Nevertheless, both P16_5 and P16_13 retained significant resistance across all three vaccines, maintaining reduced sensitivity even in the presence of multi-valent vaccine sera. To elucidate the structural and physical mechanisms responsible for the diminished neutralization of P16_5 and P16_13, the investigators conducted fifty-nanosecond all-atom molecular dynamics simulations using GROMACS with the CHARMM36m force field, modeling the variants in complex with the neutralizing monoclonal antibody Fab fragment H16.001 under physiological aqueous conditions. While the overall volume of the antigen-antibody complexes remained unchanged across variants and the minimum interatomic distances exhibited only minor shifts, root-mean-square deviation and root-mean-square fluctuation analyses demonstrated markedly heightened dynamic fluctuations in the antibody complexes formed with P16_5 and P16_13 compared to wild type, pointing to pronounced structural instability at the binding interface. These computational predictions were validated experimentally through modified enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays employing guanidine hydrochloride chaotropic elution to determine the avidity index of L1-specific serum IgG antibodies. The assays confirmed that polyclonal antibodies induced by all three vaccines bound to P16_5 and P16_13 with significantly lower avidity than to the reference wild type, demonstrating that accelerated complex dissociation impairs viral neutralization. To ascertain whether these immune-evading mutations emerged in response to vaccine deployment or through ancestral evolutionary processes, the authors performed positive selection analyses across the 228 unique L1 sequences by calculating nonsynonymous to synonymous substitution rate ratios using HyPhy software. The adaptive branch-site random effects likelihood model identified positive selection operating on 3.1 percent of phylogenetic branches. Furthermore, four discrete evolutionary models—MEME, FUBAR, FEL, and SLAC—concordantly confirmed that specific amino acid sites had undergone statistically significant positive selection. Specifically, residue N181, which is carried by variant P16_13, and residue A266, carried by variant P16_5, demonstrated robust evidence of positive selection across the predictive algorithms. Crucially, archival records show that P16_5 and P16_13 were isolated in 1994 and 1996, respectively, preceding the clinical introduction of the first prophylactic HPV vaccine in 2006. This chronological evidence proves that these mutational profiles evolved through natural, long-term adaptive host-pathogen interactions entirely independent of vaccine-induced selective pressure. The study highlights significant epidemiological implications, noting that variants P16_5 and P16_13 collectively account for approximately 17 percent of global HPV16 L1 prevalence in circulating populations. Sequence comparisons from P16_9 through P16_13 identified a recurring mutational signature spanning substitutions from H76Y to L474F, including T176N and T353P, suggesting that cumulative structural alterations across multiple surface residues drive antibody resistance rather than isolated point mutations. Discussing study limitations, the authors observed that while four variants failed to assemble pseudoviruses due to defective L1 expression or stability in human embryonic kidney cells, these sequences originated from cervical cancer biopsies where viral integration or unexamined interactions with native L2 variants might yield different biological behaviors in natural settings. Because current L1 virus-like particle vaccines remain indispensable for controlling cervical cancer and broader valency formulations provide enhanced cross-neutralization, the researchers concluded that sustained molecular surveillance of naturally circulating L1 variants is vital to anticipate ongoing evolutionary divergence and inform the composition of next-generation broad-spectrum vaccines. supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Saturday, November 28, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Cancer Inhibiting CDK5 and HPV18 E6 Interaction Suppresses Cervical Cancer Cell Growth by November 23, 2026 in Cancer Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Inhibiting CDK5 and HPV18 E6 Interaction Suppresses Cervical Cancer Cell Growth Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Persistent infection by high-risk types of human papillomavirus represents the primary causative factor in cervical cancer, which ranks as the fourth most common cancer diagnosed among women globally. Although regular clinical screening and surgical intervention provide reliable disease prevention in regions with developed health infrastructure, the overall global burden has remained high, particularly across low- and middle-income countries where financial resources and vaccination access continue to be constrained. Among more than four hundred identified viral genotypes, thirteen are classified as high-risk variants, with types 16 and 18 together responsible for more than seventy percent of all invasive cervical malignancies. During persistent infection and neoplastic progression, viral DNA integrates into the human genome, resulting in sustained overexpression of viral early oncoproteins designated E6 and E7. Historically, research has emphasized the capacity of E6 to recruit the ubiquitin ligase E6-associated protein to degrade the host tumor suppressor p53, while E7 targets the retinoblastoma protein pRB. However, identifying host cellular factors that directly bind viral oncoproteins to reinforce their stability represents a critical frontier for targeted oncology. In a newly reported study, investigators explored how host cyclin-dependent kinase 5, an enzyme traditionally characterized for its multifunctional regulatory roles in neuronal migration, survival, and differentiation within the central nervous system, interfaces with high-risk human papillomavirus oncoproteins. While earlier broad gene expression analyses drawn from public cancer databases demonstrated increased messenger RNA levels of the kinase in cervical squamous cell carcinoma and ovarian cancers compared to normal tissue, these repositories did not stratify samples by viral status. To resolve this question experimentally, the researchers examined baseline protein abundance across a panel of cultured human cell lines. Immunoblotting demonstrated that the kinase was expressed at significantly higher levels in human papillomavirus-positive cervical cancer models, including HeLa cells expressing type 18 and CaSki cells harboring type 16, relative to virus-null controls such as immortalized HGK12 primary gingival keratinocytes and tongue squamous cell carcinoma lines SAS and UPCI:SCC025. This observation provided direct initial evidence that high-risk viral oncoproteins correspond with elevated host kinase expression. To investigate whether a physical complex forms between the host enzyme and viral factors, researchers conducted in vitro protein-protein interaction assays. Scansite computational modeling first predicted that human papillomavirus E6 contains potential consensus motif sequences recognized by the kinase. Subsequent glutathione S-transferase pull-down experiments and co-immunoprecipitation assays using transfected human embryonic kidney 293 cell extracts confirmed that the host kinase forms stable physical complexes with both viral proteins. Quantitative measurements revealed that the kinase bound significantly more readily to E6 than to E7, displaying a marked preference for type 18 E6 over type 16 E6, with relative binding values measured at 1.343 ± 0.04749 compared to 0.8133 ± 0.02427. Immunofluorescence microscopy performed in virus-negative osteosarcoma U-2 OS cells further confirmed that the kinase and viral E6 proteins colocalize predominantly within the nuclear compartment. This nuclear assembly took place without altering the natural subcellular distribution of the host enzyme, establishing that the interaction represents an authentic intracellular event occurring inside the cell nucleus. Further biochemical experiments revealed a reciprocal, mutualistic relationship governing the abundance of both proteins within the cell. Transient gene expression experiments in embryonic kidney cells using escalating plasmid ratios demonstrated that increasing kinase transfection from one to four micrograms elevated type 18 E6 protein levels by 5.25 ± 0.98-fold at a four-to-two ratio. Conversely, increasing viral oncoprotein expression elevated kinase abundance by 1.78 ± 0.23-fold at a one-to-two ratio and by 2.18 ± 0.13-fold at an equal ratio. Similar results were documented in cervical cancer cells and virus-negative head and neck cancer cells. Furthermore, selective short interfering RNA knockdown targeting viral oncoproteins in HeLa cells caused a marked drop in host kinase levels down to 0.67 ± 0.11 relative to control, accompanied by a robust 6.21 ± 1.20-fold rescue of the host tumor suppressor p53. In addition, an immortalized human keratinocyte line stably engineered to express the full-length type 18 genome exhibited pronounced elevations in both total and phosphorylated active kinase forms compared to parental controls, indicating that viral expression actively stimulates host kinase activity. To establish how the host kinase sustains elevated viral oncoprotein levels, the authors conducted cycloheximide chase assays measuring protein half-life and turnover kinetics over two hours. When human embryonic kidney cells expressed type 18 E6 alone, the viral protein decayed with a half-life of 54.24 minutes. Co-expression of the host kinase dramatically extended this survival, prolonging the viral protein half-life beyond 120 minutes. A parallel stabilization was noted for type 16 E6, whose half-life rose from 52.22 minutes to 120 minutes in the presence of the kinase. Notably, kinase activity profiling utilizing bioluminescent ADP-Glo kinase assays revealed that the host enzyme does not significantly phosphorylate the viral oncoprotein, demonstrating that the kinase does not utilize the viral protein as an enzymatic substrate. Instead, the experimental evidence indicates that physical non-covalent association outside the primary kinase domain shields the viral factor from degradation, sustaining steady-state oncoprotein levels through structural stabilization rather than direct biochemical phosphorylation. Having established the functional significance of the kinase-oncoprotein interaction, the investigators conducted a multistage virtual and biological screen to identify small molecules capable of disrupting the protein complex. By filtering a structural chemical library of one thousand diverse compounds collected from PubChem, DrugBank, ZINC, and ChemSpider using molecular docking algorithms, ten promising candidates were advanced to biological testing. Cell counting kit-8 viability assays identified the small molecule designated CP681301 as a highly selective inhibitor of virus-positive cancer cells. In comparative dosage assessments, the compound displayed a half-maximal inhibitory concentration of 2.0 micromolar against type 18-positive HeLa cells and 3.7 micromolar against type 16-positive CaSki cells. In stark contrast, virus-negative C33A cervical cancer cells exhibited resistance, with inhibitory concentration values exceeding 10 micromolar. Longitudinal tracking over four days of 1.5 micromolar compound exposure maintained durable suppression of proliferation in HeLa and CaSki cells while showing no detectable growth inhibition in virus-negative controls. Direct biophysical characterization using microscale thermophoresis validated that the compound engages the target proteins with distinct binding affinities. The equilibrium dissociation constant of CP681301 was measured at 36 micromolar for purified type 18 E6 and 112 micromolar for type 16 E6, both showing higher affinity than its binding to the host kinase itself, which registered at 127 micromolar. In competitive pull-down assays, incubating purified components with 1.5 micromolar of the inhibitor significantly attenuated binding between the host kinase and type 18 E6, reducing relative protein association by 0.4600 ± 0.09-fold. Analysis of concentration-dependent cellular responses yielded median effective concentrations of 0.45 micromolar for oncoprotein reduction and 1.14 micromolar for kinase reduction in cultured HeLa cells. Quantitative polymerase chain reaction further verified that high-dose inhibitor exposure suppressed kinase messenger RNA in both positive lines and lowered viral oncoprotein transcripts in type 18-positive cells, indicating that transcriptional repression accompanies the observed protein loss. Functional cellular assays demonstrated that disrupting the host-viral complex profoundly diminished hallmark malignant phenotypes in cell culture models. In wound healing scratch assays, exposure to 0.6 and 1.5 micromolar concentrations of the inhibitor significantly restricted cell migration over twenty-four hours in both HeLa and CaSki lines. Anchorage-independent growth in soft agar was similarly curtailed: vehicle-treated HeLa cells generated robust colonies, whereas cells exposed to 1.5 micromolar compound produced only 69.00 ± 27.03 colonies, reflecting a statistically significant loss of transformation capacity. Transwell chamber invasion assays through extracellular matrix Matrigel demonstrated comparable dose-dependent reductions; relative to vehicle controls, HeLa cell invasion dropped to 230.00 ± 66.73 at 0.6 micromolar and fell to 65.00 ± 41.82 at 1.5 micromolar. Identical suppressive effects occurred in type 16 cells, whereas virus-negative C33A cells experienced no significant reduction in migratory, colonizing, or invasive behaviors under identical treatment conditions. At the mechanistic level, the inhibitor dismantled the oncogenic degradation cascade that normally eliminates host tumor suppressors. Cycloheximide chase measurements in HeLa cells revealed that 0.6 micromolar inhibitor treatment accelerated oncoprotein decay, reducing its cellular half-life from 71.97 minutes in control conditions to just 21.96 minutes, representing a more than threefold destabilization. Western blotting confirmed that pharmacological treatment caused simultaneous, dose-dependent depletion of endogenous kinase, viral E6, and the ubiquitin ligase E6AP over twenty-four hours. Biochemical pull-down experiments utilizing purified proteins demonstrated that 1.5 micromolar of the compound physically disrupted complex formation between type 18 E6 and the E6AP enzyme. By destabilizing the viral oncoprotein and preventing assembly of the tripartite degradation machinery, treatment effectively rescued the p53 protein from proteasomal destruction, restoring endogenous levels of this critical tumor suppressor in virus-positive cervical cancer cells without modifying p53 or E6AP levels in virus-negative control cells. Despite these promising cellular outcomes, the authors outlined key technical and biological limitations that restrict the immediate clinical translation of their findings. All experimental observations were derived from established in vitro cell cultures, and the investigations relied primarily on C33A as the single comparative virus-negative cervical cancer line, which may not encompass the full genomic diversity of human malignancies. The research team also lacked stable genomic knockdown cell models for the kinase and viral oncoprotein in HeLa cells, preventing evaluation of the permanent consequences of chronic complex disruption. Furthermore, because CP681301 exhibited comparable baseline growth suppression against certain virus-negative head and neck cancer cells and reduced E6AP across varied cellular backgrounds, the molecule possesses inherent cytotoxic liabilities and potential off-target effects. The authors concluded that while the host-viral interaction represents a validated therapeutic vulnerability, future drug development must design optimized pharmacological agents with enhanced structural specificity to safely disrupt this target across human papillomavirus-driven malignancies. supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Saturday, November 28, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Vaginal Microbiome Imbalance Associates With Cervical Dysplasia and HPV in Togolese Women by November 26, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Vaginal Microbiome Imbalance Associates With Cervical Dysplasia and HPV in Togolese Women Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram In a community-based cervical cancer screening study conducted in Lomé, Togo, researchers identified significant associations linking vaginal microbial dysbiosis with high-risk human papillomavirus infection and cervical dysplasia among asymptomatic adult women. Evaluating a screening cohort of 338 women, investigators observed an overall high-risk human papillomavirus prevalence of 31.33 percent and detected cytological cervical epithelial abnormalities in 10.06 percent of participants. Women presenting with high-risk viral infections exhibited significantly elevated Nugent scores compared to uninfected participants, reflecting a marked phenotypic disturbance in baseline vaginal bacterial composition. A parallel elevation in Nugent scores was documented among individuals diagnosed with cervical dysplasia compared to those showing normal cytology. Rather than identifying a single infectious etiology, subsequent molecular analyses demonstrated that these clinical outcomes were characterized by a structural depletion of protective Lactobacillus species and a concurrent expansion of diverse polymicrobial anaerobic consortia, providing novel insights into mucosal cofactors within sub-Saharan Africa. Cervical cancer represents a severe public health crisis in sub-Saharan Africa, where limited screening infrastructure and constrained access to clinical interventions drive elevated morbidity and mortality rates. In Togo, cervical malignancy is the second most frequent cancer among female populations, responsible for an estimated age-standardized incidence of roughly 21.5 cases per 100,000 women and generating more than 400 annual deaths. While persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus genotypes is widely established as the primary causal driver of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia and invasive carcinoma, viral presence alone does not invariably lead to malignant progression. The vast majority of acquired viral infections are successfully cleared by host immune mechanisms within one to two years without causing persistent epithelial damage. Emerging scientific evidence has increasingly highlighted the cervicovaginal microenvironment, particularly mucosal microbial equilibrium, as an influential biological cofactor modulating viral persistence, local tissue inflammation, and early neoplastic transformation. However, mucosal microbiome research has historically remained skewed toward cohorts in industrialized nations, leaving microbial profiles among West African women largely uncharacterized prior to this community investigation. To investigate cervicovaginal microbial features associated with viral carriage and cervical abnormalities, investigators recruited sexually active, non-pregnant adult women aged 18 years or older through social media announcements and radio broadcasts in Lomé. Participants reported to the Association Togolaise pour le Bien-être Familial clinic for comprehensive cervical screening. Study eligibility required participants to be asymptomatic, in good general health, and without prior histories of cervical cancer, precancerous treatments, loop electrosurgical excision procedures, conization, or adnexectomy. To eliminate confounding biological exposures, the protocol excluded women who were actively menstruating, had engaged in sexual intercourse within the preceding three days, had received human papillomavirus vaccination, were currently receiving antibiotics or had taken them within three months, or presented known immune deficiencies. A total of 428 women completed structured face-to-face interviews documenting sociodemographic characteristics, reproductive histories, and lifestyle habits. Following these initial evaluations, 338 participants completed pelvic examinations, provided cervical samples for high-risk viral detection and Papanicolaou cytological assessment, and contributed vaginal swab specimens for standardized Nugent scoring. Clinical evaluations integrated cytological assessment, phenotypic bacterial vaginosis grading, and molecular viral genotyping to characterize each participant. Conventional cervical cytology smears were stained according to the Papanicolaou protocol using automated instrumentation and independently reviewed by three pathologists using the Bethesda 2014 classification system. Smears were categorized as negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy, atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance, atypical squamous cells that cannot exclude high-grade lesions, low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions, or high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions. Concurrently, vaginal smears were Gram-stained to calculate Nugent scores from 0 to 10 based on relative morphotype counts of large Gram-positive rods, small Gram-negative rods, and curved bacilli. Genomic DNA was extracted from swab specimens using column-based purification kits. High-risk viral genotyping was executed utilizing the Anyplex II HPV HR Detection assay on a Bio-Rad CFX96 real-time PCR platform. This multiplex real-time polymerase chain reaction assay simultaneously amplified the L1 region across 14 high-risk viral genotypes alongside human beta-globin control genes, applying melting curve analysis across defined cycle thresholds to determine semi-quantitative viral load levels. Genotyping across the 338 screened participants revealed a diverse landscape of oncogenic viral types, led predominantly by HPV16, which accounted for 35.33 percent of all detected high-risk infections. The second most prevalent genotype was HPV51 at 14.66 percent, followed by HPV35 at 9.33 percent, HPV52 at 8.90 percent, HPV56 at 8.66 percent, and HPV58 at 7.33 percent. Genotypes HPV18 and HPV59 each represented 6.66 percent of infections, while HPV31, HPV66, HPV45, and HPV39 accounted for 3.66 percent, 2.66 percent, 1.94 percent, and 1.33 percent, respectively. Cytological examinations demonstrated that 10.06 percent of the screened cohort harbored cervical squamous abnormalities, including low-grade intraepithelial lesions, atypical squamous cells, and high-grade intraepithelial lesions, alongside pervasive evidence of local tissue inflammation. Women presenting cervical dysplasia were significantly older on average than those with negative cytology, whereas parity, age at sexual debut, and lifetime partner counts showed no statistically significant differences between groups. Multivariable logistic regression confirmed that high-risk viral carriage, early sexual debut, and higher parity served as independent predictive variables associated with elevated Nugent-defined vaginal dysbiosis. For deep molecular characterization of the mucosal ecosystem, a subset of 150 satisfactory vaginal DNA specimens fulfilling rigorous cellularity and purity thresholds underwent high-throughput 16S ribosomal RNA gene sequencing. Amplicons spanning the hypervariable V3-V4 region were generated using universal 319F and 806R primers, purified with magnetic beads, indexed through dual-indexing adapters, and sequenced on an Illumina MiSeq platform utilizing paired-end 300-base-pair reads. Raw sequence data were processed through the DADA2 pipeline in the R software environment for quality filtering, read denoising, paired-end merging, and chimera removal, yielding 5,110 unique amplicon sequence variants across 148 fully analyzed samples at an average read depth of 23,810 reads per library. Taxonomic classification was executed using the Ribosomal Database Project classifier matched against SILVA reference databases, supplemented by high-resolution secondary BLASTn alignments against the NCBI RefSeq 16S ribosomal RNA database requiring at least 99 percent sequence identity and 98 percent query coverage to assign putative species-level classifications conservatively. Rarefaction analysis demonstrated complete sequencing saturation, with Rarefaction Saturation Index values reaching 99.99 percent across all clinical subgroups, confirming that observed community metrics were not biased by uneven sequencing depth. Alpha diversity evaluations evaluating Chao1 richness, Shannon diversity, and Simpson evenness demonstrated no statistically significant differences between high-risk viral-positive and viral-negative women, nor between dysplastic and normal cytology groups. Specifically, mean Shannon diversity remained virtually indistinguishable between viral-positive women and uninfected controls at 3.68 and 3.67, respectively. Global beta diversity evaluated through Principal Coordinate Analysis of Bray-Curtis dissimilarity matrices revealed that viral infection status did not induce significant community restructuring across global coordinate planes. Similarly, Permutational Multivariate Analysis of Variance indicated that cervical dysplasia displayed only a modest, non-significant divergence trend, while community ecological volatility assessments remained statistically comparable across groups. These findings demonstrated that viral carriage and early cytological lesions do not cause complete wholesale ecological collapses, but instead correspond to selective compositional substitutions within an otherwise globally intact vaginal ecosystem. Despite stable global community metrics, fine-scale differential abundance analyses using negative binomial generalized linear models in DESeq2 revealed profound compositional rearrangements. Healthy, lesion-negative women exhibited vaginal microbiomes dominated by Firmicutes and protective Lactobacillus species. In contrast, participants carrying high-risk human papillomavirus or presenting cervical dysplasia demonstrated an extensive depletion of lactobacilli accompanied by substantial enrichment of opportunistic and strict anaerobic bacteria. Enriched taxa included Atopobium vaginae, Fannyhessea vaginae, Sneathia sanguinegens, Peptostreptococcus anaerobius, Peptoniphilus faecalis, and multiple Prevotella species. Stratified validation analyses restricted strictly to confirmed low-grade and high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions while excluding indeterminate atypical cytological classifications confirmed that these anaerobic signatures remained significantly elevated, exhibiting log2 fold changes exceeding 2.5. Concurrently, protective Lactobacillus crispatus and Lactobacillus mulieris species remained significantly depleted in confirmed dysplasia cases. High-resolution heatmaps confirmed that dysplasia was linked to the coordinated expansion of polymicrobial anaerobic consortia rather than the isolated proliferation of an individual pathogen. Ecosystem classification into recognized human vaginal Community State Types demonstrated that CST IV, defined by high bacterial diversity and severe Lactobacillus depletion, represented the dominant ecological state across the studied population. CST IV was identified in 76.7 percent of healthy cytological controls and 81.5 percent of participants diagnosed with cervical dysplasia. CST III, characterized by an intermediate dominance of Lactobacillus iners, appeared in 15.0 percent of controls and 18.5 percent of dysplastic women, whereas classic Lactobacillus-dominated configurations designated as CST Other were found in only 8.3 percent of healthy controls and were completely absent among women with cervical dysplasia. Spearman correlation analysis indicated that quantitative human papillomavirus viral burden was not significantly correlated with the degree of community dysbiosis, yielding a correlation coefficient of -0.006. This absence of linear correlation suggests that viral replication intensity and mucosal bacterial disruption operate through partially decoupled pathways influenced by host immunity, mucosal barrier integrity, or preexisting anaerobic colonization rather than direct viral load kinetics. Functional pathway profiling inferred through the PICRUSt2 pipeline and MetaCyc database revealed that mucosal dysbiosis was accompanied by significant metabolic reprogramming toward anaerobic carbohydrate utilization and cellular stress responses. Dysplastic states and viral infection were characterized by significant enrichment in sucrose degradation II pathways alongside activation of chorismate biosynthesis II, heme biosynthesis, and lysine biosynthesis networks. These metabolic adaptations reflect bacterial mechanisms for sustaining cellular survival, promoting biofilm formation, and maintaining chronic local mucosal inflammation. The study authors emphasized that because their protocol employed a cross-sectional design, observed microbial shifts represent statistical associations rather than proven causal relationships. Furthermore, 16S rRNA gene sequencing provides predicted metagenomic capacity rather than direct enzymatic activity, and the down-selection of screened participants to 148 sequenced samples introduces potential selection limitations. Nonetheless, as the first West African community-based study combining blinded cytology, Nugent scoring, and next-generation sequencing, these findings establish critical baseline evidence supporting the development of microbiome-targeted screening and intervention strategies across high-burden settings. supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Saturday, November 28, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Cancer HPV Integration Testing Improves Diagnostic Accuracy in Cervical Cancer Triage by November 26, 2026 in Cancer Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 HPV Integration Testing Improves Diagnostic Accuracy in Cervical Cancer Triage Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A cross-sectional study within a major screening cohort demonstrates that detecting human papillomavirus chromosomal integration offers a highly accurate molecular biomarker for identifying severe precancerous cervical lesions in virus-positive women. Conducted across regional centers, the research evaluated whether identifying viral integration could resolve a critical dilemma in modern screening: distinguishing transient viral carriage from clinically dangerous pathology requiring colposcopy. In an analytical cohort of 949 women testing positive for high-risk human papillomavirus who underwent biopsy-confirmed histopathological assessment, viral integration testing demonstrated 95.3 percent accuracy and 97.0 percent specificity for identifying cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 or worse. These metrics substantially surpassed conventional liquid-based cytology, which registered 64.5 percent accuracy and 64.3 percent specificity. Crucially, the molecular assay detected high-grade disease without sacrificing clinical sensitivity, matching cytology at 66.7 percent versus 68.5 percent. These findings indicate that viral integration testing provides an objective molecular triage mechanism capable of refining clinical referrals and minimizing unnecessary invasive procedures. Cervical cancer represents a severe global health challenge, accounting for roughly 7 percent of female cancers with an estimated 660,000 incident diagnoses and over 340,000 deaths annually, with burdens concentrated disproportionately in low-resource settings. International guidelines recommend primary screening with high-risk human papillomavirus deoxyribonucleic acid testing because of its elevated diagnostic sensitivity. However, most viral infections are transient and naturally cleared by host immunity, creating a high volume of positive screening tests that complicate patient management. Current clinical algorithms rely heavily on liquid-based cytology, such as the ThinPrep cytology test, to triage virus-positive patients for colposcopy. Unfortunately, cytology demonstrates widely varying diagnostic performance, with reported sensitivity ranging from 55 percent to 94 percent and specificity between 63.8 percent and 75.5 percent. This morphological variability leads to frequent misclassification, unnecessary diagnostic biopsies, and overtreatment. Consequently, researchers have focused on viral genomic integration, a critical biological transition wherein viral deoxyribonucleic acid inserts into host chromosomes, disrupting genomic stability, elevating oncogene expression, and driving precancerous progression toward invasive carcinoma. To evaluate viral integration within routine clinical practice, researchers analyzed participants from the Fujian-Hubei Cervical Lesion Screening Cohort, which comprised 31,628 women presenting for screening. Between October 2021 and June 2024, investigators enrolled 1,326 women undergoing simultaneous primary screening and viral integration testing. Following the application of inclusion criteria, exactly 949 participants with valid integration results, definitive colposcopy-guided biopsies, and histopathological diagnoses formed the final analytic cohort. Ethical authorization was granted by the Institutional Review Board of Fujian Maternity and Child Health Hospital under approval identifier 2024KLR09009, with all participants providing written informed consent. Patients diagnosed with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 or worse were managed under American Society for Colposcopy and Cervical Pathology consensus guidelines. Histopathological diagnoses served as the reference standard, categorized into benign or inflammatory findings, grade 1 neoplasia, grade 2 neoplasia, and grade 3 or worse. By requiring biopsy confirmation across all 949 participants, the investigators ensured an objective benchmark for verifying diagnostic accuracy. The testing protocol utilized commercial polymerase chain reaction reverse dot blot genotyping alongside high-throughput viral integration detection, known as HIVID. Genotyping categorized 23 types in exfoliated cervical cells, encompassing 13 high-risk types, five possible high-risk types, and five low-risk types. For integration testing, genomic deoxyribonucleic acid was extracted and captured via a multiplex probe system targeting entire viral genomes, followed by sequencing on an Illumina platform. To guarantee assay reproducibility, standardized spike-in reference fragments were added to each specimen, demanding a recovery rate of at least 0.01 percent for analytical validity, while sequencing quality maintained a Q30 score of 90.0 percent or higher. An automated bioinformatics pipeline classified specimens as integration-positive when at least six unique virus-host chimeric reads were detected at a specific genomic site, eliminating observer bias. Independent evaluations by two blinded pathologists determined histological status, resolving discrepancies through third-expert adjudication. Exclusions were applied to participants lacking definitive histological diagnoses or showing genotype discrepancies between testing platforms. Across the 949 evaluated participants, viral integration was detected in 6.6 percent, representing 63 individuals. The median age was 38 years in integration-negative women and 37 years in integration-positive women, showing no statistically significant age difference. In contrast, viral genotype distribution differed substantially: HPV16 and HPV18 appeared in 63.5 percent of integration-positive individuals compared to 29.0 percent of integration-negative patients. Genotype analysis identified integration in 28.3 percent of HPV18 infections, 11.5 percent of HPV16 infections, 4.4 percent of HPV52 infections, and 1.4 percent of HPV58 infections, with no integration observed in HPV45, 66, 68, 73, or 82. Viral integration rates correlated with cytological severity, increasing from 5.1 percent in normal cytology to 7.2 percent in atypical or low-grade cytology, and reaching 21.6 percent in high-grade squamous lesions. Pathological examination revealed that 57.1 percent of integration-positive participants harbored confirmed grade 3 or worse intraepithelial neoplasia, compared to just 2.0 percent among integration-negative women, confirming an association with advanced lesion severity. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age demonstrated that viral integration had the strongest association with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 or worse, showing an adjusted odds ratio of 68.1 with a 95 percent confidence interval from 34.4 to 140.9. In contrast, non-HPV16/18 infections showed an adjusted odds ratio of 0.2, reflecting lower relative risk compared to HPV16/18. When evaluating infection patterns alongside integration, single infections with positive integration exhibited an adjusted odds ratio of 121.8, while multiple infections alone did not significantly alter risk relative to single infections. Sensitivity analyses confirmed the stability of these statistical models: bootstrap resampling with 10,000 iterations produced an adjusted odds ratio of 68.1 with a 95 percent bias-corrected confidence interval of 31.7 to 138.7, and Bayesian logistic regression yielded a posterior median odds ratio of 64.3 with a 95 percent credible interval of 32.7 to 130.4, mitigating concerns of model overfitting. Head-to-head diagnostic comparison revealed that viral integration testing significantly outperformed liquid-based cytology across multiple performance parameters for detecting grade 3 or worse lesions. Integration detection achieved a specificity of 97.0 percent compared to 64.3 percent for cytology, alongside an overall diagnostic accuracy of 95.3 percent versus 64.5 percent. The positive predictive value of integration testing reached 57.1 percent, more than five times higher than cytology at 10.4 percent. Diagnostic sensitivity remained comparable between the two modalities at 66.7 percent for integration testing and 68.5 percent for cytology. Subgroup analyses corroborated these findings: in HPV16/18-positive women, integration testing achieved a positive predictive value of 60.0 percent compared to 21.0 percent for cytology; in women older than 45 years, positive predictive value reached 38.9 percent versus 6.6 percent. Both approaches sustained high negative predictive values exceeding 97 percent, confirming low residual risk among test-negative patients. Evaluating combined diagnostic strategies showed that pairing viral integration testing with genotyping substantially improved diagnostic accuracy over existing clinical paradigms. Combining cytology with HPV16/18 genotyping yielded a sensitivity of 92.6 percent but exhibited a low specificity of 44.3 percent, an accuracy of 47.0 percent, and a positive predictive value of 9.1 percent. In contrast, combining viral integration detection with HPV16/18 genotyping significantly improved specificity to 69.5 percent and accuracy to 70.5 percent, while maintaining comparable sensitivity at 87.0 percent and raising the positive predictive value to 14.7 percent. Similarly, combining integration detection with cytology achieved 92.6 percent sensitivity and 64.0 percent accuracy, with 62.4 percent specificity. Across all combined modalities, negative predictive values remained high between 98.89 percent and 99.29 percent without statistically significant differences, demonstrating that incorporating integration detection sharpens risk assessment while maintaining high safety margins against missed high-grade lesions. Risk stratification demonstrated practical advantages for clinical decision-making. Women identified as integration-positive showed a 57.1 percent direct risk of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 or worse, markedly exceeding the 10.4 percent risk observed among women with abnormal cytology. Conversely, integration-negative individuals accounted for 93.4 percent of the cohort and exhibited a low disease risk of 2.0 percent. Notably, women with normal cytology and negative integration status represented 59.2 percent of the entire cohort, with a disease risk of only 0.7 percent. This expands upon the standard low-risk cohort defined by the American Society for Colposcopy and Cervical Pathology—women with normal cytology who test negative for HPV16/18—which represented 42.1 percent of participants with a 1.0 percent risk. By reliably identifying a broader subset of low-risk patients, molecular integration triage could allow clinical systems to safely reduce surveillance intensity for the majority while prioritizing colposcopy for high-risk integration-positive individuals. The authors noted important methodological strengths alongside notable clinical limitations. Strengths included multivariable adjustment for key confounders, validation through bootstrap and Bayesian frameworks, and consistent subgroup performance across age categories and viral genotypes. However, the study cross-sectional design cannot determine the temporal sequence between integration events and lesion development, while the absence of longitudinal data precludes causal inferences regarding disease progression. Furthermore, the overall integration positivity rate of 6.6 percent and low regional prevalence for genotypes such as HPV45 limited sample sizes for specific subgroups, preventing firm conclusions regarding rare genotypes. The financial cost of high-throughput integration testing also remains higher than routine genotyping, and this investigation did not perform a formal health-economic analysis. The researchers concluded that larger longitudinal studies are necessary to evaluate cost-effectiveness, establish standardized laboratory protocols, and validate integration testing as an objective triage tool in primary screening programs. supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Saturday, November 28, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Scaling HPV Screening Alongside Vaccination Could Eliminate Cervical Cancer in Zambia by November 26, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Scaling HPV Screening Alongside Vaccination Could Eliminate Cervical Cancer in Zambia Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A nationwide transmission modeling study has demonstrated that scaling up community-based human papillomavirus DNA screening alongside adolescent vaccination could reduce cervical cancer incidence in Zambia by 97 percent over the next four decades, placing the World Health Organization elimination threshold within practical reach by 2060. Conducted by researchers from Columbia University and the Zambia Ministry of Health, the investigation utilized an individual-based transmission model calibrated to national demographic records, local sexual partnership dynamics, and empirical epidemiological data. The primary findings establish that while routine vaccination of pre-adolescent girls serves as a vital cornerstone for long-term control, immunization alone produces minimal epidemiological impact during the initial twenty years of implementation because existing disease burdens reside almost exclusively among adult cohorts who remain unimmunized. By contrast, pairing school-based vaccination programs with an expansive molecular screening campaign capable of administering approximately 400,000 tests annually accelerates clinical gains dramatically, averting an estimated 34,000 cervical cancer cases by 2040 and more than 183,000 cumulative cases by 2060. Zambia currently confronts one of the highest cervical cancer burdens documented worldwide, characterized in 2020 by an estimated crude annual incidence of 34.1 cases per 100,000 women and an associated mortality rate of 20.5 per 100,000 women, corresponding to an observed case fatality ratio of roughly 60 percent. This public health crisis is intensified by exceptionally high baseline exposure to high-risk viral strains, with a 2022 national population survey indicating that approximately 30 percent of women aged 25 to 49 test positive for oncogenic human papillomavirus. The transmission dynamic is further compounded by the concurrent human immunodeficiency virus epidemic, where an estimated 14.2 percent of Zambian women aged 15 to 49 live with HIV. Zambia introduced visual inspection with acetic acid within HIV clinics in 2006 and initiated a national single-dose vaccination campaign for girls aged 9 to 14 in 2019, yet structural access barriers across rural territories have continually constrained diagnostic coverage. Under this collaborative framework designed by ICAP at Columbia University and the Zambia Ministry of Health, rural community health volunteers facilitate patient self-collection of vaginal specimens, which undergo rapid automated testing using portable battery-powered molecular equipment capable of delivering high-performance DNA results equivalent to provider-collected samples. Expanding this molecular see-and-treat protocol beyond HIV-dedicated settings to all women aged 25 to 49 establishes a practical programmatic mechanism to bypass facility deficits and extend effective secondary prevention across remote populations. To rigorously evaluate the population-level consequences of this expanded diagnostic delivery model, the investigators constructed an individual-based computational model that simulated transmission mechanics and disease natural history across 50,000 synthetic individuals initialized from Zambia’s 2019 age and sex distribution. Demographic projections incorporated empirical survival schedules, age-stratified birth rates, and historical census data compiled by the United States Census Bureau. The computational architecture simulated annual time steps wherein individuals entered the sexually active population upon reaching age 15. Annual partnership formation was governed by Poisson distributions reflecting age-specific mean partnership frequencies derived from sub-Saharan African behavioral datasets, with mixing constrained to opposite-sex partnerships within a five-year age difference to mirror documented national marital age gaps. The model accounted for changing human immunodeficiency virus background dynamics by holding adult HIV incidence fixed at 0.31 percent overall, reflecting calibrated 2021 national survey findings, while assigning risk ratios to represent accelerated infection and progression rates among immunocompromised women receiving modern antiretroviral therapy. The biological natural history within the model tracked individual infection longevity across discrete disease compartments: uninfected susceptibility, active oncogenic infection, aggregated precancerous cervical lesion, invasive cancer, and cause-specific mortality. Drawing on established biological trajectories, the authors specified that 85 percent of newly acquired infections clear spontaneously within four years without inducing permanent tissue dysplasia. For individuals experiencing persistent infection, transition probabilities governed progression into an aggregated lesion state, where lesions were required to persist for a mandatory dwell time of at least five years before becoming capable of advancing to invasive malignancy. Model calibration aligned parameters against observed empirical benchmarks, identifying a calibrated cumulative progression probability of 0.30 from persistent lesion to cancer, an annual infection-to-lesion transition rate of 0.012, a median progression interval from viral acquisition to invasive disease of 27 years, and a median age at cancer presentation of 46 years, matching observed clinical profiles in southern Africa. Using these calibrated baseline parameters, the research team projected Zambian disease trajectories through 2064 across five standardized counterfactual scenarios to contrast isolated interventions against integrated programmatic scale-up. The reference counterfactual, designated as No Interventions, modeled the complete withdrawal of national testing and vaccination activities after 2024, causing projected cervical cancer incidence to climb from 34 cases per 100,000 women in 2020 to 49 cases per 100,000 by 2060 as population aging expanded the demographic pool of mature adult women. The second scenario, Vaccination Only, sustained a constant 73 percent single-dose coverage rate among girls aged 9 to 14 with an assumed lifelong vaccine efficacy of 90 percent, but discontinued secondary screening. The third scenario preserved ongoing visual inspection with acetic acid starting at 154,280 annual tests and expanding by 5 percent annually while maintaining historical prioritization for women living with HIV. The fourth and fifth scenarios modeled universal molecular screening for all women aged 25 to 49, initiating testing volumes at 200,000 and 400,000 molecular tests per year respectively, both incorporating annual 5 percent expansion. Analysis of the simulation trajectories showed that relying exclusively on adolescent immunization leaves national cancer rates largely unaffected for multiple decades. Under the Vaccination Only pathway, cervical cancer incidence declined by an imperceptible 3.4 percent over the initial twenty years through 2040, because vaccinated adolescents required decades to age into the peak demographic windows of oncogenic vulnerability. Although isolated immunization eventually yielded a 29 percent reduction in annual cancer incidence by 2050 and a 47 percent reduction by 2060, it averted only 1,000 cumulative cancer cases during the first twenty years and 57,000 cumulative cases across the full forty-year horizon. Continuing traditional visual inspection with acetic acid produced intermediate outcomes, achieving a modest 14 percent incidence reduction by 2040 and a 61 percent reduction by 2060, while averting 80,000 cumulative malignancies over forty years. The visual approach was constrained by lower operator-dependent diagnostic sensitivity, documented between 22.8 percent and 48 percent in Zambian clinical evaluations, and structural reliance on clinical examination rooms. Universal population screening utilizing molecular DNA assays yielded dramatic, immediate reductions in disease incidence, fundamentally outperforming visual triage. Expanding molecular testing capacity to 200,000 tests annually achieved a 40 percent decline in cervical cancer incidence within twenty years and an 88 percent reduction after forty years, averting more than 143,000 cumulative cases by 2060. Increasing molecular throughput to 400,000 annual tests reduced national incidence by 64 percent by 2040 and 97 percent by 2060, bringing crude incidence down to approximately 2 cases per 100,000 women. Furthermore, the 400,000 annual test scenario satisfied the global target of maintaining 70 percent of adult women up to date with screening guidelines by 2032, averting 34,000 incident malignancies by 2040, 94,000 by 2050, and 183,000 cumulative cases by 2060, while preventing over 18,000 premature deaths. In secondary exploratory analyses simulating eighty-year transmission dynamics across varying vaccination coverage levels without concurrent screening, the researchers examined the indirect herd protection conferred by extending human papillomavirus vaccination to school-aged boys. At low to intermediate coverage levels, adding boys to national immunization registers produced substantial secondary protection for women. Specifically, achieving 37 percent coverage among both sexes prevented more than 120,000 additional cervical cancer cases over eighty years compared to immunizing 37 percent of eligible females alone, demonstrating how male immunization suppresses circulating viral transmission throughout shared sexual networks. However, the marginal epidemiological benefit of male vaccination diminished sharply as female immunization rates reached higher thresholds; under a hypothetical 91 percent female coverage scenario, expanding coverage to boys yielded only 4,387 additional averted cases across eighty years. These findings indicate that while universal sex-neutral immunization offers an effective mechanism to bolster herd immunity when female uptake is constrained by social hesitancy or delivery logistics, prioritizing universal coverage among girls remains the most efficient allocation of constrained resources. The authors highlighted several critical methodological assumptions and real-world operational challenges that contextualize their projections. The mathematical architecture utilized an aggregated lesion compartment rather than differentiating specific histological grades of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia, and partnership formation relied on annual stochastic resampling rather than dynamic long-term partnership tracking. Moreover, while baseline projections incorporated an optimistic 73 percent female vaccination coverage rate, actual Zambian adolescent uptake dropped from 99 percent in 2019 to 44 percent in 2021 before recovering to an estimated 52 percent by 2025. supplementary_news.content: New research reveals that among women with persistent human papillomavirus (HPV) infection, increasing and persistently high viral-load trends may be an indicator of the presence of cervical cancer. The analysis is published by Wiley online in CANCER, a peer-reviewed journal of the American Cancer Society. Although persistent HPV infection is central to the development of cervical cancer, studies have not examined how viral-load trajectories over time are associated with this outcome. In this new study, when researchers led by investigators at the Changzhou Maternal and Child Health Care Hospital of the Changzhou Medical Center at Nanjing Medical University, in China, prospectively followed 624 women with persistent HPV infection, they identified 4 distinct viral-load trajectories. Women with moderate increasing or persistently high trajectories had a markedly greater likelihood of developing signs of cervical cancer than those with low stable or moderate declining trajectories. Cervical precancerous lesions occurred in 10.9%, 17.8%, 74.2%, and 90.4% of women in the low stable, moderate declining, moderate increasing, and persistently high trajectory groups, respectively. The risks of cervical precancerous lesions relative to the low stable group were 1.95, 29.66, and 124.29 times higher for the other respective groups. Considering these trends in viral load improved the ability of clinicians to predict a woman's likelihood of developing cervical cancer beyond baseline clinical characteristics and baseline viral load. Two women with similar HPV viral loads at one visit may have very different outcomes depending on how those levels change over time. Our findings suggest that a rising or persistently high viral load may signal a greater likelihood of cervical lesions." Lina Zhang, MD, co–corresponding author Co–corresponding author Zhonghua Shi, MD, added that a major challenge in managing persistent HPV infection is identifying women who need closer surveillance while avoiding unnecessary examinations. "We hope these findings will contribute to more personalized follow-up strategies and ultimately improve cervical disease prevention," he said. Zhou, Y., et al. (2026). supplementary_news.content: 下载客户端 登录 无障碍 +1 4 打HPV疫苗前,这些“副作用”你一定要知道 腾讯医典她知 关注 2026-11-25 10:55 上海 来源:澎湃新闻·澎湃号·湃客 听全文 字号 2025年11月,我国已经把HPV(人乳头瘤病毒)疫苗纳入免疫规划,适龄女生可以免费接种两剂。 但疫苗热度一高,关于“副作用”的传言也跟着来了。 比如,打完HPV疫苗后会“月经不调、闭经、卵巢早衰?”“发烧、恶心、呕吐、头晕头痛”等,甚至会“瘫痪”“死亡”? 不少家长和学生被网上各种传言劝退,或打完第一针后,由于害怕而不敢再去打第二针。 (来源:网络) 不过,一个“反应”或“疾病”是不是疫苗副作用,是不是和打疫苗有关,需要科学判断,也要看整体数据,而不是“我自己”“我身边”“我听说”这样的个例。 关于HPV疫苗的不良反应和应对办法,建议每个准备去打疫苗的女性都了解一下。 先说一个前提:打任何一种疫苗,都有“副作用”,在医学上称为“不良反应”。 其实吃药也是,只是大家往往更关注药品的作用,而忽略了副反应。 但对于疫苗,由于大多是身体健康的人去打的,所以很多人会更关注副反应。 打完HPV疫苗后,可能出现一些“不良事件”,比如[1]: 局部的:接种部位的红疹、肿胀、疼痛、瘙痒、硬结、出血等。 全身的:常见发热、头痛、乏力、恶心、呕吐等;偶见过敏性皮炎、皮疹、眩晕等。 严重不良事件:如血栓、癫痫、格林巴利综合征、死亡等[2]。 自 2006 年获批以来,全球已接种HPV疫苗超过 8 亿剂[3]。 美国疾控中心(CDC)、世界卫生组织(WHO)、欧洲药品管理局(EMA)以及我国卫生部门都在长期密切监测疫苗的副反应。 WHO 疫苗安全全球资讯委员会明确表示:没有证据表明 HPV 疫苗与上面这些“不良事件”有关,更多是时间上的巧合[3]。 美国疾控中心也表示,没有证据表明 HPV 疫苗会导致生育问题[4]。 事实上,上面这些“反应”并不常见。 以说明书为例,按发生频率从高到低[1]: 十分常见(≥10%):头痛、疼痛、肿胀、红斑等; 常见(1%-10%,含1%):发热、恶心、头晕、疲劳、腹泻、瘙痒、淤青等; 偶见(0.1%-1%,含0.1%):淋巴结病、眩晕、腹痛、呕吐、晕厥、硬结、寒战、痛经、荨麻疹、过敏等; 而且是否出现、程度如何,因人而异:有人第一针没事,第二、三针也可能出现。 疼痛 最常见,是肌肉注射的正常反应,一般轻微,也可忍受。 若出现注射部位以外的疼痛(如肢体痛、关节痛、偏头痛等),及时向接种单位反馈并寻求医疗建议。 晕厥 接种后晕厥概率约 0.2%[1],可能跌倒受伤,所以建议打完疫苗后留观 30 分钟。 WHO 研究认为,晕厥多与焦虑紧张有关[3],接种时别太紧张。 过敏反应 有过敏史者接种前要告知医务人员,必要时延长留观事件。 若出现全身荨麻疹、血管性水肿、呼吸困难等严重过敏反应,应及时就医处理[5],并由医生评估能否再次接种同类疫苗。 发烧 不超过 38.5°C 无需特别处理;超过可服退热药、多喝水;高热不退要尽快就医。 恶心、呕吐 可单独出现,也可伴发热、头晕、寒战等流感样症状,适当休息、清淡饮食即可。 月经失调 没有证据表明月经失调、闭经与疫苗有直接关系。 若接种后出现,按一般情况做妇科检查即可。 总之,接种 HPV 疫苗后的不良反应大多轻至中度,短期内可自行缓解。 相比接种HPV带来的巨大收益,完全没有必要因为害怕副反应而拒绝接种。 建议适龄女性和男性及时接种,守护自己和爱人的健康。 审稿专家 邓晟 | 中南大学湘雅医院药学部主任药师 参考文献 [1]Product Information: GARDASIL(R) 9 intramuscular injection, human papillomavirus 9-valent vaccine, recombinant intramuscular injection. Merck Sharp &Dohme Corp. (per FDA), Whitehouse Station, NJ, 2015. [2]HPV vaccine safety,www.nhs.uk [3]https://ncirs.org.au/20-years-hpv-vaccination-celebrating-progress-and-recognising-ongoing-challenges [4]Preventing and Managing Adverse Reactions,www.cdc.gov [5]Administering HPV Vaccine.www.cdc.gov 内容制作 *腾讯医典内容团队出品 原标题:《打HPV疫苗前,这些“副作用”你一定要知道!》 阅读原文 特别声明 本文为澎湃号作者或机构在澎湃新闻上传并发布,仅代表该作者或机构观点,不代表澎湃新闻的观点或立场,澎湃新闻仅提供信息发布平台。申请澎湃号请用电脑访问http://renzheng.thepaper.cn。 +1 4 收藏 我要举报 评论(0) 发表 加载中 1央行发布人民币存贷款利率管理新规:取消贷款罚息利率的上下限 2合力稳市!“国家队”护盘过程中各类机构均为净买入,股票型ETF十月以来净申购近8000亿 3受贿5.87亿余元,广西自治区政府原主席蓝天立一审被判死缓 4雅迪、台铃、爱玛、小牛等15家电动自行车企业被集中约谈 5四川德阳一体校回应“教练当学生面连摔多部手机”:可能处理问题比较简单粗暴 6日产汽车在华销量大减,计划首次将与中国合资生产汽车“反向进口”至日本销售 7初中生刺伤霸凌者羁押336天后被判正当防卫,检察院已张贴公告道歉 8暖侬心|72岁老人跳下3米深河救起6岁幼童:这份善良不声张,也不算账 9经济日报刊文:“399元羽绒服卖断货”是消费降级吗? 10产业观察丨制造基地迈向产业高地:南昌针纺产业集群的破局攀登 展开更多 封面|三线齐发 央行发布人民币存贷款利率管理新规 上交所调整多项指数样本 查看更多 专访|荷兰国立博物馆总馆长:我所理解的伦勃朗与维米尔 杨苗燕|先生教我的事——记忆中的吴宏聪先生 查看更多 特朗普:老有人说中国刺探美国情报,说不定美国刺探得更狠 加盟德甲富尔达,方博回应:不为赚钱,想提升对抗性打WTT 更多澎湃快讯 开始答题 澎湃早晚报|早餐湃·三线齐发 言短意长|政府部门发布《情况通报》也标原创,有这必要吗? 美股三大指数全线收涨:存储概念爆发,中概股普遍上扬 查看更多 扫码下载澎湃新闻客户端 Android版 iPhone版 iPad版 关于澎湃 加入澎湃 联系我们 广告合作 法律声明 隐私政策 澎湃矩阵 澎湃新闻微博 澎湃新闻公众号 澎湃新闻抖音号 派生万物开放平台 IP SHANGHAI SIXTH TONE 新闻报料 报料热线: 021-962866 报料邮箱: news@thepaper.cn 沪ICP备14003370号 沪公网安备31010602008124号 互联网新闻信息服务许可证:31120170006 增值电信业务经营许可证:沪B2-2017116 © 2014-2026 上海东方报业有限公司 反馈

supplementary_news.content: Aller au contenu principal Chercher Produits Communauté Marchés Courtiers Plus FR Black FridayJusqu'à 80% en MOINS Actualités /绿叶制药(02186.HK):拟用于治疗宫颈癌前病变和HPV相关肿瘤的mRNA疫苗LY01620即将开展中国II期临床试验 绿叶制药(02186.HK):拟用于治疗宫颈癌前病变和HPV相关肿瘤的mRNA疫苗LY01620即将开展中国II期临床试验 2186+7,19% 格隆汇8月20日丨绿叶制药2186宣布,集团自主研发的信使核糖核酸(「mRNA」)疫苗LY01620即将在中国开展II期临床试验。该研究拟纳入经组织学确诊的人乳头瘤病毒16(「HPV16」)阳性子宫颈高级别鳞状上皮内病变(「HSIL」)患者,以进一步评估LY01620的有效性和安全性。 LY01620是一种治疗性mRNA疫苗,注册类别为治疗用生物制品1类,其作用靶点为HPV16亚型E6和E7蛋白抗原。LY01620利用mRNA表达HPV特异性抗原E6/E7,通过诱导机体产生特异性T细胞免疫清除HPV感染的宫颈上皮细胞,阻断癌变过程并使宫颈上皮细胞恢复正常。 LY01620在中国的I期临床研究已取得积极结果并支持II期研究的开展。I期研究旨在评价LY01620在HPV16阳性经组织学证实为HSIL患者中的安全性、耐受性、免疫应答、免疫原性和初步有效性。研究结果显示,LY01620可明显激活细胞免疫和体液免疫,HPV病毒清除率近90%,组织病理学改善的比例接近标准手术治疗水平,且本品无创,不影响生育功能。本品总体安全耐受性良好,发生的不良反应均为疫苗常见不良反应。 与传统的手术治疗相比,治疗性疫苗可应用于HPV感染後的不同病程阶段,阻断向宫颈癌进展。集团管理层相信,作为一种高效非手术的免疫治疗方案,开发治疗性HPV疫苗已成为临床的急切需求。LY01620有望填补HPV治疗性疫苗的空白,为HPV相关疾病提供新的治疗选择。此外,集团亦积极探索LY01620在HPV相关实体肿瘤中的临床应用前景,进一步挖潜产品的治疗价值和潜力。 集团自主mRNA技术平台已打通抗原筛选、mRNA序列优化、专有递送载体系统开发及GMP规模化生产的全流程技术闭环,依托该技术平台,集团具有持续开发基于肿瘤新抗原的个性化和通用型mRNA疫苗产品的能力。 Actions hong-kongaisesGelonghui Plus d'articles de Gelonghui Afficher plus Afficher plus Afficher plus Afficher plus Afficher plus Afficher plus Afficher plus Afficher plus Afficher plus Afficher plus Afficher plus Afficher plus Afficher plus Afficher plus Afficher plus Afficher plus Afficher plus Afficher plus

supplementary_news.content: 首页 要闻 北京 科技 AI 看热点 更多 正在浏览:关注 | 事关HPV疫苗,权威解答! 天津经济广播 搜索 趣玩 游戏 网页设置 Skills服务NEW 登录 安装电脑版 内容更精彩 广告 关注 0 评论 收藏 分享 复制链接 微信好友 微信高于4.0.2版本可点击分享 低版本建议使用手机扫码分享 QQ好友 QQ高于9.9.17版本可点击分享 低版本建议使用手机扫码分享 腾讯元宝 手机看 微信扫一扫,随时随地看 元宝 · 新闻妹 关注 | 事关HPV疫苗,权威解答! 天津经济广播 2026-11-22 16:45发布于天津 关注 问AI · 初中女生接种HPV疫苗抗体为何高? 近年来,随着HPV疫苗在我国全面普及,这款能够有效预防宫颈癌等疾病的疫苗,受到社会各界的广泛关注。 在大众普遍认可的同时,网络上也滋生出各类不实传言,引发不少家长疑虑,甚至干扰了科学接种决策。 事实上,从疫苗制备原理、大规模临床试验数据,到全球近二十年上市后的监测结果,均充分证实HPV疫苗安全可靠。 针对家长普遍关心的热点问题,市疾控局联合市疾控中心作出权威解答。 疑问一: 网上说HPV疫苗是“绝育疫苗”,千万不能打? 一是疫苗成分安全,不含活病毒和激素。HPV疫苗是重组蛋白疫苗,里面没有活病毒,也不会改变人体DNA,更不含激素成分,所以不会干扰内分泌。其有效成分只是病毒外壳的一小段蛋白,没有病毒的遗传物质,不会感染人体。 二是不会损伤卵巢、不影响月经和生长发育。疫苗成分不会跑到卵巢里去损伤卵泡,全球范围内的监测数据都没有发现HPV疫苗与卵巢早衰之间存在因果关系,也不会影响月经周期或孩子的生长发育。所谓“绝育”“影响生育”的说法毫无科学依据。 三是全球长期验证,疫苗反应一般轻微。HPV疫苗已上市使用多年,全球已有163个国家纳入免疫规划,安全性和有效性已经得到充分验证。接种后个别孩子可能会出现发热、头痛、疲劳、接种部位疼痛等反应,属于正常的一般反应,一般2—3天就会自然缓解,家长不必过度担忧。 疑问二: 孩子才上初中,这么小就要打HPV疫苗吗? 一是13岁正是接种的黄金年龄。按照国家将HPV疫苗纳入免疫规划的部署,为2011年11月10日后出生、年满13周岁的适龄女孩免费接种。9—14岁是世界公认的接种黄金年龄,此时接种产生的抗体水平更高、保护更持久。多数国家和地区为低年龄组儿童提供免费接种,英国为8年级(12-13岁)儿童免费接种,香港地区、澳门地区为小学五年级、六年级学生免费接种。 二是早接种抗体水平更高、“起跑储备”更足。我国临床研究显示,9-17岁女性接种二价、四价HPV疫苗后免疫应答较强,血清学抗体滴度是18—26岁女性的1.42-3.00倍。也就是说,青春期的孩子“起跑储备”约为成年女性的2倍,将来即使缓慢消耗,“家底”也更丰厚。丹麦一项关于86万名女性的全国性队列研究结果显示,与未接种疫苗者相比,在小于16岁时接种HPV疫苗,宫颈癌发病率降低了86%;在17-19岁时接种,宫颈癌发病率降低了68%。 三是无需担心抗体会“过期”、不必反复加强。接种后可产生保护性抗体和记忆效应,整体保护效果良好、不需要加强接种,最长的持久性保护效力已超过10年。多国研究显示,9-15岁女孩接种后随访10年,89%-96%的人疫苗相关抗体仍为阳性,对相关感染和疾病的保护效力达到100%。芬兰对16-17岁女性随访了12年,二价疫苗接种者HPV16/18型抗体阳性率仍超过90%。接种疫苗后,血液里的抗体水平确实会随时间缓慢下降,这是所有疫苗的共同规律。但判断疫苗有没有“失效”,不能只看血里的抗体数值,还要看身体里的免疫记忆细胞是否记住了敌人。打个通俗的比方,新房子的防盗系统装好后,不需要24小时轰鸣报警,只要主机还记着入侵者的“脸谱”,一旦小偷翻窗,系统会在第一时间精准报警、快速出击。 疑问三: 听说HPV疫苗是强制接种,非打不可吗? 一是接种免疫规划疫苗既是权利,也是法定义务。《中华人民共和国疫苗管理法》第六条明确,居住在中国境内的居民依法享有接种免疫规划疫苗的权利,也应当履行接种义务,监护人须依法保证适龄儿童按时接种。符合条件的适龄女孩可免费、就近接种,这是国家提供的一份健康保障,也是公民应尽的责任和义务。 二是全程坚持知情告知、健康评估、规范接种。学校通过告知书、家长会、主题班会等方式如实告知接种事项,家长接种前如实告知孩子的身体状况、疾病史、过敏史和用药情况,由接种医生进行健康评估后接种,绝非“不明不白硬打”。 疑问四: 天上不会掉馅饼,免费接种是不是存在利益输送? 一是免费接种是国家提供的健康保障,不是商业行为。人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)疫苗已纳入国家免疫规划,由政府免费向居民提供,符合条件的适龄女孩可以免费、就近接种,无需承担任何疫苗费用,免费的目的是提高疫苗可及性,保护孩子健康、推进宫颈癌防控。 二是更高价次疫苗属自愿自费惠民选择,不存在强迫牟利。适龄女孩可免费接种国产二价HPV疫苗,全程共2针、间隔6个月,足以满足基本防护需求;家长也可根据需要,自愿自费、惠民减免选择接种九价等高价次疫苗,选择权在家长,具体可咨询辖区接种单位。 疑问五: 我怎么知道疫苗安全不安全、效果行不行? 一是国家实行最严格的全程监管,疫苗质量有保障、有监管、有罚则。《中华人民共和国疫苗管理法》第三条确立对疫苗实行最严格的管理制度。疫苗上市前须完成动物实验和多期人体临床试验;上市后每批出厂须经批签发机构逐批检验合格方可放行;储存运输全程冷链监控;接种后建立疑似预防接种异常反应监测与补偿制度,免费疫苗和自费疫苗在安全标准上没有区别。目前全国适龄儿童HPV疫苗接种率已接近70%,整体异常反应发生率极低、疫苗安全稳定。 二是疫苗上有安全有效期,效期内接种的都有效。疫苗外包装上的有效期,是厂家保证在此日期前,疫苗的活性、免疫原性、安全性都符合标准的最后期限。在规范冷链储存前提下,未超过包装标注有效期时,疫苗里面HPV病毒样颗粒(VLP蛋白)免疫原性稳定,保护效力不会下降。因此,在疫苗标注的有效期之内,哪怕临近到期,疫苗的保护效力、安全性都不会下降,可以正常接种,不影响免疫效果。 疑问六: 学校一直催促接种,还要去医院开具不能打的证明? 一是反复通知是为督促补种、防范健康风险。按照《中华人民共和国疫苗管理法》第四十八条,儿童入托、入学时学校应当查验预防接种证、核查免疫规划疫苗完成情况;发现未按规定接种的,向接种单位报告并配合督促监护人补种。第九十二条,监护人未依法保证适龄儿童按时接种免疫规划疫苗的,由县级人民政府卫生健康主管部门批评教育、责令改正。学校、接种单位反复提醒,是履行查验、上报、督促补种的法定职责。不接种意味着孩子缺少对HPV16/18型病毒(导致超过70%的宫颈癌)的防护,请家长理解配合,尽早带孩子完成接种。 二是只要没有禁忌,就应当接种。只要没有绝对禁忌等特殊情况,免疫规划HPV疫苗应当依法接种;仅有对疫苗成分或辅料严重过敏、既往接种后出现超敏反应等特殊情况不能接种,并需由接种医生评估后确定,普通感冒、轻微湿疹、鼻炎、过敏体质、经期等大多不属于接种禁忌。接种前接种医生会开展健康评估,并非要开具“免打证明”。 提醒广大家长 在此真诚提醒广大家长:HPV疫苗是预防宫颈癌最经济、最有效的手段,早接种、早保护,切勿因轻信谣言、犹豫观望而错过最佳防护时机。 如有疑问,请通过学校咨询电话、辖区接种单位咨询电话等官方渠道咨询,不轻信、不传播未经证实的网络信息。 -END- 来源 | 天津疾控、天津中老年时报、天津新闻广播 编辑 | 高晶 免责声明:本内容来自腾讯平台创作者,不代表腾讯新闻或腾讯网的观点和立场。 举报 WorkBuddy把重复劳动交给AI干 广告WorkBuddy 了解详情 相关推荐 天冷了,提醒糖友们注意:1不碰,2不洗,3要吃! 吕军医生7评论昨天 这3个部位开始痛,可能是尿毒症早期信号,别再以为是小事 部分试看心理咨询师阿秋11-23 人不会无缘无故得糖尿病,医生提醒:得糖尿病的人,通常有这4个根源! 部分试看心理咨询师阿秋11-20 秒秒爆装一秒五刀,高爆率传奇爽快不停! 广告王者 了解详情 医生:希望你的肾功能报告里,永远不要出现这2点描述 部分试看心理咨询师阿秋11-07 人为什么会得高尿酸?原来尿酸是这样产生的,早知道早预防! 部分试看心理咨询师阿秋11-07 幽门螺杆菌一家人都查吗?治完会不会再感染,说清 部分试看荚博士说肿瘤10-29 这两个方法,对糖尿病患者保护眼睛非常有好处,建议大家用起来 糖尿病之友昨天 存钱不如存“肌肉”——警惕肌少症偷走您的晚年健康 达医晓护1评论4小时前 WorkBuddy AI办公助手,免部署安装即用 广告WorkBuddy 了解详情 每周一练 | 很多老年人悄悄在家练这个,不光腿脚稳,脑子还快了 云梦县广播电视台昨天 老年常见收缩期高压,降压药怎么选,不容易踩坑?
